articles.title: Applied Materials Bets $5B on a New Model for Chip Innovation - EE Times
articles.text:
Applied Materials CEO Gary Dickerson sees semiconductor innovation becoming a race in which speed matters as much as technological capability. Artificial intelligence is driving demand for faster transistors, higher-bandwidth memory, and more efficient connections between chips. Delivering those improvements requires advances across multiple manufacturing processes, often several generations before the resulting devices enter production.
Applied Materials bets $5 billion that bringing more of the industry’s R&D activities together will help it win that race.
On Oct. 12, the company officially opened its Equipment and Process Innovation and Commercialization (EPIC) Center in Silicon Valley. The facility is designed to bring Applied Materials’ engineers together with researchers and engineers from chipmakers, universities, and other equipment suppliers to develop future semiconductor technologies.
The investment represents more than an expansion of Applied Materials’ R&D infrastructure. It reflects a shift in the company’s relationship with the semiconductor industry, from supplying equipment for processes developed with customers toward participating earlier in decisions about the materials, architectures, and manufacturing methods that will define future chips.
“We’re working four generations ahead of time,” Dickerson told EE Times in an interview before the opening. “Whoever brings those innovations to market fastest is going to win.”
Rethinking the R&D model
The need for a different approach stems partly from a growing mismatch between the pace of semiconductor product development and the time required to introduce new manufacturing technologies. AI processors are increasingly developed on annual cycles, while new semiconductor materials have historically taken eight to 12 years to move from research into production.
Stephen Sopko, semiconductor and deep-tech practice lead at HyperFRAME Research, recently authored a white paper on semiconductor R&D commissioned by Applied Materials. He sees a growing mismatch between the rapid development cycles of AI processors and the much longer time needed to bring new semiconductor materials and manufacturing processes into production.
“I think the clock mismatch is the thing that’s bringing it to attention right now,” Sopko told EE Times. He argued that the problem is not simply the difficulty of discovering new materials. It’s the way semiconductor R&D is organized.
Research frequently begins in universities or government laboratories, moves to equipment suppliers for process development, and eventually reaches chipmakers for integration into manufacturing. Each organization has different objectives, budgets, and measures of success.
Those transfers can create delays, particularly when researchers develop materials or processes that later prove impractical to manufacture at scale.
“The biggest thing that needs to be addressed is the way that work is organized,” Sopko said. “The integration bottleneck is not so much the physics piece. It’s the industrialization piece that’s the bottleneck.”
Dickerson described EPIC as an extension of changes Applied Materials began making years ago. The company established teams specializing in process integration, recognizing that improvements to individual pieces of equipment were no longer sufficient to deliver the performance gains customers needed. “When you’re innovating in a transistor, for instance, with faster and lower-power transistors, you’re integrating across that entire flow,” he said.
EPIC is intended to bring those capabilities together with customers’ engineers much earlier in the development process. Dickerson said leading chipmakers will have engineers working full time at the facility, collaborating directly with Applied Materials’ specialists in materials, deposition, process integration, and analysis.
The objective is to shorten the interval between identifying a promising technology, integrating it into a complete manufacturing flow, and achieving acceptable production yields. Dickerson described this as improving the velocity from concept to commercialization.
Applied Materials already operates development laboratories near customers’ manufacturing facilities, where engineers optimize existing processes and prepare upcoming technology generations for production.
Customer-adjacent laboratories are effective at solving immediate manufacturing problems, Sopko said, but their focus on current and near-term requirements can leave less room for technologies three or four generations ahead.
EPIC is designed to complement those facilities, allowing longer-term ideas to be tested against manufacturing requirements before customers commit to particular architectures.
From materials to systems
The growing interdependence of semiconductor technologies makes early collaboration particularly important. Dickerson pointed to the combination of logic, memory, and advanced packaging required by AI computing. Improving transistor performance alone is insufficient if data cannot move efficiently between processors and memory.
“How you connect all of these computing components, how you connect the chips together, is more important than ever,” he said.
Dickerson cited hybrid bonding, high-bandwidth memory, backside power delivery, and vertically stacked transistor architectures as areas where manufacturing processes must evolve together.
The partnerships surrounding EPIC reflect that broader scope. Intel recently joined TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron as a founding partner. With Intel’s addition, the world’s five leading chipmakers are now participating in the initiative, according to Dickerson.
Broadcom has also joined the EPIC platform, bringing the perspective of a company designing custom AI silicon and networking chips rather than operating leading-edge fabrication plants. Other participants include equipment suppliers and research universities.
Broadcom’s participation is particularly significant, Sopko argued, because chip designers need to understand manufacturing possibilities years before their products reach production. “They want to know what the limits of design are,” he said.
That broadens EPIC’s potential role beyond equipment and process development toward earlier coordination between system requirements and semiconductor manufacturing capabilities.
But bringing competing chipmakers into a shared research facility also creates challenges. TSMC, Samsung, and Intel compete in foundry services, while Micron, Samsung, and SK Hynix compete in memory. All have strong incentives to protect their technology roadmaps.
Dickerson said Applied Materials addresses those concerns by separating customer innovation teams and maintaining strict controls over physical access and information. “We segment,” he said. “We firewall our innovation teams.”
Within EPIC, partner areas are separated, and Applied Materials controls who can enter particular locations. Dickerson said the company can track individuals’ locations within centimeters and has established rules governing access to data.
These arrangements are intended to allow multiple companies to work with Applied Materials without exposing confidential development programs to competitors. Trust is fundamental to the model because customers must share sensitive information about future technologies before they can collaborate effectively.
But this new R&D model raises a broader question: How much of the semiconductor industry’s future technology development will become concentrated around major equipment suppliers capable of funding facilities on this scale?
A strategic investment for Applied Materials
For Applied Materials, the commercial benefits extend beyond helping customers accelerate their development programs. The $5 billion commitment covers construction of the facility and installation of equipment, with additional annual investment expected as operations expand.
Dickerson expects EPIC to improve Applied Materials’ R&D productivity while helping its technologies become incorporated into future manufacturing processes earlier. Being involved when customers define new architectures can give an equipment supplier an advantage over competitors entering the process later.
Sopko sees that as one of EPIC’s most important business implications. “I think Applied doing this moves them earlier in the decision cycle,” he said. Early participation gives the company a clearer view of customers’ future requirements and may improve its chances of winning equipment and service business when those technologies enter production.
The advantage is not guaranteed. Chipmakers can still qualify competing equipment and pursue alternative manufacturing approaches. But participating before process architectures are finalized could make Applied Materials’ technologies more deeply embedded in customers’ manufacturing plans.
Dickerson readily acknowledged the commercial objective. “EPIC is just an accelerator of our design wins,” he said.
For Sopko, one of the most important measures of success will be whether EPIC can identify technologies that cannot be manufactured economically, allowing companies to abandon them before investing years in development. Recognizing an unworkable technology is only half the challenge. The organizations involved must also be willing to redirect their investments before the project advances too far.
That may prove harder than simply accelerating successful research programs, particularly when multiple partners have committed resources and reputations to a particular technology.
EPIC’s long-term value will therefore depend not only on how quickly promising materials and processes reach production, but also on whether the new collaboration model helps the industry make better decisions about which technologies deserve to get there.

articles.title: Des pirates ont fait chauffer les frigos de supermarchés Leclerc, Super U et Intermarché à 50 °C en pleine nuit
articles.text:
Une cyberattaque a visé cette nuit les systèmes frigorifiques Danfoss de nombreux supermarchés français. Chez Intermarché, Leclerc et Super U, des rayons surgelés entiers ont été vidés, et la facture pourrait se chiffrer en millions d'euros.
L'attaque informatique qui frappe les supermarchés Intermarché, Leclerc et Super U est grave, en plus d'être relativement inédite, puisqu'elle ne s'en prend ni aux caisses ni aux fichiers clients, mais aux frigos. D'après les informations de BFMTV, des pirates auraient déclenché à distance un dégivrage forcé sur des installations équipées de régulateurs Danfoss, avec une température réglée sur 50 °C, en pleine nuit. Au réveil, certains magasins ont découvert des stocks à jeter et une ardoise qui donne le vertige.
Cyberattaque inédite chez Intermarché, Leclerc et Super U, les congélateurs se sont mis à chauffer
Dans un supermarché, les frigos et les congélateurs dépendant d'un système de régulation, une sorte de thermostat central connecté, qui pilote leur température. Il programme aussi le dégivrage, une opération de routine qui réchauffe brièvement les équipements pour faire fondre le givre qui s’y forme, par exemple deux heures sur 24. Mais dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi, les pirates auraient détourné cette fonction pour la déclencher en continu, avec une consigne réglée à 50 °C.
Pendant des heures, les meubles froids auraient donc chauffé au lieu de refroidir. Selon une source du secteur, une bouffée d’air chaud s’est échappée à l’ouverture des frigos et des congélateurs. Lundi, un rayon de glaces affichait par exemple 26 °C en température. Autant dire qu'ici, tout doit passer à la poubelle.
D’après nos confrères, les hackers ont ciblé des versions anciennes du logiciel de régulation Danfoss, celles antérieures à la version 4. Or le groupe danois, l’un des grands noms mondiaux du froid commercial, équipe un très grand nombre de magasins en France, ce qui pourrait expliquer qu’autant d’enseignes aient été touchées la même nuit. Ces boîtiers n’en sont d’ailleurs pas à leur première alerte. Des chercheurs en cybersécurité, notamment chez Claroty, y avaient déjà repéré des failles, des portes d’entrée mal verrouillées. Danfoss les a depuis refermées grâce à une mise à jour, encore faut-il que les magasins l’aient installée. Rien ne permet toutefois d’affirmer, à ce stade, que ce sont ces failles-là qui ont servi cette nuit.
Les enseignes dénoncent une attaque inédite
Intermarché figure parmi les enseignes les plus touchées, avec quelque 150 magasins potentiellement concernés. Des Metro et des commerces indépendants, comme des boucheries, pourraient aussi faire partie des victimes. Tout dépend de l'heure de l'attaque, car là où elle aurait commencé vers minuit, tous les produits concernés auraient été détruits, alors que des magasins touchés plus tard auraient pu en sauver une partie. À Haguenau, en Alsace, l'Intermarché aurait perdu tous ses surgelés, soit 50 000 euros de marchandise. Le Leclerc de la même ville aurait dû jeter aussi ses produits frais, pour une perte estimée à 220 000 euros. À l'échelle nationale, la note pourrait atteindre plusieurs millions d'euros.
Chez les distributeurs, forcément, c'est la grogne. Sur X, le patron de Coopérative U juge inédite et inacceptable une attaque contre des équipements essentiels à la conservation des produits frais et à l'approvisionnement alimentaire. En interne, Système U admet que dans les pires cas, tous les produits frais ont dû être jetés. Intermarché, dans une note à ses magasins, confirme bien une attaque survenue chez Danfoss et promet de traiter en priorité leurs commandes exceptionnelles. Des cellules de crise ont été mises en place, et une réunion a lieu en ce moment même entre Danfoss, Axima et d'autres spécialistes du froid. Rien n'a filtré, pour le moment, sur l'identité ou les motivations des pirates.

articles.title: ATK Introduces the Blazing Sky Phantom, a 44g Carbon-Fiber Wireless Gaming Mouse With Dual 8K Polling
articles.text:
Monday, October 12th 2026
ATK Introduces the Blazing Sky Phantom, a 44g Carbon-Fiber Wireless Gaming Mouse With Dual 8K Polling
ATK GEAR has expanded its Blazing Sky mouse lineup with the new ATK Blazing Sky Phantom Hollow Carbon Fiber Composite Wireless Gaming Mouse, a lightweight esports-focused model built around a composite carbon-fiber shell, an open cutout structure, and ATK's latest in-house wireless performance platform. The Phantom is aimed at competitive FPS players who want a small-to-medium symmetrical shape, low click latency, and a high-end sensor package without moving into an oversized chassis.
The Phantom is available through ATK's official store.At first glance, the Phantom stands out from ATK's more conventional shells. The mouse uses a hollow carbon-fiber composite construction with staggered geometric cutouts across the body. Instead of making the weight-saving structure look purely functional, ATK has paired the cutouts with a distressed retro sunburst side print, giving the mouse a layered visual identity that looks closer to a custom enthusiast peripheral than a standard esports mouse. Four color options are listed: Prime, Dune, Verge, and Eon.
The headline number is weight. ATK lists the Blazing Sky Phantom at 44±3 g, placing it firmly in the ultralight category while retaining wireless connectivity and an internal 300 mAh battery. The dimensions are 119.7 mm × 62.5 mm × 37.3 mm, which positions it as a compact-to-mid-size option. The shape is symmetrical and relatively low-profile, with a tapered waist, centered ridge, and thumb support designed for controlled repositioning during fast aim adjustments. ATK recommends the Phantom for small-to-medium hands, with support for claw, palm, and fingertip grip styles.
Inside, the Phantom uses the PAW3955 Master sensor, a flagship-grade optical sensor configured for very fine sensitivity control. ATK lists support for up to 50,000 DPI, with 1-2 DPI step adjustment depending on configuration, and an adjustable lift-off distance range from 0.7 mm to 1.7 mm. For competitive players who tune their setup around consistent tracking and repeatable flicks, that level of granularity gives the Phantom a strong technical foundation.
The mouse is also built around ATK's self-developed ApexShark MAX Mouse Solution, using the NORDIC 54LM20 MCU and third-generation competitive firmware. According to ATK, the platform supports a static scan rate of over 20,000 FPS and enables dual 8000 Hz polling in both wired and 2.4 GHz wireless modes. The Phantom ships with support for ATK's 8K receiver ecosystem, including the GEM 8K Dongle / NANO 8K Dongle depending on configuration.
Click performance is another major selling point. The Phantom uses Omron optical switches and is rated for click latency as low as 0.174 ms. Optical switches also avoid traditional mechanical debounce behavior, helping deliver more consistent actuation over time. Combined with 8K polling, the Phantom is clearly being positioned for players who care about input responsiveness as much as raw weight.
Battery life is rated at up to 200 hours at 1000 Hz, powered by a 300 mAh high-density battery. As usual with high-polling-rate wireless mice, real-world endurance at 4000 Hz or 8000 Hz will be lower, but the 1000 Hz figure gives users flexibility when switching between competitive sessions and everyday desktop use. Connectivity includes both wired and 2.4 GHz wireless operation.
The Phantom also features ATK's all-new nano coating, a Raesha optical scroll wheel encoder, and the brand's broader software ecosystem through ATK HUB, which is designed to manage device settings, profiles, and performance tuning. ATK has increasingly positioned its peripherals as part of a connected esports hardware/software stack rather than standalone devices, and the Phantom continues that direction.
From a market perspective, the Blazing Sky Phantom enters a crowded but fast-moving category: ultra-lightweight wireless gaming mice for FPS players. Its differentiators are the carbon-fiber composite shell, distinctive hollow design, PAW3955 Master sensor, dual 8K polling, and very low quoted click latency. For players already using compact symmetrical shapes, the Phantom's 44 g target weight and small-to-medium hand tuning may be the biggest draw.
ATK GEAR says its product development is shaped by its background in gaming media, esports feedback, and hardware R&D. The company has built visibility through products such as the ATK68 magnetic keyboard, ATK F1 mouse, EDGE 60HE, and RS6 keyboards, while continuing to test and refine products with competitive teams. articles.title: Dónde ver Las Guerreras K-Pop en español latino de forma legal y segura
articles.text:
Las Guerreras K-Pop en español latino se puede ver de forma legal y segura a través de Netflix, la plataforma que distribuye la película de animación conocida internacionalmente como KPop Demon Hunters. La producción permanece disponible en el catálogo del servicio, aunque las opciones de idioma pueden variar según el país, el dispositivo y la configuración de cada cuenta.
La búsqueda de la película aumentó tras su expansión como fenómeno de entretenimiento digital. Sus canciones, personajes y secuencias de baile circularon en redes sociales, mientras el grupo ficticio HUNTR/X trascendió la historia principal para convertirse en un punto de referencia entre seguidores del K-pop, la animación y las producciones originales de streaming.
Netflix es la plataforma oficial para ver la película
Quienes busquen Las Guerreras K-Pop en español latino deben ingresar a la aplicación o al sitio web de Netflix, iniciar sesión y escribir el título en el buscador. En algunos mercados puede aparecer bajo su nombre internacional, KPop Demon Hunters, por lo que conviene probar ambas opciones.
La película sigue a Rumi, Mira y Zoey, tres artistas que integran un grupo musical de K-pop y que, fuera del escenario, enfrentan amenazas sobrenaturales. La producción fue realizada junto con Sony Pictures Animation y dirigida por Maggie Kang y Chris Appelhans.
Netflix ofrece versiones con distintos idiomas de audio y subtítulos. Para comprobar si está disponible el doblaje latino, es necesario abrir la ficha de la película y revisar el apartado de audio y subtítulos antes de iniciar la reproducción. La disponibilidad lingüística depende de las licencias de cada territorio y de los ajustes del perfil.
La plataforma también cuenta con una versión para cantar las canciones de la película, que incorpora las letras en pantalla. Esa edición amplía la experiencia para quienes siguen los temas de HUNTR/X y de los Saja Boys.
El fenómeno creció entre la música, la animación y las redes sociales
El interés alrededor de KPop Demon Hunters no quedó limitado al estreno. Netflix la presenta como su película más vista y mantiene una sección especial con información sobre el reparto, las canciones y el universo de la historia.
La banda sonora impulsó gran parte de esa conversación. “Golden”, interpretada por HUNTR/X, llevó la película a las listas musicales y reforzó un modelo que une largometrajes animados, música original, videos, coreografías y contenidos compartidos por los usuarios.
En redes sociales, las escenas musicales alimentaron desafíos de baile, videos de reacción, ilustraciones y montajes de fans. Esa circulación convirtió a los personajes en figuras reconocibles más allá de la plataforma. Para quienes llegan tarde a la tendencia, la película combina referencias a la industria del K-pop con una trama de fantasía, acción y comedia.
Cómo revisar el audio en español latino
El procedimiento cambia poco entre televisores, teléfonos, tabletas y computadoras. Una vez que comience la reproducción, estos son los pasos habituales:
- Pulse o seleccione el ícono de audio y subtítulos.
- Busque la opción “Español latino” o una denominación similar.
- Elija el idioma de audio deseado.
- Active los subtítulos si lo considera necesario.
- Regrese a la película para continuar la reproducción.
Si esa alternativa no aparece, puede deberse a que la cuenta está configurada para otro idioma, que el dispositivo tiene una versión desactualizada de la aplicación o que el catálogo local ofrece una selección distinta de pistas de audio. Netflix recomienda mantener la aplicación actualizada y verificar las preferencias del perfil.
Ver la película en la televisión desde el móvil
La forma más estable de ver Las Guerreras K-Pop en una pantalla grande consiste en usar la aplicación de Netflix instalada directamente en un Smart TV, una consola, un reproductor multimedia o un dispositivo compatible.
En equipos que admitan transmisión desde el teléfono, el móvil y el televisor deben estar conectados a la misma red WiFi. Después, abra Netflix en el celular, seleccione la película y toque el ícono de transmisión si aparece disponible. Elija el dispositivo de destino y controle la reproducción desde el teléfono.
También es posible acceder desde el navegador del televisor o conectar una computadora mediante un cable compatible. Antes de elegir una alternativa, conviene verificar que el equipo cuente con soporte oficial para Netflix.
Las páginas que prometen ver estrenos sin suscripción suelen incluir publicidad invasiva, enlaces falsos, solicitudes de datos personales o archivos que pueden instalar programas maliciosos. La Organización Internacional de Policía Criminal (INTERPOL) advierte que la piratería digital puede exponer a los usuarios a malware, virus, fraudes y robo de información.
La opción oficial evita esas descargas y permite acceder a la película con calidad de imagen, controles parentales, soporte técnico y actualizaciones de seguridad. Para confirmar la disponibilidad de audio en cada país, la referencia debe ser siempre la ficha de Netflix.

articles.title: ‘We know how much the fans like it’: Nintendo says it has ‘no plans’ to ditch physical games, as fans beg Sony to change course
articles.text:
‘I hope Sony takes notice’: Nintendo says it has ‘no plans’ to ditch physical media as GTA 6 goes entirely disc-less
Nintendo is taking a different approach
- Nintendo has confirmed its commitment to physical games
- The statement comes as Sony abandons physical media
- “We go off of what the consumer prefers,” Nintendo declared
Physical game releases are becoming increasingly rare these days, but one company that still plans to sell its titles this way is Nintendo. The Japanese gaming giant confirmed as much in an interview that might come as some relief to fans of disc-based media — although don’t take it as a guarantee that things will stay this way forever.
Speaking to Brazilian interviewer Rodrigo Coelho, Bill van Zyll, Vice President & General Manager of Nintendo Latin America, explained that, “There are no plans to ditch physical [media]. We know how much the fans like it as well.”
Nintendo’s van Zyll gave the example of the Nintendo Switch 2, for which games are available in both digital and physical formats. That's something Nintendo appears to be committed to continuing, at least for the time being, which could help to assuage the concerns of some fans.
Nintendo fans on social media seemed hopeful about the revelation. “Maybe there is window for cartridges to make a comeback in some capacity,” mused one on Reddit, while another proclaimed that “I have no plans to abandon Nintendo. The system works!” “I hope Sony takes notice,” wrote a third, referring to Sony’s decision to completely abandon physical games by 2028.
Good news — for now
Of course, there’s no way to know exactly how long Nintendo will remain devoted to physical games for. As van Zyll said in the interview, “historically, we’ve been very agnostic. We go off of what the consumer prefers and take that into account very heavily”. While that might mean physical releases are here to stay at the moment, van Zyll’s response doesn’t rule out a change of approach in the future if consumer tastes shift.
With that in mind, it’s worth considering that Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick has previously noted that “Our business is well over 90% digitally distributed,” which explains why GTA 6 is going to be an entirely disc-less launch. While Graft Theft Auto players and fans of Nintendo games are two quite different groups, I wouldn’t be too surprised to see Nintendo follow Take Two’s example in the future.
If you are a keen collector of physical games, and prefer to own hard copies of every title you play, Nintendo’s announcement will be great news. But with the industry increasingly heading in the digital direction, you might want to pick up hard copies of your favorites, just in case Nintendo decides to change course.

articles.title: Nouvelle Apple TV 4K : Apple aurait prévu deux nouveautés très pratiques
articles.text:
Ce mardi 13 octobre, Apple dévoilera plusieurs nouveaux produits domotiques. Nous devrions ainsi enfin découvrir l’Apple TV 4K de nouvelle génération, près de quatre ans après la sortie du dernier modèle, en 2022. Si nous disposions jusqu’à maintenant de peu d’informations à son sujet, le toujours très bien informé Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, est venu apporter deux nouveautés majeures concernant la nouvelle Apple TV 4K. En effet, le boîtier de cette dernière devrait intégrer un microphone, tandis que la télécommande présenterait un haut-parleur. Mais pourquoi faire ?
Deux nouveautés pour l’Apple TV 4K de nouvelle génération
Selon les informations de Mark Gurman, le boîtier de l’Apple TV 4K devrait intégrer un microphone, ce qui permettrait de contrôler l’appareil via Siri AI, sans devoir parler à travers la télécommande ou dans le HomePod. Le boîtier de l’Apple TV 4K se transformerait ainsi en véritable petit hub domotique, l’utilisateur pouvant contrôler le thermostat ou fermer les portes à travers celui-ci. Rappelons tout de même que Siri AI est toujours bloquée en Europe.
De son côté, la télécommande intégrerait un haut-parleur. L’intérêt ici est simple : un son est émis à travers la télécommande pour permettre à l’utilisateur de la retrouver facilement. Cela devrait permettre d’éviter de rechercher la télécommande pendant quinze minutes alors qu’elle était sous un oreiller. Il ne s’agit donc pas d’une révolution, mais d’une petite nouveauté qui devrait éviter de perdre du temps.
Pour rappel, la nouvelle Apple TV 4K devrait être équipée d’une puce A19.
Apple dévoilera plusieurs nouveaux produits ce 13 octobre
L’entreprise à la pomme dévoilera ce mardi 13 octobre l’Apple TV 4K de nouvelle génération, une nouvelle version de l’HomePod mini et un hub domotique équipé d’un écran qui porte finalement un autre nom que HomePad.
Toujours selon Gurman, l’Apple TV 4K de nouvelle génération et le nouveau HomePod mini devraient être commercialisés le 30 octobre prochain. La commercialisation du HomePod équipé d’un écran devrait quant à elle survenir un peu plus tard, soit en novembre.

articles.title: Planbare Nachrichten: Whatsapp testet neue, praktische Funktion
articles.text:
Jetzt schreiben, später versenden: Whatsapp arbeitet an praktischer Planungsfunktion für Nachrichten
Whatsapp hat eine neue Funktion entwickelt, mit der Nutzer:innen ihre Nachrichten planen können. Wie WABetainfo berichtet, ist diese mit dem Beta-Update 2.26.40.7 jetzt im Googles Play-Store für Android-Geräte verfügbar. Mithilfe der neuen Funktion können Nutzer:innen eine Nachricht verfassen und festlegen, zu welchem Zeitpunkt sie verschickt werden soll.
So funktioniert das neue Planungsfeature
Whatsapp ist der beliebteste Messenger der Deutschen. Fast neun von zehn der über 16-Jährigen nutzt die App laut einer Analyse von Meltwater und We Are Social mindestens einmal im Monat. Die neue Funktion ermöglicht es Nutzer:innen, eine Nachricht über die Chat-Oberfläche zu planen. Nachdem sie einen Text eingegeben haben, muss die Schaltfläche zum Versenden gedrückt und gehalten werden. Ist die Funktion verfügbar, erscheint ein Fenster, in dem sich der Versand zeitlich festlegen lässt. Anschließend wird die Nachricht durch Whatsapp automatisch zum gewählten Zeitpunkt versendet – auch wenn die App geschlossen ist.
Derzeit unterstützt die Nachrichtenplanung laut WABetainfo Text, Links, Fotos und Videos. Wer in einer Unterhaltung die Galerieauswahl öffnet, kann nach der Auswahl eines Bildes ebenfalls die „Senden”-Schaltfläche antippen und gedrückt halten. Die Funktion unterstützt laut Bericht allerdings nur jeweils ein Element. Das bedeutet, dass Nutzer:innen nicht mehrere Fotos oder Videos in derselben Nachricht einplanen können. Die Funktion ist auch mit dem Bearbeitungsmodus kompatibel. Dort können Nutzer:innen das Foto bearbeiten oder eine Bildunterschrift hinzufügen, bevor sie den Versandzeitpunkt festlegen. Nachrichten, die eingeplant werden, sind ebenfalls End-to-End-verschlüsselt.
Wichtige Einschränkung für Gruppen
Laut WABetainfo muss der Versandzeitpunkt mindestens zehn Minuten in der Zukunft liegen. So können Nutzer:innen in letzter Minute noch Änderungen vornehmen. Der maximale Planungszeitraum beläuft sich auf zwei Wochen im Voraus, um beispielsweise Geburtstagsgrüße frühzeitig vorzubereiten. Sobald eine Nachricht geplant ist, wird sie in einem eigenen Bereich in Whatsapp angezeigt. Dort können Nutzer:innen ihre geplanten Nachrichten einsehen, verwalten oder löschen.
Die Planung von Nachrichten soll auch mit Gruppen-Chats funktionieren. Dabei ist laut WABetainfo allerdings zu beachten, dass eine geplante Nachricht nur an die Mitglieder versendet wird, die zum Zeitpunkt der Planung Teil der Gruppe waren. Wer der Gruppe erst danach beitritt, erhält die Nachricht nicht. Da Whatsapp die Funktion schrittweise einführt, ist sie noch nicht für alle Nutzer:innen verfügbar. Aktuell können nur Testpersonen darauf zugreifen, die Android nutzen.
Neue Funktion für Gruppen-Admins
Der Funktionsumfang von Whatsapp wird ständig erweitert, um die Nutzung noch praktischer und vielfältiger zu gestalten. Im August führte die App beispielsweise eine neue Funktion ein, die sich gezielt an Gruppen-Admins richtet. Diese können jetzt eine optionale Begrüßungsnachricht einrichten, die automatisch an neue Mitglieder gesendet wird. Die Option ist standardmäßig deaktiviert, sodass bestehende Gruppen neue Mitglieder nur dann begrüßen, wenn ein Admin die Funktion manuell aktiviert hat.

articles.title: GlobalFoundries unveils 7nm-class FDX Fusion node — FD-SOI node doubles 22FDX transistor density, comes 7 years after firm abandoned FinFET
articles.text:
GlobalFoundries unveils 7nm-class FDX Fusion node — FD-SOI node doubles 22FDX transistor density, comes 7 years after firm abandoned FinFET
FDX Fusion to address emerging devices that need high integration, cost efficiency, low power consumption, and decent compute performance.
When GlobalFoundries abandoned development of leading-edge nodes in 2018, it also canceled the development of its 7nm-class FinFET fabrication technology that it co-developed with IBM. Almost exactly eight years later, GlobalFoundries is back with a 7nm-class manufacturing process, only this time the node relies on planar transistors and fully-depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI). It is aimed at automotive, edge AI, industrial, robotics, sensors, and other devices that prioritize low power consumption, high integration, and cost efficiency over maximum performance.
"We are delighted that GlobalFoundries has announced its next-generation 'single-digit FD-SOI; node, building on technology that CEA-Leti has been advancing for decades," said Sébastien Dauvé, chief executive of CEA Leti. "Through the FAMES pilot line, CEA-Leti continues to shape the future European roadmap for FD-SOI and works every day to promote its adoption in a wide range of applications."
FDX Fusion enters the scene
The new fabrication technology from GlobalFoundries is called FDX Fusion, and it promises 7nm-class 'digital performance' (an ambiguous claim; we will try to interpret it later) and more than twice the transistor density of its original 22FDX process introduced circa 2015. To achieve its target goals, the first generation of FDX Fusion will combine innovations in SOI substrates, transistor structures, and back-end interconnects, though keep in mind that GF has not disclosed transistor dimensions, contacted gate pitch, minimum metal pitch, or actual transistor density. GF plans to launch production of chips on FDX Fusion at its Dresden, Germany, facility in 2028, which will mark its return to the development of substantially more advanced FD-SOI fabrication processes after years of efforts to enhance its existing 22nm-class platform.
In addition to improved 'digital performance,' FDX Fusion will support RF transistors with fT/fmax of up to 0.5 THz, analog and mixed-signal circuitry, embedded nonvolatile memory, and in-memory computing capabilities. The combination is intended to enable highly integrated chips that can process information from sensors, execute AI inference workloads, control external devices, and communicate wirelessly without the need for numerous separate ICs. GF also intends to provide processor IP based on MIPS, ARC, and RISC-V architectures to accelerate the development of such products.
That being said, the main selling point of FDX Fusion is not necessarily its 7nm-class 'digital performance' and high-performance processor IP, but rather its ability to combine relatively powerful digital logic with RF, analog and mixed-signal circuitry, embedded nonvolatile memory, and in-memory computing capabilities on a single chip. This combination — which is why GloFo calls the process technology FDX Fusion — could enable highly integrated SoCs that would otherwise require multiple chips manufactured on different process technologies, which means additional tapeout costs as well as power consumption.
GlobalFoundries said it plans to deliver initial demo silicon for customer evaluation in early 2027, followed by the first process design kit (PDK) in mid-2027. The company is already collaborating with several customers on the technology, although it has not identified specific products or committed production volumes. Specifically, GF mentioned in its press release that BMW, Bosch, Infineon, NXP, Siemens, and Tesla have expressed interest in FDX Fusion, though only Infineon specifically confirmed collaboration on future 7nm-class technologies for radar and wireless communications.
Significant development
The GlobalFoundries announcement represents a significant development for GF's FD-SOI roadmap. The company introduced 22FDX in 2015 and announced its 12FDX successor in 2016, which promised performance comparable to 10nm FinFET, full-node density improvements, and up to 50% lower power consumption. Initial 12FDX customer tape-outs were expected in 2019, but the technology has never been adopted for commercial products. Instead, GF focused on enhancements to 22FDX and eventually the introduction of 22FDX+ (around the time when Samsung unveiled its 18FDS+), with additional capabilities for RF, embedded memory, and low-power applications. Interestingly, 12FDX was still a part of GF's investor roadmap in 2022.
FDX Fusion could therefore represent the realization of GF's original ambitions to scale FD-SOI beyond 22nm-class, although the company has not explained whether the new technology incorporates developments from its earlier 12FDX program. Meanwhile, CEA-Leti, which has conducted research into advanced FD-SOI technologies for years, describes FDX Fusion as a single-digit FD-SOI node. Nonetheless, GF's claim of 7nm-class 'digital performance' does not necessarily imply comparable transistor dimensions or integration density.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
From an industry perspective, FDX Fusion could provide an alternative to advanced FinFET and perhaps even gate-all-around processes for applications that require reasonably powerful digital logic alongside RF, analog, and embedded memory. Such integration could reduce system complexity and power consumption, particularly in edge AI devices where energy efficiency and real-time responsiveness are critical.
Perhaps more importantly, the technology could give European semiconductor developers access to a more advanced locally manufactured process without dependence on leading-edge foundries in Asia or the U.S.
Questions remain
However, the commercial success of FDX Fusion will depend on its actual performance, density, production costs, and the availability of a competitive design ecosystem, the latter arguably being the hardest part given the lack of any comments from leading electronic design automation (EDA) and IP developers.
When GlobalFoundries claims 2X 'digital performance' comparable to that of 7nm-class technologies, it doesn't reveal whether it means transistor switching speed, standard cell performance, achievable operating frequency, or something else. In addition, the company promises more than twice the logic density of its first-generation FDX technology, although the firm does not reveal any actual numbers. Consequently, it is unclear how FDX Fusion will compare with established 7nm-class FinFET technologies, which offer mature defect density and yields, plenty of supply, an established design ecosystem, and predictable pricing among other things, in terms of transistor density, performance, power consumption, and production costs. While CEA-Leti's comment seems promising, actual numbers are always better.
The very fact that GF's FDX Fusion planned 2028 introduction will come roughly nine years after the originally anticipated first 12FDX tape-outs illustrates significant technological and/or financial difficulties associated with the development of FD-SOI beyond the 22nm generation. So, while GlobalFoundries' FDX Fusion initiative certainly looks promising, it remains to be seen how that is going to play out for the contract chipmaker and its clients.
For now, the lineup of supporters from the automotive and industrial sectors — BMW, Bosch, Infineon, NXP, Siemens, and Tesla — certainly looks promising. But what about other applications? While established semiconductor companies such as Infineon and NXP already possess extensive processor IP portfolios, smaller fabless developers could benefit from GF’s MIPS and ARC processor cores, RISC-V expertise, and custom chip design capabilities, which could substantially reduce the cost and complexity of developing specialized SoCs. Still, to attract a broader range of chip developers, GlobalFoundries will need a mature ecosystem of EDA tools, standard-cell libraries, memory compilers, interface IP, and other silicon-proven building blocks. These are the things that GlobalFoundries has not touched upon in its press release.

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: Mark Zuckerberg ordenó lanzar el asistente de IA de Meta pese a fallas de seguridad
articles.text:
Mark Zuckerberg, CEO de Meta, ordenó lanzar el asistente de inteligencia artificial Muse pese a fallas de seguridad detectadas en las pruebas internas, informó el diario The New York Times. El sistema llegó a cambiar la contraseña de un usuario sin autorización antes del estreno público, el 8 de septiembre.
Los agentes de inteligencia artificial son asistentes capaces de completar tareas por cuenta propia, como hacer compras, administrar contraseñas o enviar mensajes, sin que el usuario dé cada indicación paso a paso.
La decisión se tomó en una reunión con Alexandr Wang, director de inteligencia artificial de la compañía, y Nat Friedman, responsable de producto de IA, según tres personas con conocimiento del encuentro citadas por el Times. Zuckerberg temía perder terreno frente a Instinct, una startup de apenas catorce empleados cuyo asistente empezaba a ganar popularidad.
Wang y Friedman conocían las fallas detectadas en pruebas recientes, entre ellas el caso en el que Muse cambió la contraseña de un usuario sin su consentimiento, de acuerdo con dos de las fuentes consultadas por el diario. Aun así, Meta presentó Muse en público el 8 de septiembre, tal como había ordenado Zuckerberg.
Así es la carrera de los asistentes personales de IA
Meta invirtió miles de millones de dólares en su división de inteligencia artificial, pero vio durante años cómo rivales como OpenAI y Anthropic se le adelantaban con chatbots y herramientas de programación. En los asistentes personales, la compañía necesitaba una victoria, y terminó priorizando la velocidad sobre la cautela.
Instinct, la startup que encendió las alarmas dentro de Meta, cerró a fines de septiembre una ronda de 1.000 millones de dólares que la valuó en 10.000 millones de dólares, cuatro veces más que un mes antes. Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital y Coatue participaron de esa ronda.
La apuesta le dio a Meta una ventaja temprana en una categoría que se transformó en el nuevo frente de la industria de la inteligencia artificial. Otras empresas ya presentaron productos para competir: tres semanas después de Muse, OpenAI lanzó su propio asistente, llamado Dots.
Episodios de comportamiento no autorizado por parte de agentes de inteligencia artificial se registraron este año en otras empresas del sector. Semanas antes, Anthropic había reconocido que uno de sus sistemas envió una denuncia falsa de homicidio a la policía de Filadelfia, y OpenAI admitió que uno de sus modelos vulneró la plataforma Hugging Face durante un ejercicio interno.
“Lo más interesante de Muse es que a Meta le tocó llegar primero”, dijo Avi Greengart, analista de la consultora Techsponential.
Cuáles fueron las fallas después del lanzamiento
Desde su estreno, Muse tuvo algunos tropiezos de seguridad adicionales. En un caso, el asistente entregó la dirección de un usuario a un vendedor de Facebook Marketplace sin su permiso, según el mismo reporte.
Un vocero de Meta rechazó la versión de que Zuckerberg haya apurado el lanzamiento por la presión de Instinct. “Estamos orgullosos de este trabajo y, como dijimos públicamente, incluso retrasamos el envío de Muse durante varios meses para asegurarnos de hacerlo bien”, afirmó en un comunicado.
La compañía no detalló cuántos incidentes de seguridad registró Muse en total ni qué cambios aplicó a sus controles internos después del estreno.
Cómo le ha ido a Muse en descargas
Pese a los incidentes, la apuesta de Zuckerberg rindió frutos. Hasta el miércoles pasado, Muse acumulaba más de 6,6 millones de descargas y 1,8 millones de usuarios activos por día, según datos de la firma de medición de aplicaciones Sensor Tower.
Para sostener el impulso, Meta lanzó una campaña publicitaria multimillonaria que llevó a Jolly, la mascota de peluche de Muse, a carteles y comerciales de televisión en varias ciudades de Estados Unidos.
“No se puede detener a Muse”, escribió Wang en una publicación en redes sociales el mes pasado, en medio del impulso comercial del asistente.
La diferencia de escala entre ambas compañías sigue siendo amplia: Meta, dueña de Facebook e Instagram, está valuada en más de 1,5 billones de dólares, frente a los 10.000 millones de dólares de Instinct, la startup que llevó a Zuckerberg a ordenar el lanzamiento adelantado de Muse.

articles.title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Meta’s Superintelligence Lab released a pair of new state-of-the-art models on Monday, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, representing the company’s first attempt at a frontier model.
Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding.
According to Meta’s testing (presented in the model card), Wonder and Wonder Full achieve comparable benchmark scores to Fable 5.1 and GPT-6 Astra.
“Together, they mark the next step on our scaling ladder and a major leap toward personal superintelligence,” Meta’s blog post about the models reads.
That scale is reflected in the pricing: Accessed through the Meta Model API, Wonder will cost $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, making it roughly equivalent in cost to GPT-6 Sol or Opus 5.5.
Notably, Wonder Full will only be available to Muse Code subscribers and will not be served through the API. Both models will also be used to power the Muse agent.
In keeping with Meta’s interest in developing personal assistants that can perform tasks over a long period, the company placed particular emphasis on the new models’ ability to retain and synthesize information given by the user, a property Meta calls “active memory.”
To achieve better recall, Meta highlighted the MemoryBench benchmark, which challenges continual learning and memory construction frameworks. According to the company’s testing, Muse Wonder now scores higher on MemoryBench than Fable, Opus, or Astra.
“We put a tremendous amount of effort into making sure your model can remember what’s important to you over days, weeks, months, and beyond,” said research scientist Kavya Kopparapu in a video accompanying the launch.
The new models are the first frontier model release since Scale AI founder Alexandr Wang restructured Meta’s AI efforts in August of last year. Since then, Meta has released its lightweight Muse Spark model and Muse agent but has avoided the kind of state-of-the-art model releases OpenAI and Anthropic are known for.
According to the post, the models were trained at Meta’s Prometheus data center in central Ohio, which came online earlier this year.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 12, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (October 12, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Monday, October 12, 2026.
From ShuruKar, billed as the first nationwide district-level movement of its kind that aims to help young Indians identify a problem worth solving in their district, to India’s ecommerce platforms recording around Rs 24,000 crore in sales during the first two days of festive shopping, here are the latest developments across sectors.
Featured Stories
ShuruKar: Your next business could start in your hometown
A big idea does not need a big city. That was the message from Patna, where The Bharat Project, an initiative by YourStory, launched ShuruKar at Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Science City in Rajinder Nagar.
Developed in partnership with DPIIT and Startup India, ShuruKar is billed as the first nationwide district-level movement of its kind. It aims to help young Indians identify a problem worth solving in their district, build a business around it, and continue growing it.
The launch drew Shri Nitish Mishra, Minister, Urban Development and Housing Department, Government of Bihar, along with founders, students and young entrepreneurs from across the state.
Latest News
Ecommerce firms sell goods worth Rs 24k Cr in first two days of festive sales
Ecommerce firms are estimated to have sold goods worth around Rs 24,000 crore in the first two days of the festive season sale, driven by growth in order volumes, with mobile phones accounting for the biggest share in value terms, according to consultancy firm Redseer Strategy Consultants.
The consultancy firm estimated that shoppers placed about 8-9 crore orders across all platforms, including Amazon, Flipkart, Meesho, Ajio and many other marketplaces.
Redseer Strategy Consultants, Associate Partner, Nikhil Dalal told PTI that the first two days pointed to India's festive e-commerce basket getting wider. The growth is being led by order volumes, with consumers spreading spend beyond mobiles into fashion, electronics and appliances as well.
Funding News
Zetwerk sets IPO price band at Rs 143-151, aims to raise Rs 5,012 Cr
Zetwerk, the Bengaluru-headquartered manufacturing marketplace, has set a price band of Rs 143–151 per share for its initial public offering (IPO), targeting a valuation of Rs 25,583 crore.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale (OFS). The company has expanded the size of the public issue to Rs 5,012 crore.
The fresh issue has been increased from Rs 2,600 crore to Rs 2,830 crore, while the OFS component has been expanded from 9.68 crore shares to 14.45 crore shares.
Other News
Kyndryl and WPP Expand Strategic Partnership to Drive AI-Powered Transformation and Growth
Kyndryl and WPP have expanded their strategic partnership to drive business transformation, marketing growth, and joint go-to-market initiatives. WPP will deploy Kyndryl’s Agentic AI Framework and Kyndryl Bridge to modernize its IT applications, streamline cloud operations, and support its Elevate28 strategy for cost efficiency.
In turn, Kyndryl named WPP as its preferred global marketing partner, broadening their work across digital, experiential, and integrated marketing powered by WPP Open. Furthermore, Kyndryl Consult and WPP Enterprise Solutions will deepen joint go-to-market efforts to help enterprise clients transform customer engagement through AI, data, and emerging technology.
TimBuckDo and Hubble Partner to Deliver Exclusive Brand Rewards to Student Gig Workers
Bangalore-based consumer tech platform TimBuckDo has partnered with fintech rewards infrastructure provider Hubble to expand benefits for India’s student community. Through this collaboration, TimBuckDo's network of over 700,000 verified, educated college students—known as "Doers"—will gain access to relevant discounts and offers from more than 500 brands across 20+ categories.
While TimBuckDo enables students to find on-demand gig, household, and campaign opportunities to build the "Pink Collar Economy," the partnership with Hubble ensures students maximize the value of their earnings by connecting rewards directly to their active income moments.""
River Mobility enters Nepal with first international store in Kathmandu
River Mobility has entered Nepal, marking its first international expansion with the opening of a retail and service centre in Kathmandu’s Naxal neighbourhood, in partnership with Vishal Group. The store will showcase its flagship electric scooter, the Indie, alongside accessories and merchandise, with after-sales support available through a dedicated service centre.
River plans to expand beyond Kathmandu into other key cities in Nepal, building a wider retail and service network. In India, the company operates more than 90 stores and aims to expand this to over 400 by March 2028. The Indie is priced at NPR 3,70,000 in Kathmandu.
Apna launches Campus Tank Season 2, raises startup funding pool to $15 million
Apna has launched the second season of Campus Tank – India’s Next Unicorn 2.0, expanding its funding pool from $6 million to $15 million to support emerging entrepreneurs. In partnership with Chandigarh University, the initiative connects founders with investors, mentorship and incubation support, with funding opportunities spanning pre-seed to Series A.
Season 1 attracted 21,789 registrations from more than 1,200 cities, with Krvvy, Offlyn and Medoc Health emerging as winners across consumer brands, offline experiences and healthcare technology. The initiative aims to extend Apna’s employment mission by helping young entrepreneurs build businesses that generate jobs and drive innovation.
Xoriant adds 25 AI customers, unveils human-centric AI strategy under ‘New Horizons’
Xoriant, the ChrysCapital-backed engineering and technology services firm, has announced its transformation into a human-centric AI company, unveiling a new brand identity, ‘New Horizons’, built around its Human Ingenuity (HI) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) philosophy.
The company said it has added 25 new customers for its AI services as it combines AI capabilities with human judgment, creativity and accountability. Xoriant also plans to make its workforce of more than 5,000 engineers fully AI-fluent while strengthening partnerships with Microsoft, Anthropic, OpenAI and Salesforce. The rebranding reflects its strategy to expand applied AI services and deliver technology solutions for enterprise customers.

articles.title: Toute la puissance de Chrome, sans l'espionnage de Google : découvrez ungoogled-chromium
articles.text:
Toute la puissance de Chrome, sans l'espionnage de Google : découvrez ungoogled-chromium
Vous souhaitez continuer à utiliser Chrome mais vous détacher un maximum de Google et Gemini ? Peut-être que la solution ungoogled-chromium est faite pour vous.
Lourd, blindé d'IA et très mauvais pour la vie privée, Google Chrome est pourtant le navigateur web le plus utilisé au monde depuis de nombreuses années. Malgré des concurrents qui innovent régulièrement comme Opera, Edge, Brave, Firefox ou encore notre chouchou Vivaldi, les habitudes ont la vie dure. Cependant, il est possible de profiter de Chrome tout en se débarrassant de la plupart de ses défauts en se passant totalement de l'intégration avec Google : voici ungoogle-chromium.
Chromium sans Google, c'est possible
Comme son nom l'indique, cette solution open source se base sur Chromium, le navigateur libre de Google sur lequel s'appuient Chrome et de nombreux autres navigateurs. L'objectif d'ungoogle-chromium est simple : supprimer totalement les liens avec les services web de Google pour protéger la vie privée de l'utilisateur, tout en proposant une expérience aussi proche que possible de Chromium sans la dénaturer.
Ainsi, la connexion et la synchronisation à un compte Google dans le navigateur ont disparu, de même que Gemini et toutes les fonctionnalités de Google qui "entravent le contrôle et la transparence". Il reste possible d'utiliser des services comme Gmail et YouTube, et même de s'y connecter avec un compte Google, mais toutes les requêtes de Google en arrière-plan dans le navigateur sont désactivées de base.
Des guides pour installer et mettre à jour des extensions ou encore activer la correction orthographique sont de la partie, prouvant qu'il faudra probablement un peu mettre les mains sous le capot pour personnaliser son expérience selon ses besoins. Par défaut, de nombreuses fonctionnalités sont désactivées, y compris celles orientées contrôle et transparence ajoutées par le projet. Il faudra se rendre dans les flags pour les activer.
Disponible sur Windows, macOS et Linux, ungoogle-chromium n'est pas la solution la plus aisée côté installation pour les néophytes. Le logiciel est cependant disponible via plusieurs répertoires d'applications et sur sa page GitHub.

articles.title: La CIA tenía una pista aérea secreta para combatir al comunismo. 50 años después, China la está llenando de aviones para la guerra
articles.text:
El 30 de septiembre, un satélite comercial fotografió una pista militar en construcción a unos 50 kilómetros de Vientián, la capital de Laos. Las imágenes revelaron ocho aviones de ataque ligero y decenas de vehículos militares en una instalación que China acababa de presentar como un centro conjunto de entrenamiento. El hallazgo tenía una dimensión histórica inesperada: el mismo aeródromo había sido utilizado clandestinamente por la CIA durante la guerra de Vietnam.
El descubrimiento. Las imágenes tomadas por la empresa estadounidense Vantor el 30 de septiembre, apenas un día después del anuncio oficial chino, mostraban ocho aviones identificados por especialistas como probables Hongdu JL-8, también conocidos como K-8, junto a más de veinte vehículos de apoyo. Las fotografías revelaban también importantes obras alrededor de una pista que todavía estaba en construcción.
La transformación del lugar resulta especialmente llamativa al compararla con imágenes de meses anteriores, cuando buena parte del terreno estaba ocupado por campos agrícolas y caminos de tierra. En su lugar aparecen ahora edificios, instalaciones militares y una pista pavimentada cuya ampliación continúa en marcha.
Aviones con capacidad de combate. Los Hongdu JL-8 son aviones biplaza desarrollados conjuntamente por China y Pakistán, diseñados principalmente para la formación de pilotos militares y equipados para realizar misiones de ataque ligero. Pueden transportar bombas y otras armas, lo que les permite participar en operaciones de combate, aunque sus capacidades son inferiores a las de un caza moderno.
Tanto China como Laos utilizan este modelo, y el Instituto Internacional de Estudios Estratégicos calcula que la fuerza aérea laosiana dispone de cuatro aparatos, cuyo estado operativo ha sido cuestionado por algunos analistas. La presencia de ocho unidades en Ban Keun ha despertado interrogantes sobre su procedencia y sus futuras funciones, sin que las fotografías permitan determinar quién las opera o si están preparadas para entrar inmediatamente en combate.
El antiguo aeródromo secreto de la CIA. Durante la guerra de Vietnam, Ban Keun formaba parte de una red clandestina de pistas utilizadas por Estados Unidos para sostener sus operaciones encubiertas en Laos. La instalación era conocida como Lima Site 44 y estaba vinculada a Air America, una aerolínea controlada discretamente por la Agencia Central de Inteligencia estadounidense.
Sus aviones y helicópteros transportaban suministros y combatientes de la minoría hmong, aliados de Washington en la lucha contra las fuerzas comunistas. Según documentación histórica citada por Reuters, ya en 1968 los helicópteros de Air America utilizaban Ban Keun para trasladar tropas hmong hacia otras zonas de combate. El mismo lugar que sirvió a las operaciones secretas estadounidenses está siendo transformado ahora con ayuda de su principal competidor estratégico en Asia.
La explicación oficial de Pekín. El Ministerio de Defensa chino anunció el 29 de septiembre la apertura de un centro conjunto de apoyo y entrenamiento destinado a mejorar la preparación de los pilotos de la fuerza aérea de Laos. Pekín aseguró entonces que las instalaciones responden a un acuerdo bilateral y que sus actividades no están dirigidas contra ningún tercer país.
UN VISTAZO A...
La elección de Ban Keun ofrece ventajas prácticas: se encuentra en una zona relativamente llana de un país predominantemente montañoso y dispone de conexiones terrestres con China, incluido el corredor ferroviario que une ambos territorios. Para Rachel Vandenbrink, analista del Australian Strategic Policy Institute, la decisión parece responder a una oportunidad favorable para establecer una presencia militar accesible en el sudeste asiático continental.
Con potencial para aviones mucho mayores. Uno de los detalles que más interesa a los especialistas es la configuración de las obras, que parece contemplar una futura prolongación de la pista. Alexander Neill, investigador del Pacific Forum, considera que esa ampliación podría permitir la llegada de aeronaves de mayor tamaño, incluidos aviones dedicados a inteligencia de señales y vigilancia electrónica.
Los analistas siguen también la posible aparición de defensas antiaéreas, depósitos de combustible, almacenes de municiones e instalaciones de vigilancia, elementos que indicarían funciones militares más amplias. Por ahora, el Instituto para el Estudio de la Guerra considera que Ban Keun todavía carece de la infraestructura necesaria para sostener grandes operaciones de combate.
La expansión militar china fuera de sus fronteras. La instalación de Laos representa un paso significativo para un país que, pese a décadas de modernización militar, mantiene una red de bases exteriores relativamente limitada. China dispone de una base logística en Yibuti, instalaciones militares en islas disputadas del mar de China Meridional y acceso a una infraestructura naval conjunta en Ream, Camboya.
Ban Keun podría convertirse en su primera instalación militar exterior centrada específicamente en operaciones aéreas en el sudeste asiático continental. Su desarrollo permitiría al Ejército Popular de Liberación reforzar sus vínculos con Laos y disponer de nuevas opciones logísticas y rutas de acceso hacia una región de creciente importancia estratégica.
La inquietud de los vecinos. Qué duda cabe, la evolución de Ban Keun está siendo observada especialmente por Vietnam y Tailandia, dos países directamente afectados por cualquier cambio en el equilibrio militar regional. Vietnam mantiene disputas territoriales con Pekín en el mar de China Meridional, mientras que Tailandia ha reconocido el derecho soberano de Laos a permitir la instalación, aunque ha anunciado que seguirá vigilando su desarrollo.
Algunos expertos taiwaneses también han señalado que una base aérea china plenamente desarrollada en Laos podría adquirir relevancia en una eventual crisis relacionada con Taiwán o las rutas aéreas del sudeste asiático. El alcance real de esas posibilidades dependerá de las capacidades que Pekín termine desplegando en una pista que, durante la Guerra Fría, ya ocupó un lugar en las operaciones militares secretas de otra superpotencia.

articles.title: Microsoft Edge prépare un assistant IA pour résoudre vos problèmes de navigation
articles.text:
Microsoft teste un nouvel assistant capable de diagnostiquer les problèmes d’Edge grâce à l’intelligence artificielle. Pour affiner ses recommandations, il pourra examiner des données techniques du navigateur, mais uniquement avec votre accord.
Une vidéo qui refuse de se lancer, une synchronisation qui échoue, un site qui met une éternité à charger… Quand Edge dysfonctionne, trouver l’origine du problème peut vite tourner au casse-tête. Microsoft travaille donc sur « Résoudre un problème » (Fix an issue), un assistant de dépannage intégré aux paramètres du navigateur, capable d’analyser les difficultés rencontrées et de proposer des solutions. Repéré dès juin dans Edge Canary, l’outil a récemment fait son apparition en version bêta, tandis que Microsoft a également publié une documentation officielle pour préciser quelles données l’IA pourra utiliser et dans quelles conditions.
Une IA pour trouver l’origine des problèmes dans Edge
Accessible depuis les paramètres du navigateur, Résoudre un problème permet aux internautes de décrire leur problème ou de choisir parmi plusieurs situations prédéfinies. Dans la version bêta testée par Windows Report, l’outil en propose quatre : les vidéos qui ne se lancent pas, les problèmes de synchronisation, les difficultés de connexion à un compte et les sites web trop lents.
L’assistant analyse ensuite la demande et propose des pistes de résolution. Pour une vidéo qui refuse de démarrer, il peut par exemple conseiller de mettre à jour le pilote graphique. Face à un site qui peine à charger, il suggère plutôt de vérifier la connexion Internet ou de mettre Edge à jour.
En revanche, la fonction ne prend pas directement la main sur Edge pour appliquer ses recommandations. Les internautes doivent effectuer les manipulations proposées, sans garantie de résultat. Microsoft reconnaît d’ailleurs que l’IA peut se tromper, fournir des réponses incomplètes ou échouer à identifier l’origine du problème.
Des données de diagnostic accessibles avec votre accord
Pour affiner ses recommandations, Résoudre un problème pourra s'appuyer sur les données de diagnostic facultatives d'Edge et consulter l'état de ses paramètres. L'assistant pourra ainsi tenir compte d'informations sur la configuration du navigateur, sans dépendre exclusivement de la description du problème fournie par les internautes.
Mais cet accès nécessitera leur autorisation. Dans sa documentation officielle, Microsoft assure que l'outil ne collectera ces informations qu'après avoir obtenu le consentement de l'utilisateur, dans le cadre d'une session de dépannage qu'il aura lui-même lancée. La collecte se limitera alors à cette session, sans surveillance permanente de l'activité de navigation en arrière-plan. La fonction n'accédera pas non plus aux ressources professionnelles.
Les internautes pourront refuser de partager ces informations et désactiver cette collecte dans les paramètres d’Edge, sous « Copilot et IA ». Cette option concerne uniquement les données facultatives utilisées par l'assistant de dépannage, et non les autres données de diagnostic que le navigateur peut déjà recueillir selon ses propres réglages.
La documentation consacrée à la fonctionnalité ne détaille toutefois ni la liste exacte des informations utilisées par l'assistant ni leur durée de conservation. Microsoft indique avoir réalisé des évaluations des risques liés à la confidentialité avant le déploiement, sans apporter davantage de précisions sur le traitement des données propres à cet outil. Pour l'heure, l'assistant fait toujours l'objet de tests et aucune date de lancement général n'a été annoncée.

articles.title: Homeview: Was Apples Smarthome-Display können soll
articles.text:
Die lange erwartete neue Heimzentrale von Apple könnte „Homeview“ heißen. Davon geht Bloomberg-Reporter Mark Gurman aus, der den Begriff in seinem aktuellen Newsletter durchgehend verwendet. Vorgestellt werden soll das Gerät bereits am 14. Oktober. Bislang lief es in der Gerüchteküche unter Namen wie „Home Hub“ oder „HomePad“.
Für den Namen spricht eine Markenanmeldung, die Macrumors entdeckt hat. Eine Firma namens „Home Service LLC“ meldete „Homeview“ im vergangenen Jahr in den USA und weiteren Ländern an. Zum gleichen Zeitpunkt sicherte sich eine „Home Operations Suite LLC“ den Begriff „homeOS“. Dahinter dürfte das Betriebssystem des Geräts stecken. Beide Firmen stehen vermutlich mit Apple in Verbindung.
Zwei Bauformen, sechs Farben
Laut Gurman ist der Homeview das zentrale Element einer neuen Apple-Smart-Home-Strategie. Dazu gehört auch günstige Hardware, die der iPhone-Hersteller gemeinsam mit LG auf den Markt bringen will. Sie soll mit HomeKit funktionieren, Apples System zur Steuerung vernetzter Geräte, und von Apple direkt beworben werden. Das Display des Homeview könnte früheren Gerüchten zufolge sechs Zoll groß und quadratisch sein.
In der „Siri-Kommandozentrale“ arbeitet laut Gurman ein A18-Chip – derselbe Prozessor, den Apple in der iPhone-16-Reihe verbaut. Den Homeview soll es in zwei Varianten geben: als Tischgerät mit einer Lautsprecherbasis aus Metall, die besseren Klang liefern soll als ein HomePod Mini, und als Wandversion mit flacher, quadratischer Lautsprecherbasis unten. Das Tischmodell erscheint angeblich in vier Farben: Spacegrau, Silber, „Starlight“ (ein Goldton) und Pink. Die Wandversion soll es in Silber und Spacegrau geben.
Sehen statt tippen
Der Name beschreibt laut Gurman das Bedienkonzept: Die Nutzer schauen auf das Display, steuern das Gerät aber vor allem per Sprache. Eine Bedienung per Touch ist ebenfalls möglich. Einen App-Store plant Apple zunächst nicht, obwohl das Gerät mit homeOS ein eigenes Betriebssystem bekommt. Stattdessen gibt es Apple-eigene Apps wie FaceTime, vermutlich auch Nachrichten (iMessage) und natürlich Home zur Smart-Home-Steuerung.
Im Standby soll der Homeview die Uhrzeit und weitere Informationen wie das Wetter anzeigen – ähnlich wie konkurrierende Heimzentralen wie die von Amazon. Nähert sich eine Person, erkennt das die eingebaute Kamera und das Gerät wechselt in den aktiven Modus. Die Oberfläche könnte eine Mischung aus iPadOS und watchOS sein.
Europa muss wohl warten
Zusammen mit Zubehör von LG und – für Europa – von Schneider Electric soll der Homeview als Einsteigerpaket fürs smarte Zuhause dienen – und damit Boden gegenüber Amazon und Google gut machen. Für europäische Kunden gibt es allerdings einen Dämpfer: Das Gerät ist nach bisherigen Erkenntnissen zunächst auf Englisch optimiert, zudem läuft Siri mit KI-Funktionen in der EU noch nicht auf dem iPhone, das vermutlich zur Einrichtung des HomeView dient. Der Verkaufsstart hierzulande könnte sich deshalb verzögern.
Neben dem HomeView erwartet Gurman für den 13. Oktober auch ein neues Apple TV 4K mit schnellerem Chip und Unterstützung für Siri AI sowie eine zweite Generation des HomePod Mini. Gegen Mittag europäischer Zeit könnte Apple dazu ein Video veröffentlichen, das die neuen Geräte zeigt. Ein Livestream ist offenbar nicht geplant.

articles.title: NexPhone, a Pocket PC-Smartphone Running Windows 11 Linux and Android, Launching in 2027
articles.text:
Monday, October 12th 2026
NexPhone, a Pocket PC-Smartphone Running Windows 11 Linux and Android, Launching in 2027
Nex Computer is the company behind the NexPhone, an upcoming smartphone that doubles as a pocketable computer running Android, Linux, and Windows 11. While the project was first announced a whole 14 years ago, Nex Computer recently published a development blog update revealing a Q1 2027 launch, indicating that the NexPhone will launch around March 2027.
Our estimated shipping window is now the end of Q1 2027 (March 2027). New preorders are priced at $599, and the device price remains protected for customers who reserved at either $549 or $599. NexPhone is now running Android 17 on development devices, with continued Linux and Windows development.
In the post, Nex Computer also clarifies that the NexPhone will run Android 17 when it launches, and it will be able to switch to a Debian Linux installation without rebooting the device, with a Windows 11 dual-boot option available as well. The idea behind the NexPhone is to pack a fully desktop-class device, with cross-platform access to files and information, into a smartphone form factor. In addition to the Windows and Linux installations, NexPhone will feature a customized Android desktop mode with a custom tabbed file manager and support for files and folders on the desktop.Judging from the wording in the dev log, it seems as though the Windows 11 and Linux installations may not be full-featured at launch, since the developer notes that driver and platform support for Windows 11 on the Qualcomm SoC is still in-development. However, Linux support appears to be included, even if Nex Computer also notes that development is ongoing for that as well.The NexPhone preorders start at $599, but the MSRP will be higher when it fully launches, although no indication has been provided for that MSRP.

articles.title: Employees are faking using AI at work to impress their bosses
articles.text:
Employees are faking using AI at work to impress their bosses
Workers are lying about AI adoption out of fear
- Half say AI has significantly changed their roles, a quarter are worried about job loss
- Three in five believe their employer has no clear AI plan – or no plan at all
- Training and transparency are the most demanded changes by workers
A new Visier report has uncovered just how prolific AI exaggeration could be in the workforce, raising questions about exactly how useful the technology actually is to most workers.
As many as one in two (48%) employees admitted exaggerating their usage or expertise to colleagues or managers some or most of the time, with nearly as many (45%) feeling pressured to use AI at work.
This comes against a backdrop of major change – more than half (54%) say AI has significantly changed their roles over the past two years. With that in mine, the report details how workers feel they've been impacted, and how much support they're getting from the workplace.
AI is changing roles, and many are lying about how they use it
One in three (32%) admit their employer has no clear plan, and more than a quarter (27%) aren't even sure their employer has any AI plan at all, and that much is clear in that only one-third believe their leaders understand how much AI training and support they need.
Barely one-fifth (21%) would strongly agree that their employer provides sufficient training and support, making upskilling opportunities (32%) the most sought-after thing workers are calling for – a close first, just ahead of greater transparency (31%).
Workers are also worried about AI's impacts on their jobs, with 24% calling for more career advancement opportunities and 18% calling for clearer communication about how it could impact them. In fact, the most frequently identified concern is job loss – a worry raised by one in for (24%).
"People told us that they actually want to be equipped and informed, not shielded or protected from AI-driven change," Research and Customer Value Principal Dr Andrea Derler explained.
