articles.title: Marvell Unveils Second-generation Structera X, Industry-first Six-channel CXL 3.2 Memory Expanders for AI Inference
articles.text:
Monday, October 12th 2026
Marvell Unveils Second-generation Structera X, Industry-first Six-channel CXL 3.2 Memory Expanders for AI Inference
Marvell Technology, Inc. , a leader in data infrastructure semiconductor solutions, today announced the second-generation Marvell Structera X 3406 and Marvell Structera X 3506 CXL memory expanders, designed to help cloud, enterprise and AI infrastructure providers build more efficient, scalable and higher-performance systems for the next era of AI and computing. Designed to address the evolving needs of leading hyperscale datacenters, Structera X addresses the most demanding data center workload requirements.
AI and ML workloads are rewriting the rules of data center design. Growing LLM sizes, expanding context windows and growing KV-cache requirements are driving unprecedented memory demands that traditional server architectures simply cannot meet. Memory is a critical constraint of AI performance and infrastructure efficiency.Modern AI inference workloads, from LLM serving to deep learning recommendation models (DLRM), are memory bound. KV-cache capacity directly determines time to first token (TTFT), throughput, and XPU utilization. Structera X 3406/3506 addresses these bottlenecks with:
- Industry-first six-channel CXL memory expansion: Six DDR4/DDR5 memory channels deliver 50% more channels than the previous generation, increasing memory bandwidth and capacity so AI servers can sustain larger models and longer context windows - up to 18 DDR4 RDIMM slots supporting 9 TB for Structera X 3406 and 12 DDR5 RDIMM slots supporting 6 TB for Structera X 3506.
- Industry-first four host connectivity: Enables memory capacity sharing with up to four hosts and up to 256 GB/s PCIe 6.0 x16 of host bandwidth, improving memory utilization and efficiency across AI clusters.
- 5x higher LZ4 compression throughput from previous generation: Up to 250 GB/s compression/decompression throughput unlocks up to 2-3x more effective memory capacity, depending on workloads.
- StructGuard enterprise-grade RAS: Provides advanced error correction to enhance memory reliability and resilience against DRAM device failures.
- Industry-first post-quantum security: Combines post-quantum cryptography, Caliptra 2.0, CXL IDE and AES-256 memory encryption to provide advanced data protection.
For DLRM workloads, Structera X delivers up to 2x higher queries per second and 2-3x more effective embedding-table capacity per controller. For LLM serving, Structera X delivers up to 40-50% faster TTFT at equivalent context length, or up to 2x longer supportable context windows at equivalent latency compared to the previous generation.
Building on the success of the first-generation Structera X 2404/2504, the Structera X 3406/3506 leverages the proven software stack and ecosystem integrations enabling an accelerated ramp. The Marvell CXL ecosystem continues to expand across the full data center stack through close partnership with CPU and memory vendors, OEMs, ODMs and system integrators.
"CXL is starting to gain widespread adoption in AI systems since they reap strong benefits from its very high bandwidth and support of large memory sizes," said Jim Handy, general director of Objective Analysis, and author of a CXL market report. "In addition, today's memory shortage and subsequent high prices are driving IT managers to use CXL to re-deploy used DDR4 DIMMs into DDR5 systems for immediate cost savings. In the near future, these same managers will use CXL's memory pools to reduce stranded memory and drive greater savings, and they will find controllers that offer compression, as this one does, to be even more interesting."
By bringing together connectivity, memory and storage technologies, the expanded data center portfolio improves how compute and memory work across AI systems, increasing utilization, infrastructure efficiency and AI performance. These next-generation offerings increase access to memory resources, improving both memory and compute utilization, helping customers optimize AI infrastructure performance as workloads continue to grow in scale and complexity.
"Marvell is the only provider with a complete end-to-end CXL portfolio spanning memory expansion (Structera X), near-memory acceleration (Structera A), and PFMA (Photonic Fabric Memory Appliance), pod-scale CXL memory-sharing appliance, giving customers a complete portfolio from direct-attach to disaggregated memory pooling," said Will Chu, executive vice president and general manager, Custom Cloud Solutions at Marvell. "We are delivering industry-leading CXL controllers, co-developed with leading hyperscalers to address the most demanding AI infrastructure requirements."
Industry Ecosystem Support
"AMD is advancing an open ecosystem that gives enterprises the freedom to build infrastructure around their evolving workloads," said Raghu Nambiar, corporate vice president, Data Center Ecosystems and Solutions, AMD. "CXL is an important part of that vision, enabling customers to expand memory capacity and use resources more efficiently as AI and data-intensive applications grow. Our collaboration with Marvell builds on the performance and scalability of AMD EPYC processors to help enterprises realize those benefits, bringing greater flexibility and long-term value to their data center investments."
"As AI becomes more agentic, memory and compute need to scale together to meet growing infrastructure demands. Marvell's latest Structera X controllers bring CXL 3.2, memory expansion and compression to the Arm ecosystem, giving hyperscaler customers more options to efficiently support complex AI workloads," said Eddie Ramirez, vice president of go-to-market, Cloud AI, Arm.
"Marvell and Alibaba are collaborating to advance CXL memory solutions for the rapidly growing demands of AI infrastructure. As AI models and workloads continue to increase in scale, expanding memory capacity and bandwidth without compromising system performance and efficiency has become a critical requirement. CXL enables a more flexible approach to memory expansion and sharing, providing a path to scale memory resources across increasingly complex AI systems. Our collaboration with Marvell brings together its leadership in CXL technology with Alibaba's experience in large-scale AI and cloud infrastructure to develop memory architectures designed for the next generation of AI data centers."
"CXL is reshaping how memory is deployed in data centers, and our work with Marvell ensures customers can confidently deploy Structera with Samsung DDR memory for reliable, high-performance systems," said Jangseok Choi (JS Choi), vice president of the Memory Product Planning Team at Samsung Electronics. "The move to CXL 3.2 and six memory channels in Structera X 3406/3506 further strengthens the flexibility our joint customers need."
"Working with Marvell to validate Structera with SK hynix memory supports our shared goal of making memory expansion more accessible and flexible," said Uksong Kang, Head of Next Generation Product Planning and Enabling at SK hynix. "Structera X 3406/3506 gives customers the tools they need to build future-ready, disaggregated architectures with less friction and more choice."
Availability
Marvell Structera X 3406 and Structera X 3506 CXL memory expansion controllers are expected to sample in Q1 2027.

articles.title: Microsoft president says UK is best placed to drive AI regulation | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Microsoft president Brad Smith is calling for urgent regulation of AI, and his argument is that consumer products like milk and washing machines have more oversight than the companies building artificial intelligence.
On a recent BBC podcast, Smith called AI both a “weapon and a tool” that is putting the world’s cybersecurity at risk and said the “moment has arrived” to institute global safety rules.
Smith also said the U.K., and not the U.S. or European Union, is best placed to lead on global safety rules. Britain’s AI Security Institute (AISI), launched in 2023, receives access to major models from U.S. frontier labs before they are deployed and has quickly become a leader in AI safety testing.
That role has been under threat in recent weeks, with U.S. president Donald Trump warning against “globalist” organizations, which he claims are interfering with American companies. Last month, he reportedly asked Anthropic and OpenAI to withhold new models from British testers, but AISI confirmed on Monday that it is able to access and test the latest models.
Despite the president’s pushback, however, Smith argued the U.K. can regulate AI in ways that the U.S. cannot.
“In Washington, D.C., people don’t look at the U.K. and they don’t look at London the way they look at Brussels,” he told the BBC. “That’s a strength.”
His comments come amid rallying cries from tech leaders, including Anthropic’s Dario Amodei and OpenAI’s Sam Altman, to slow the pace of AI development in the wake of several incidents where AI agents went rogue.
Last month, Trump hosted tech leaders of companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Nvidia, AMD, SpaceX, Meta, and Google, at the White House to discuss AI safety. They signed a “morally binding” document in which they agreed to work with “independent auditors” to assess the safety and capabilities of their AI models.
Smith says the document is a “good step,” but it stops short of the type of regulation that is necessary. The problem with voluntary self-regulation, he said, is that only the “good companies” will comply.
“It’s the companies that are not as responsible that you need to worry about,” he said.
Smith outlined several AI safety rules he’d like to see put into place, like a legal obligation to alert an organization if its system was breached by rogue AI agents. He also appears to be in favor of AI labs getting the approval of outside evaluators before an AI product is released and spoke positively about kill switches to pause or slow down AI if humans lose control of it.
“Let’s speak calmly, maybe even softly, but firmly, and start to bring people together,” Smith said. “I hope that’s the role we can play as a company. I hope that’s the role the U.K. can play as a country.”

articles.title: VR ohne Brille: Macht dieser Sessel Meta Quest und Vision Pro Konkurrenz?
articles.text:
Statt Meta Quest und Vision Pro: Dieser Sessel will VR ohne Brille ermöglichen
Der Preis, um in die virtuelle oder erweiterte Realität (VR/XR) einzutauchen, hört nicht bei den Kosten für Brillen wie die Meta Quest oder die Apple Vision Pro auf. Sie drücken bei längerer Tragezeit auf Stirn, Nase und Ohren, man schwitzt und mitunter kommt noch Übelkeit hinzu, wenn sich die Augen und der Gleichgewichtssinn nicht einig sind, wie sie die Eindrücke verarbeiten sollen.
Die Alternative zu den Datenbrillen sind Vorführräume, in denen die Inhalte auf Bildschirmen oder mithilfe von Projektoren in einem geschlossenen Raum rund um die Besuchenden gezeigt werden. Das ist eine Option für Messen und Ausstellungen in Museen, aber eher nichts für den Heimgebrauch.
Doch was wäre, wenn es eine dritte Möglichkeit gäbe, virtuelle Realität zu erleben? Quasi einen Mittelweg zwischen Datenbrille und Projektionsraum? Genau daran arbeiten Forschende rund um Shogo Fukushima an der Kyushu University im japanischen Fukuoka. Das Team hat einen Prototypen eines neuartigen VR-Sessels entwickelt und diesen im Sommer im Rahmen der renommierten Konferenz SIGGRAPH für Computergrafik vorgestellt.
Bilder, die im freien Raum schweben
Der Sessel soll die fixierte Umgebung eines Vorführraums mit der individuellen Perspektive einer VR-Brille kombinieren. Sobald eine Person im Sessel sitzt, fährt die optische Einheit von oben runter und erzeugt so einen halb offenen, halb geschlossenen Raum. Die Besonderheit liegt darin, dass die Betrachter nicht auf einen Bildschirm schauen, sondern auf Bilder, die in der Luft zu schweben scheinen.
Das Team aus Fukuoka nennt das Aerial Imaging, zu Deutsch etwa Luftbildprojektion, nicht zu verwechseln mit statischen Hologrammen, die mithilfe von Lasern auf eine Oberfläche projiziert werden.
Ausgangspunkt ist ein besonders heller Bildschirm, der leicht geneigt unter dem natürlichen Blickfeld der Betrachter platziert ist. Dessen Licht fällt zunächst durch eine sogenannte Sammellinse. Sie bündelt die Lichtstrahlen, die anschließend auf eine spezielle Platte aus zahlreichen winzigen Spiegeln treffen. Diese Mikrospiegel lenken das Licht schließlich gezielt um, sodass das ursprüngliche Bild an einer anderen Stelle im Raum erscheint.
Um den gewünschten immersiven Effekt zu erzielen, also das Gefühl, sich tatsächlich innerhalb einer Szene zu befinden, bekommen das linke und das rechte Auge eine etwas unterschiedliche Perspektive angezeigt – wie beim natürlichen Sehen und bei VR-Brillen. Das Gehirn besorgt den Rest und erstellt daraus einen dreidimensionalen Raum.
Weniger Übelkeit im VR-Sessel
Der Einsatz von Luftbildprojektion als 3D-Displays ist nicht neu; gerade japanische Wissenschaftlerinnen und Wissenschaftler sind in diesem Forschungsfeld seit einigen Jahren aktiv. Das Team der Kyushu University hat das Prinzip nun um einen drehbaren Sessel ergänzt: Ein Tablet registriert mithilfe seines eingebauten Bewegungssensors, wenn sich der Betrachter im Sessel dreht. Daraufhin wird die dargestellte Perspektive in Echtzeit angepasst, was den VR-Effekt verstärkt.
Trotzdem ist dieser natürlich nicht so ausgeprägt wie mit einer Brille. Die erfasst jede kleinste Kopfbewegung und passt die Perspektive entsprechend an, während sich im vorgestellten Fall der Sessel dreht. Zudem ist das Sichtfeld begrenzt, da dieses von der Größe der Spiegelplatten abhängig ist. Das Sichtfeld und die Bildqualität ließen sich durch „austauschbare Komponenten“ anpassen, schreiben die Forschenden.
„Unser System hat zudem das Potenzial, die VR-Übelkeit in Zukunft zu verringern“, sagt Studienleiter Shogo Fukushima in einer Pressemitteilung. „Da das Design nicht durch ein Headset eingeschränkt wird, lassen sich größere optische Komponenten und Bewegungsmechanismen freier integrieren. Diese Flexibilität könnte neue Ansätze ermöglichen, um die Diskrepanz zwischen visuellen und körperlichen Empfindungen zu verringern, die zur VR-Übelkeit beitragen kann.“
Das Team sucht nun nach Partnern aus der Industrie, um das Prinzip unter anderem in interaktiven Museumsausstellungen, zur Steuerung von Maschinen und in der Robotik zu testen.

articles.title: Gigabyte GO27Q24G 27-inch OLED 240 Hz QHD gaming monitor review: Tremendous bang for the buck
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Gigabyte GO27Q24G leaves out a few peripheral bits but delivers incredible performance and image quality for a super low price. It’s a competition weapon and gamers’ dream for sure.
Reasons to buy
- + Brighter than the competition
- + Accurate color with calibration
- + Premium video processing with options for slower systems
- + Premium styling and build quality
- + Terrific value
Reasons to avoid
- - Light gamma and warm color temp out of the box
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
OLED or LCD? This is a question many monitor shoppers ask themselves. When you consider the pros and cons of each, there isn’t a clear winner. OLED has better image quality thanks to its extreme contrast. But LCDs are brighter and less expensive. So, what if you could move the needle further towards one of the best OLED gaming monitors?
Gigabyte has done this with the GO27Q24G. This 27-inch QHD 240 Hz OLED delivers brightness over 1,300 nits for a shockingly low price of just $350 as I write this. Cutting corners? That’s a hard nope. You get 240 Hz, FHD gaming modes, wide gamut color, Adaptive-Sync, gaming aids, HDR10 and premium build quality. Let’s take a look.
Gigabyte GO27Q24G Specs
| Panel Type / Backlight | Organic Light Emitting Diode (OLED) | 
| Screen Size / Aspect Ratio | 27 inches / 16:9 | 
| Max Resolution and Refresh Rate | 2560x1440 @ 240 Hz | 
| Row 3 - Cell 0 | FreeSync and G-Sync Compatible | 
| Native Color Depth and Gamut | 10-bit / DCI-P3 | 
| Row 5 - Cell 0 | HDR10 | 
| Row 6 - Cell 0 | DisplayHDR 400 True Black | 
| Response Time (GTG) | 0.03ms | 
| Brightness (mfr) | 275 nits full field | 
| Row 9 - Cell 0 | 1,300 nits 1.5% window | 
| Contrast | Unmeasurable | 
| Speakers | None | 
| Video Inputs | 1x DisplayPort 1.4 | 
| Row 13 - Cell 0 | 2x HDMI 2.1, 1x USB-C | 
| Audio | 3.5mm headphone output | 
| USB | None | 
| Power Consumption | 30.5w, brightness @ 200 nits | 
| Panel Dimensions WxHxD w/base | 23.8 x 15.5-20.6 x 7.4 inches (604 x 394-523 x 188mm) | 
| Panel Thickness | 2.1 inches (54mm) | 
| Bezel Width | Top/sides: 0.3 inch (8mm) | 
| Row 20 - Cell 0 | Bottom: 0.4 inch (11mm) | 
| Weight | 12.3 pounds (5.6kg) | 
| Warranty | 3 years | 
The GO27Q24G saves some cost by omitting USB ports, internal speakers, and LED lighting. But there is nothing else critical missing from this impressive display to meet the low price point. The refresh rate is 240 Hz with Adaptive-Sync and certified G-Sync and FreeSync operation. There’s an anti-flicker option to prevent image pumping during rapid frame rate transitions. And you can turn on black frame insertion to keep motion blur at bay when frame rates drop. Video processing gives nothing away to more expensive monitors.
There’s plenty of color and contrast from the WOLED panel. WOLED, or white OLED, achieves color with filters rather than RGB stripes or Quantum Dots. There’s a definite cost saving and you won’t quite get the huge color gamuts found in higher-priced displays. But you do get 96% of DCI-P3 by my measurements, and that’s a colorful image. Accuracy is there as well, with solid results in my tests that you can read about on pages four and five.
The panel’s high brightness comes from a Micro Lens Array, which is essentially a textured layer over the pixels that amplifies light. Each pixel has around 5,000 of these lenses over it, and given the numbers I saw in testing, it clearly works. This approach also reduces power consumption and improves viewing angles.
The GO27Q24G’s screen is glossy but includes an optical coating that deepens black levels and cuts reflections. There’s a lot of metal used here, both behind the panel and in the stand, which is one of the nicest bits I’ve seen in a while. You would never imagine the price tag being so low.
In addition to pro-level video processing, there are gaming aids like reticles, timers and a frame counter. OLED care options are plentiful, with pixel orbiting, logo and perimeter protection, and screen refresh. Variable brightness is available too, which helps bump up the impact of small highlights to as much as 1,300 nits.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
If you’ve been fancying an OLED but didn’t want to spend $600 or more on a 27-inch monitor, the GO27Q24G is a compelling option.
Assembly and Accessories
The GO27Q24G comes packed in crumbly foam in three parts. I was impressed by the stand, which is all-metal and super solid. Everything assembles tool-free. The accessory bundle includes an external power supply and a DisplayPort cable. If you want to use an arm, there’s a 100mm VESA mount, but you’ll need to source your own fasteners.\
Product 360
The GO27Q24G’s styling and build is minimalist in all the right ways. From the front, you only see the image surrounded by a very narrow flush bezel of 8-11 millimeters. There is no plastic trim anywhere in sight and no logos either. Even the power LED is tucked well underneath where you won’t be distracted.
The base is a stamped steel plate with a gray satin finish. Its footprint is small, but with rubber feet and an ideal shape, it’s very stable. The upright is all-metal with very smooth movements and the same gray satin finish. The GO27Q24G includes full ergonomics with 5/21 degrees of tilt, 15 degrees swivel, a 90-degree portrait mode, and a 5.1-inch height range. A small cable clip is included to keep your wires tidy.
The only plastic used is in the back, where a small component bulge is trimmed with generous ventilation and a small Gigabyte logo. There’s a joystick flanked by two buttons and the input panel. It features two HDMI 2.1 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4 with DSC, and a USB-C input which has 15 watts of power. There are no additional USB ports or internal speakers, but you do get a 3.5mm headphone jack.
OSD Features
A single joystick controls the GO27Q24G’s OSD. Two flanking buttons toggle power and switch between aspect ratio modes.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
The OSD screen is well appointed with information. Resolution and refresh numbers are at the top while other parameters are at the bottom. You can quickly check the active input, SDR/HDR status, picture mode, brightness level, gamma setting, and color temp mode.
The GO27Q24G’s Gaming menu has Ultra Clear, which is Gigabyte’s term for black frame insertion. It effectively eliminates motion blur below 120 Hz. It also cuts brightness by around 40%, but it’s a great solution for slower PCs and consoles that operate at low frame rates.
The Picture menu offers 10 picture modes, each with its own set of calibration options. Standard works well and leaves all controls available. There are gamma presets and color temps along with gamut selections. For sRGB, use the sRGB picture mode. The GO27Q24G has variable brightness, which you’d think would be here, but it isn’t. Read on to find it.
The GO27Q24G includes PIP and PBP options with full control of the PIP window’s size and location. You can also program the four joystick directions for quick access to commonly used settings.
To find OLED Care, press the joystick and click left. There are many bits here, like pixel shift, cleaning routines that you can schedule, logo and corner dimming, and APL Stabilize. What is that, you ask? It’s the variable brightness option, which should be in the Picture menu. It has three levels which are termed counterintuitively. You’d think Low means the least stable, as in the most aggressive dimming. Nope, it’s effectively the off button. If you want constant brightness, choose that. High is great for HDR and watching SDR video. With it, you get very bright highlights and deep blacks for an impactful image.
Press the joystick and click right for the Game Assist menu. It has crosshairs and the Tactical Switch. This is fancy-speak for the resolution modes. You can switch on the fly to FHD either full screen or in a 24-inch window. I recommend the latter because it pixel-maps 1:1, thereby avoiding the softness that comes with displaying FHD graphics on a QHD screen. You get black borders, but you can position the picture at the top, bottom, or center of the screen. The switch itself is the button on the right side of the joystick. Don’t press the left one unless you want to turn off the GO27Q24G.
Gigabyte GO27Q24G Calibration Settings
In Standard mode, the GO27Q24G measures OK out of the box but leaves room for improvement. Grayscale is a tad warm, and gamma is too dark, which makes the picture less lively. With a few tweaks to the RGB sliders and a change of gamma preset from 2.2 to 2.0, the picture is greatly improved. Color gamut coverage is nearly 100% of DCI-P3, so you can see a vivid picture in SDR or HDR mode. If you want sRGB, choose that mode from the 10 presets. It has only a brightness control available. My recommended settings are below.
For HDR signals, there are five specific modes. To get the brightest possible picture, choose Peak 1300. It has a lot of impact, but for the most accurate luminance tracking, HDR is the way to go. You can read more about this on page five.
| Picture Mode | Standard | 
| Brightness 200 nits | 76 | 
| Brightness 120 nits | 41 | 
| Brightness 100 nits | 33 | 
| Brightness 80 nits | 24 | 
| Brightness 50 nits | 12 (min. 24 nits) | 
| Contrast | 50 | 
| Gamma | 2.0 | 
| Color Temp User | Red 95, Green 100, Blue 99 | 
Gaming and Hands-on
You’ll see in the upcoming tests that the GO27Q24G delivers more brightness than any other OLED in its class. But does that translate to gaming goodness? I’m going to say yes. Because it’s one of the most precise monitors I’ve ever played on. Qualifier: you’ll need to keep the frame rate above 200fps. But that’s true of any OLED, regardless of resolution. I had no problem with that thanks to a GeForce RTX 4090. And when I say precision, I mean that I could pretty much not miss. The firing accuracy I enjoyed made me a bit overconfident, to the point where I was wading into hordes of enemies rather than taking my time picking them off one by one. I can’t promise that the GO27Q24G will make you a better player, but it is an absolute weapon. Pro competitors will surely want to give it an audition.
Picture quality was superb thanks to its high brightness. I tried both HDR and Peak 1300 modes for Doom Eternal and picked the latter as my favorite. You can see the technical differences between them in my test on page five. Quick spoiler: Peak 1300 is much brighter, almost double, in fact. And it has tremendous impact. The GO27Q24G has a bit less color volume than Quantum Dot or Tandem OLED monitors, but its extra light output makes up for that.
I noted from the get-go that the GO27Q24G has premium build quality. Though many OLEDs share this trait, I was particularly impressed with the all-metal stand. It’s sleek and slender, but supremely solid. The panel’s fulcrum is equally tight, which creates a monolithic package. And with nothing facing the viewer besides the screen, there are no distracting elements; no lights, no logos, no plastic trim, no nothing. I was amazed when I learned that the price is only $350.
If you want to make the GO27Q24G an everyday screen, it is more than up to the task. I recommend calibration, but it’s a simple matter. Just plug in my numbers above to see the same image I did. It has variable brightness, which you’ll find in the OLED Care menu. Choose Low for constant brightness and High for maximum contrast and impact. For those who need sRGB, that option is in the picture mode list. With 109ppi, there is enough pixel density to show a finely detailed and smooth image for things like Photoshop or YouTube.
Takeaway: The GO27Q24G is one of the best values I’ve seen in the OLED category. It offers all the performance of more expensive monitors while outpacing them in brightness. It also has the smoothness and response of the best gaming panels I’ve experienced. There are a few peripheral bits missing, like USB ports, LEDs, and internal speakers. But for the money, there isn’t a better 27-inch QHD OLED.

Christian Eberle is a Contributing Editor for Tom's Hardware US. He's a veteran reviewer of A/V equipment, specializing in monitors. Christian began his obsession with tech when he built his first PC in 1991, a 286 running DOS 3.0 at a blazing 12MHz. In 2006, he undertook training from the Imaging Science Foundation in video calibration and testing and thus started a passion for precise imaging that persists to this day. He is also a professional musician with a degree from the New England Conservatory as a classical bassoonist which he used to good effect as a performer with the West Point Army Band from 1987 to 2013. He enjoys watching movies and listening to high-end audio in his custom-built home theater and can be seen riding trails near his home on a race-ready ICE VTX recumbent trike. Christian enjoys the endless summer in Florida where he lives with his wife and Chihuahua and plays with orchestras around the state.

articles.title: Nintendo 3DS : cette application inattendue lui permet de faire tourner vos jeux PC récents
articles.text:
Six ans après l’arrêt de sa production, la Nintendo New 3DS trouve une seconde jeunesse grâce à Kasumi. Ce client non officiel permet de jouer à des titres PC récents via GeForce Now ou de diffuser les jeux de son propre ordinateur avec Steam Link.
Nintendo a cessé de produire la 3DS en septembre 2020, mais certains développeurs refusent visiblement de la laisser prendre la poussière. Avec Kasumi, publié sur GitHub par p0mpurin, une New 3DS modifiée peut désormais servir d’écran et de manette pour des jeux exécutés à distance.
La console ne fait évidemment pas tourner ces titres elle-même. GeForce Now s’occupe des calculs dans le cloud, puis lui envoie l’image et le son tandis que Kasumi transmet les commandes. L’application exploite au passage toute la largeur de l’écran supérieur, qui affiche une définition de 800 points par 240, soit 400×240 pixels par œil lorsque la 3D est utilisée.
Une New 3DS modifiée suffit pour se lancer
Le fonctionnement reprend celui de n’importe quel service de cloud gaming. L’utilisateur choisit un jeu compatible qu’il possède notamment sur Steam, Epic Games Store ou Ubisoft Connect, puis celui-ci est exécuté sur les serveurs de NVIDIA.
La connexion au compte passe par un code affiché sur la console et saisi depuis un téléphone ou un ordinateur. Aucun mot de passe NVIDIA ne transite ainsi directement par la 3DS.
Kasumi reste toutefois un homebrew et nécessite donc une console modifiée, par exemple avec Luma3DS. La 3DS originale n’est pas compatible. Il faut une New 3DS, une New 3DS XL ou une New 2DS XL, dont la puce de décodage vidéo est indispensable au fonctionnement de l’application.
Le projet s’appuie sur OpenNOW, déjà adapté à la Switch et à la PS Vita. Gratuit et open source, Kasumi est un projet indépendant, développé sans affiliation avec Nintendo ou NVIDIA.
GeForce Now compressé dans seulement 1,3 Mbit/s
Les limites matérielles de la console ont obligé son développeur à faire quelques compromis plutôt malins. Par défaut, Kasumi reçoit un flux en 960×540 points à 30 images par seconde, pour un débit avoisinant seulement 1,3 Mbit/s.
La New 3DS n’est de toute façon pas taillée pour beaucoup plus. Son décodeur vidéo fonctionne idéalement à 30 images par seconde et son Wi-Fi 2,4 GHz commence à perdre des paquets lorsque le débit grimpe. Kasumi compense en redemandant ceux qui manquent. Un mode 60 images par seconde existe également en bêta, mais réclame une connexion nettement plus stable.
La différence avec l’application officielle de GeForce Now est spectaculaire. NVIDIA recommande au minimum 15 Mbits/s pour jouer en 720p à 60 images par seconde, soit plus de dix fois le débit utilisé ici.
Le développeur mesure également entre 60 et 80 millisecondes de latence réseau. La valeur reste suffisante à ses yeux pour les RPG, les jeux d’aventure et une bonne partie des titres d’action, mais elle devient beaucoup plus gênante dans un FPS compétitif. Kasumi conserve en outre une ou deux images en tampon afin de limiter les à-coups du Wi-Fi.
Même l’offre gratuite de GeForce Now fait l’affaire
Pas besoin de payer GeForce Now Ultimate pour en profiter. L’offre gratuite fonctionne avec Kasumi, au prix de ses files d’attente et de ses sessions limitées à une heure. La console peut même être refermée pendant l’attente et prévient son propriétaire avec sa LED et un signal sonore lorsque la session est prête.
Si les très hautes définitions proposées par NVIDIA dépassent largement les capacités de l’écran supérieur (qui compte 800×240 points), les offres payantes conservent toutefois un intérêt pour leurs files d’attente plus courtes et leurs sessions de jeu plus longues.
Les commandes ont été adaptées aux particularités de la machine. L’écran tactile remplace notamment les boutons L3, R3 et PS absents de la 3DS, le gyroscope peut être utilisé pour viser et la disposition des touches peut être réglée jeu par jeu. Les titres conçus uniquement pour le clavier et la souris restent plus délicats, même si Steam Input peut parfois contourner le problème.
Kasumi prend également en charge Steam Link pour diffuser les jeux de son propre ordinateur sur le réseau local vers une New 3DS. Une intégration de Xbox Cloud Gaming a aussi été ajoutée, mais elle est actuellement suspendue, le temps de résoudre des problèmes de compatibilité vidéo. Bref, si vous avez encore l’une de ces consoles portables Nintendo au fond de l'un de vos tiroirs, ça vaut clairement le coup de la ramener à la vie.

articles.title: Tonbo Imaging’s Rs 852 Cr IPO offers investor exit
articles.text:
Tonbo Imaging’s Rs 852 Cr IPO offers investor exit
The Rs 852 crore all-offer-for-sale IPO comes as falling exports, weaker profits and negative operating cash flow temper growth prospects backed by a sizeable order book.
Tonbo Imaging India will open its Rs 852 crore initial public offering (IPO) on October 15, with a price band of Rs 665-700 per share. The issue comprises 1.22 crore existing shares offered for sale by promoters and investors, with no fresh issue.
At the upper end, the company is valued at approximately Rs 4,010 crore, or about 79 times FY26 profit after tax. The offer closes on October 19, with listing expected on October 23.
The IPO is primarily an exit opportunity for existing shareholders. The largest sellers are CEAQ Technologies Private Limited, offering 49.98 lakh shares, and CEAQ Technologies Pte. Ltd., offering 41.55 lakh shares. Together, they account for about 75.2% of the shares on offer.
Promoters Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar, Ankit Kumar and Cecilia D’Souza will sell 11.50 lakh, 5.80 lakh and 2.30 lakh shares, respectively. Other sellers include Vinimaya Advisory LLP, Timothy Guy Mitchell, Artiman Partners and other individual and institutional investors.
The selling reflects an already investor-heavy ownership structure. Before the offer, CEAQ Singapore held 25.47%, CEAQ India 8.73% and HBL Engineering 14.25%. The three promoters collectively held 17.43%. Other notable shareholders included Florintree Flowtech LLP with 5.17%, Amansa Investments with 4.25% and Yali Deeptech Fund I with 4.19%.
If all offered shares are sold, the promoters’ combined stake would fall to approximately 14.01%, CEAQ India would exit its disclosed holding and CEAQ Singapore would retain about 18.22%. These are calculations based on the disclosed holdings and proposed sale quantities, rather than final post-offer figures.
The Bengaluru-based company, incorporated in 2003, develops thermal imaging equipment, tactical sights and integrated defence sensor platforms. Its prospects are supported by demand for indigenous defence technology, but its financial performance remains sensitive to large contracts and delivery schedules.
Revenue from operations increased 9.55% to Rs 469.08 crore in FY25 before falling 22.69% to Rs 362.65 crore in FY26.
The RHP attributes the fall to “delays in the execution of certain international orders due to disruptions arising from the West Asia conflict, as well as the deferment of certain anticipated orders from Fiscal 2026 to Fiscal 2027.”
The firm’s export sales fell 93.42% to Rs 20.21 crore, accounting for 5.57% of operating revenue, against Rs 307.34 crore and 65.52% in FY25. Domestic sales rose 114.89% to Rs 337.47 crore, or 93.06% of operating revenue, but could not offset the export decline.
Profit after tax fell 30.07% to Rs 50.88 crore in FY26, while EBITDA, or earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, declined 24.77% to Rs 104.62 crore. The EBITDA margin eased to 28.85% from 29.65%.
The company’s operating cash flow was negative at Rs 63.22 crore in FY26, following an outflow of Rs 136.12 crore in FY25. The earlier outflow partly reflected payments for intellectual property acquired from CEAQ Singapore, while rising inventory and order timing have affected working capital.
The five largest customers accounted for 53.03% of FY26 revenue, leaving the company exposed to delays or changes in a relatively small number of contracts.
India’s defence exports reached Rs 38,424 crore in FY26, up 62.66% year-on-year, according to the Ministry of Defence. Paras Defence expected its exports to roughly double in FY27 amid heightened geopolitical tensions. These trends may support demand for specialised defence electronics.
Tonbo’s confirmed order book stood at Rs 314.24 crore at June 2026, with another Rs 118.15 crore of orders received between July and September.

articles.title: Moto Watch Ultra, análisis: tan bueno para ir al gimnasio como para ir a una boda
articles.text:
He probado el reloj inteligente más ambicioso de Motorola hasta la fecha, el Moto Watch Ultra. No es un smartwatch de alta gama como tal. No al menos si buscamos lo mejor de lo mejor en cuanto a seguimiento deportivo y de salud. Sin embargo, no viene cojo de esas funciones precisamente. Además, viene con un diseño híbrido entre lo deportivo y elegante que, ya te adelanto, le sienta muy bien en distintas situaciones.
Índice de Contenidos (7)
✅ Cómpralo sí...
- Buscas un buen híbrido entre reloj deportivo y elegante.
- Haces deporte a nivel aficionado y quieres ir realizando un seguimiento.
- Te interesan aspectos "básicos" de salud como las pulsaciones o la monitorización del sueño.
❌ No lo compres si…
- Buscas un reloj que te dure días y días sin pasar por el cargador.
- Quieres tener el reloj más completo en cuanto a seguimiento deportivo.
- Tienes un presupuesto ajustado y solo buscas un reloj que mida los pasos y poco más.
Lo esencial en 30 segundos
El Moto Watch Ultra es un reloj que viene impulsado por Wear OS 6, el último sistema operativo de Google para relojes inteligentes. Su pantalla pOLED de 1,5 pulgadas y su caja de acero inoxidable arrojan un reloj que vive a caballo entre lo deportivo y lo elegante, a lo cual ayudan también los dos estilos de correa con los que se vende.
En el apartado de salud y deporte, integra sensores de frecuencia cardíaca y medición de oxígeno en sangre. La colaboración con Polar añade funciones de entrenamiento, sueño y recuperación. También tiene sensor NFC, por lo que sirve incluso para realizar pagos con Google Pay.
8,1
A favor
- Diseño versátil para deporte o vestir elegante.
- Wear OS 6 se integra perfectamente.
- Buen compendio de funciones de seguimiento deportivo.
En contra
- La batería, en el mejor de los casos, dura apenas dos días.
- Se echan en falta más sensores específicos de salud.
- El soporte a nivel de software es mejorable (solo dos actualizaciones garantizadas)
Moto Watch Ultra con correas de reloj | Pantone Black Beauty
Nuestra experiencia con el Moto Watch Ultra
Diseño prémium. No será el reloj inteligente de mayor gama, pero el Moto Watch Ultra se siente premium desde el momento en que lo sacamos de la caja. Está fabricado en acero inoxidable y no pesa demasiado. Cierto es que su esfera no es pequeña precisamente, pero incluso sin tener una gran muñeca (como es mi caso) sienta bien y se siente cómodo de llevar. A su derecha, el botón principal y la corona.
¿Look elegante o look deportivo? De serie, el Moto Watch Ultra viene con dos estilos de correa distintos para cada momento, siendo una de ellas deportiva, fabricada en silicona y pensada para acompañarnos cuando hacemos deporte. Por otro lado, cuenta con una correa de cuero sintético que es más adecuada para vestir de manera formal. Con ambas me he sentido cómodo en sus respectivos contextos.
La única pega es que cambiar las correas no es tan rápido como uno esperaría. No hay ningún sistema de sujeción imantado o algo similar que permita cambiarlas con facilidad, sino que se fía todo al clásico sistema de correas de un reloj analógico.
Pantalla a la altura. Este es sin duda uno de los apartados que más he disfrutado de este reloj. Tiene un buen tamaño y, sobre todo, se ve bien en exteriores. Responde bien al tacto y tiene una muy buena calibración de colores, ya sea para ver simplemente la hora o incluso alguna foto que tengamos guardada en Google Fotos (aunque no, no es el mejor dispositivo para quedarse a ver fotos teniendo en cuenta su tamaño).
El añadido del Always On Display es otro puntazo a favor de la pantalla. Es verdad que tiende a consumir algo más de batería, pero se compensa con que el refresco se queda a 1 Hz cuando no estamos usando el reloj. Y eso de que esté siempre activa viene fenomenal para ver la hora o algún dato de la esfera sin tener siquiera que girar la muñeca.
Este sistema operativo siempre es un acierto. Wear OS 6 hace que sienta que estoy ante un smartwatch completo y no simplemente un reloj que se comunica con el móvil. Es posible instalar aplicaciones, responder mensajes, utilizar Google Maps, pagar y hacer muchas cosas directamente desde la muñeca. La interfaz me ha resultado bastante intuitiva y no he necesitado demasiado tiempo para acostumbrarme a ella.
Lo que menos me convence es que está precisamente en el futuro del reloj. Motorola promete dos actualizaciones de Wear OS, una cifra que me parece algo justa para un producto que se presenta como una opción prémium. Ahora funciona bien y no tengo ninguna queja importante con Wear OS 6. Espero que eso siga siendo así en el futuro.
Rápido y sin tirones. En el uso diario, el Moto Watch Ultra me ha transmitido muy buenas sensaciones. Las aplicaciones se abren rápido, los menús responden bien y no he tenido que esperar demasiado a que el reloj haga algo. A ello ayuda un procesador de última generación pensado para smartwatch como es el Snapdragon W5+ Gen 1.
Compañero de fatigas (literalmente). La colaboración de Motorola con Polar para el apartado deportivo ha sido un acierto. No es que sea yo un gymbro que esté empadronado en el gimnasio, pero sí acudo cada tarde y el Moto Watch Ultra ha sido mi compañero de batallas, cumpliendo de lleno en lo que uno espera de un reloj de este tipo.
Durante los entrenamientos (tiene varios prestablecidos) he podido ir consultando las métricas de un vistazo y obtener completos resúmenes al acabar, los cuales también se quedan registrados en el móvil. A poco que te interese ponerte en forma, ir viendo esa evolución con un reloj de este tipo es siempre positivo.
Se corona este apartado con un seguimiento de salud bastante completo, que permite consultar desde la frecuencia cardíaca y la saturación de oxígeno hasta el sueño y la recuperación. Eso sí, por sacar una pega, me hubiese gustado que incorporase algo más como el electrocardiograma de una derivación. Pero tampoco es que sea eso algo fundamental.
No tengas lejos el cargador. Aquí es donde más he tenido que rebajar mis expectativas, ya que no es este uno de esos relojes que te de para olvidarte durante una semana del cargador. Tener todas las métricas de salud en tiempo real acarrea que la batería vaya cayendo y haya que pasar por el cargador cada dos días como mucho (cuando he ido al gimnasio, cada día y medio).
Lo bueno es que carga bastante rápido, con alrededor de un 60% de carga en un cuarto de hora. Esto ha sido mi salvavidas en ocasiones en las que he tenido que salir de casa y me he olvidado de cargarlo, ya que con un simple chute ya me ha dado para unas cuantas horas.
Ficha técnica del Moto Watch Ultra
|  | MOTO WATCH ULTRA | 
|---|---|
| DIMENSIONES Y PESO | 4,23 x 1,21 cm 51 gramos | 
| PANTALLA | pOLED de 1,50" Resolución de 466 x 466p Tasa de refresco variable de 1 a 60 Hz Brillo de hasta 2.700 nits Corning Gorilla Glass 3 | 
| PROCESADOR | Qualcomm Snapdragon W5+ Gen 1 | 
| MEMORIA | 2 GB | 
| ALMACENAMIENTO | 32 GB | 
| SISTEMA OPERATIVO | Wear OS 6 | 
| COMPATIBILIDAD | Android 12 o superior | 
| SALUD | Frecuencia cardíaca SpO2 Monitorización del sueño Monitorización de actividad deportivo | 
| SENSORES | PPG Acelerómetro Giroscopio Brújula Barómetro Sensor de luz ambiental | 
| RESISTENCIA | IP68 + 5 ATM | 
| BATERÍA | 550 mAh | 
| CONECTIVIDAD | LTE (eSIM) Bluetooth 5.3 WiFi 802.11/a/b/g/n/c NFC | 
| MATERIALES | Acero inoxidable | 
| PRECIO | 429 euros | 
Moto Watch Ultra, la opinión de Xataka
El Moto Watch Ultra no es perfecto. La autonomía es, a mi juicio, su mayor punto débil, así como tampoco es el más completo en cuanto a funciones de salud avanzadas. Son dos aspectos que conviene tener en cuenta antes de apostar por él, especialmente si buscamos un reloj deportivo especializado o uno que nos permita olvidarnos del cargador durante días.
Sin embargo, a nivel general, es un reloj que me ha dejado un buen sabor de boca. Me ha gustado ese equilibrio entre reloj deportivo y elegante porque no desentona en ninguna ocasión. Wear OS 6 y la asociación con Polar son los otros dos elementos a destacar positivamente de este reloj.
¿Te lo recomiendo?
No tengo una recomendación única que sirva para todo el mundo. El Moto Watch Ultra tiene mucho sentido si buscas un reloj que combine funciones inteligentes, diseño, seguimiento de salud y deporte, aunque sin llegar a funciones avanzadas de un reloj deportivo especializado. También si tienes un móvil Android y quieres aprovechar al máximo la integración de Wear OS.
Pero si tienes un iPhone, no será compatible y obviamente no te lo puedo recomendar. Tampoco si buscas un reloj que dure días y días con batería, en cuyo caso hay opciones con menores prestaciones que te servirán y que, quizás, te hagan incluso ahorrar dinero.

articles.title: Epic Games reportedly pivoting to "AI first" game development model
articles.text:
Epic Games is shifting to an “AI first” development strategy for its collaboration with the Walt Disney Company, letting AI models write all the code and guide all the artwork for an upcoming shooter. That’s according to a Bloomberg report, which cites unnamed people familiar with the project who commented on the significant pivot in internal development at the Unreal Engine maker.
Human developers will be tasked with managing and guiding code and art assets generated by models such as Anthropic’s Claude, according to internal Epic employee messages viewed by Bloomberg. That means “no more hand-written code” and art assets “generated with full AI workflows,” according to the report.
The $1.5 billion collaboration between Epic and Disney, announced in early 2024, was slated to release a Marvel- and Star Wars-themed shooter in March 2027. That project has now been delayed indefinitely amid the AI-related shakeup and understaffed, slower-than-expected development thus far, according to the report.
“We’re embracing AI-accelerated development, led by Epic developers who are the visionaries and creative drivers for everything we do,” an Epic spokesperson said in a statement.
“We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration,” Epic CEO Tim Sweeney wrote on social media shortly after the Bloomberg story was posted. “The aim isn’t to do the same stuff with fewer people, but to enable everyone here to build MORE and BETTER stuff, and to bring the benefits to all teams using Unreal.”

articles.title: I tried ChatGPT’s new virtual fitting room — it nailed the outfits, but couldn't resist changing my body
articles.text:
I tried ChatGPT’s new virtual fitting room — it got the clothes right, but changing my body defeats the point
ChatGPT’s virtual try-on feature is surprisingly convincing, but there’s a catch
ChatGPT has been pushing further into becoming a shopping assistant for a while now. You can ask it for product recommendations and it’ll find specific items, show you images, prices and links to buy them. Sometimes it’ll even add contextual details from what it knows about you, like your color preferences or budget, to help personalize its recommendations even more.
I've been testing it over the past few months and I find it a strange way to shop. OpenAI has tried to make the experience as slick as possible, but I still like visiting a retailer’s website, seeing more photos, browsing the rest of the range and checking reviews and product details before I buy anything.
But its latest shopping feature is much more interesting. Because you can now virtually try on clothes within ChatGPT.
This makes a lot of sense. ChatGPT’s image generation capabilities have become much more realistic since its Images 2.5 update. With more natural lighting, convincing textures and a better understanding of how objects should look in the real world. Apply that to shopping and suddenly the idea of virtually trying on a jacket or dress becomes much more appealing.
To use the feature you’ll need to upload a photo of yourself and then look for something you want to buy, with a Try On button now appearing alongside supported shopping results. Alternatively, you can give ChatGPT an image of an item and ask it to show you what you’d look like wearing it.
Now, this sort of virtual try-on technology itself is nothing new. We’ve seen versions of it for clothes, glasses and makeup for years. But I wanted to know whether ChatGPT's newer and more realistic image generation could make the experience genuinely useful.
I find shopping in person pretty overwhelming sometimes. But online shopping comes with its own problems too. Colors can look different in person, textures aren't always what you expect and it's difficult to know whether something that looks great on a model will work on you.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
So I decided to put ChatGPT's virtual fitting room to the test.
Trying it on for size
I started with a full body photo of myself taken while I was out shopping and used that as the photo I uploaded after I clicked the Try On button.
I’d seen examples of ChatGPT recreating the original surroundings in the photo when generating try-on images for other people but that wasn't my experience. Despite trying several different items, it consistently placed me against a fairly plain studio-style background.
But I actually preferred that because it meant there was less visual noise and it made it much easier to concentrate on the clothes.
I started by asking ChatGPT to help me find suede jackets. It surfaced several options currently available to buy on the high street and I virtually tried on the ones I liked.
After it surfaced a jacket available in a shop near me, I decided to go and find out in the wild. That meant I could compare ChatGPT’s interpretation with what happened when I actually put the jacket on. And I was surprised by how close it was.
I deliberately picked an oversized jacket because I thought that would make a good test. It’s relatively easy to paste a fitted garment onto somebody. But understanding that something is supposed to hang loosely seemed like a bigger challenge.
I didn't recreate the exact pose or camera angle from the AI-generated image, so this wasn't a perfectly controlled comparison. But ChatGPT did a surprisingly good job of guessing where the jacket sat on my body, its oversized shape and the way the material fell.
It wasn't perfect, but as a way of answering the question “roughly what might this look like on me?”, I can imagine it being helpful. Even just as the first step in the buying process.
Changing things up
After trying a few more suede jackets, I wanted to see how well the feature worked when I moved away from the fairly straightforward jeans and jacket combination.
So I asked ChatGPT to find me dresses I could wear to a formal event and started virtually trying those on too.
Again, the results were convincing enough that I could imagine using them to narrow down a long list of potential purchases. One thing I found particularly useful was color. Seeing a garment against my own skin and hair gave me a much better sense of whether I actually liked a shade than seeing it on a retailer's model.
Then I decided to take things one step further. I told ChatGPT to find me something extravagant that I could wear to a 1920s-style ball and tried on one of the more dramatic options.
Even here, the result was remarkably convincing at first glance. The clothing looked like clothing rather than something crudely pasted onto my body, and ChatGPT handled the radically different silhouette surprisingly well.
But by this point I'd also noticed something else sort of awkward was going on. The woman in these pictures wasn't quite shaped like me.
ChatGPT gave me a makeover
The full-body photograph I uploaded was an accurate representation of my proportions. Yet across the generated images, ChatGPT seemed to subtly change them. I looked taller noticeably and more statuesque. My torso appeared slightly shorter and my legs were longer.
You might think that's hardly something to complain about. But that's a huge problem when the entire purpose of the feature is to show me what clothes will actually look like on my body.
We know that generative AI has a tendency to beautify people. I’m convinced this is one of the reasons people make AI images of themselves, because it makes everyone look a little more conventionally attractive. But in a virtual fitting room accuracy matters far more than flattery.
If a dress looks fantastic because the AI has subtly changed your proportions, that's potentially no more useful than looking at the dress on a model in the first place.
Should you use ChatGPT’s try-on feature?
Maybe. I went into this experiment pretty skeptical. I've tried enough AI image tools to know that "realistic" can fall apart very quickly when you look closely, and virtual try-on technology has been around long enough that simply putting digital clothes onto a photograph isn't particularly impressive anymore.
But ChatGPT did do something useful. For me, its biggest strength was color. It might have changed my body, but it kept my skin tone and the color of my hair identical.
Which meant that being able to quickly see several different shades against something approximating my own appearance could genuinely help me decide between them. I was also impressed by its ability to communicate the overall silhouette and feel of an item, particularly with the oversized jacket I was able to compare with the real thing.
So sure, it could take some of the stress out of shopping. Rather than ordering five jackets and hoping one works, I can imagine using virtual try-on to narrow those five down to two.
But I'd still be cautious about treating the resulting images as anything like an accurate prediction of exactly how something will fit. Fabric weight, sizing, movement and all the strange little differences between our bodies are difficult to judge from a generated image. And, based on my experiment, ChatGPT may give you slightly more conventionally flattering proportions in the process.

Becca is a contributor to TechRadar, a freelance journalist and author. She’s been writing about consumer tech and popular science for more than ten years, covering all kinds of topics, including why robots have eyes and whether we’ll experience the overview effect one day. She’s particularly interested in VR/AR, wearables, digital health, space tech and chatting to experts and academics about the future. She’s contributed to TechRadar, T3, Wired, New Scientist, The Guardian, Inverse and many more. Her first book, Screen Time, came out in January 2021 with Bonnier Books. She loves science-fiction, brutalist architecture, and spending too much time floating through space in virtual reality.

articles.title: LineageOS 24 apporte Android 17 aux vieux smartphones et s'installe en quelques clics — Frandroid
articles.text:
Votre vieux smartphone ne reçoit plus de mises à jour de son fabricant ? LineageOS a publié sa version 24.0 le 11 octobre, et elle repose sur Android 17, que Google a sorti en juin. Ces premières versions intègrent les correctifs de sécurité publiés entre août 2025 et octobre 2026. Un téléphone abandonné depuis des années peut donc rattraper son retard sur les failles connues.
LineageOS est une ROM personnalisée, c’est-à-dire une version d’Android qu’on installe soi-même à la place de celle du fabricant, sans les services de Google. Le projet a pris la suite de CyanogenMod, une ROM très populaire au début des années 2010. Il fêtera ses dix ans le 24 décembre 2026.
Cette fois, l’équipe a nettement pris de l’avance sur ses cycles précédents. Elle y arrive alors que Google verrouille de plus en plus le code source d’Android, sur lequel tout le projet repose.
Des applications maison enfin soignées
LineageOS livre aussi ses propres applications. Presque toutes adoptent Material Design 3 Expressive, le dernier style graphique de Google, plus coloré et plus animé. Même l’assistant du premier démarrage et l’outil de mise à jour y passent.
La grosse nouveauté s’appelle Canvas. Cet éditeur d’images intégré gère le recadrage, la balance des blancs et les filtres. Il complète la galerie Glimpse et l’appareil photo Aperture, ce qui évite d’installer une application tierce pour une retouche rapide.
Twelve, le lecteur de musique arrivé avec LineageOS 22, charge plus vite les grosses bibliothèques. Il gère aussi mieux Jellyfin, un logiciel libre qui sert à héberger sa propre médiathèque chez soi. Et il gagne un onglet dédié aux morceaux les plus écoutés.
Le navigateur Jelly sait désormais ajouter des PWA (des sites web qui se comportent comme des applications) via un raccourci. Pratique pour éviter les boutiques d’applications tierces.
Surtout, l’Updater, l’outil de mise à jour, installe désormais les nouvelles versions en streaming par défaut sur les téléphones à partitions A/B. Ces appareils gardent deux copies du système : la mise à jour s’écrit sur l’une pendant qu’on utilise l’autre, comme sur les Pixel. L’installation va donc nettement plus vite.
Une installation depuis le navigateur, mais pas sur tous les téléphones
Jusqu’ici, installer LineageOS demandait de passer par ADB et Fastboot, les outils de Google qui pilotent un téléphone branché à un ordinateur, en tapant des commandes dans un terminal. Le projet lance des outils de flashage qui fonctionnent directement dans le navigateur. Ils s’appuient sur WebUSB, une technologie qui permet à une page web de dialoguer avec un appareil branché en USB.
Concrètement, on branche le téléphone, on ouvre flash.lineageos.org dans Chrome ou Edge (Firefox et Safari ne gèrent pas WebUSB) et on lance l’installation depuis la page. Les outils gèrent ADB et Fastboot, mais aussi Amlogic Burn, utilisé par les boîtiers TV à puce Amlogic, et Odin, le protocole maison de Samsung.
On vous parlait déjà de cette promesse de se passer des lignes de commande. Ces outils restent pourtant facultatifs : les guides du wiki, appareil par appareil, restent la méthode officielle.
Les premières versions concernent une sélection de modèles, du Pixel 4, sorti en 2019, à toute la gamme Pixel 10, en passant par le OnePlus 13 et le Fairphone 5. D’autres arriveront dans les semaines à venir. Aucun calendrier par marque n’existe, car chaque modèle dépend d’un mainteneur bénévole, qui publie sa version quand elle respecte les règles du projet.
Par contre, les smartphones dont le noyau Linux est resté en version 4.4 ou 4.9 n’auront pas droit à Android 17. Le noyau est la couche du système qui dialogue avec le matériel, et les fabricants le figent en général au lancement du téléphone. Ces deux versions datent de 2016. LineageOS n’accepte plus de versions officielles 23.2 ou 24.0 pour ces appareils, qui restent sur LineageOS 22.2, basé sur Android 15, avec des correctifs de sécurité chaque mois.
Avant de vous lancer, sachez que les applications qui dépendent des services de Google peuvent ne plus fonctionner. Pour savoir quelle branche votre téléphone peut recevoir, consultez sa page sur le site du projet, qui donne aussi la marche à suivre.

articles.title: Nanya Reports Results for Q3 2026, Revenue Increases 61.9%
articles.text:
Monday, October 12th 2026
Nanya Reports Results for Q3 2026, Revenue Increases 61.9%
Nanya Technology Corporation ("NTC", TWSE: 2408), today announced its results of operations for the third quarter, ended September 30, 2026. NTC's quarterly sales revenue was NT$133,649 million, a 61.9 percent increase compared to that in the second quarter of 2026. In the third quarter of 2026, average selling prices (ASP) increased by more than sixty percent and bit shipment decreased by mid-single digit percent quarter over quarter.
Gross profit of the quarter was NT$114,482 million; gross margin was 85.7 percent, a 6.2 percentage points improvement from that in the previous quarter. Operating income of the quarter was NT$106,894 million; operating margin was 80.0 percent; a 6.3 percentage points improvement from that in the last quarter. Non-operating income of the quarter was NT$2,438 million. The Company had net income of NT$87,627 million, with net margin of 65.6 percent.Earnings per share (EPS) was NT$25.4 (based on weighted average outstanding shares of 3,450 million). Net income for the first three quarters of 2026 reached NT$163,877 million, with EPS of NT$49.28 (based on weighted average outstanding shares of 3,325 million). Book value per share was NT$118.99 at the quarter end (based on outstanding shares of 3,450 million). All numbers are unaudited.
NTC's AI infrastructure-related business, which includes servers, networking, storage and system management solutions, currently accounts for more than 20% of total revenue. NTC's new fab is scheduled for equipment move-in in the first quarter of 2027, with capacity ramping to 30,000 wafer starts per month by the end of 2028 and reach full capacity of 50,000 wafer starts per month by the end of 2030. Meanwhile, NTC plans a 3D wafer packaging and testing fab at Pingtung Science Park, incorporating advanced 3D IC technologies, including through silicon vias (TSVs) and wafer stacking, by the end of 2028. NTC's future capacity expansion will primarily be planned in line with customers' AI projects under long-term agreements (LTAs).
The Company expects to begin customer qualification of 1C in the first quarter of 2027. The development of 1D and 1E, along with EUV, continues to progress according to schedule. NTC is committed to strengthening its position as a diversified memory solutions provider. By leveraging its manufacturing expertise, technological know-how, ongoing capacity expansion, and advanced packaging and testing capabilities, NTC aims to further deepen customer partnerships and capture new growth opportunities arising from AI-driven innovation.

articles.title: This AI startup says it can generate permit-ready blueprints in minutes | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Nearly two decades ago, a young college student wrote his final thesis about software capable of generating design documents for school buildings. Al Dram was studying architecture — following in the footsteps of his parents and grandfather — but it was technology that really intrigued him.
There was just one problem: The technology his idea required didn’t exist yet.
“Then ChatGPT came along,” said Dram, recalling when OpenAI released the generative AI chatbot that uses large language models (LLMs) in November 2022.
His old idea suddenly seemed a lot more possible. Within six months, he launched the concept of Blueprints AI, a startup that uses AI to produce code-compliant and permit-ready architectural construction blueprints in minutes from a 2D sketch or PDF.
Blueprints AI, which Dram officially incorporated in 2025 in Santa Monica with co-founder Coco Cao, was selected for the 2026 Startup Battlefield 200, a cohort of promising early-stage startups that have earned a spot to exhibit at this year’s TechCrunch Disrupt, taking place this week from October 13 to 15 in San Francisco.
During that 20-year lead-up to Blueprints AI, Dram earned his bachelor’s and master’s degrees in architecture from the University of Tehran and completed two years of PhD coursework on digital design at the European Graduate School in Switzerland. He moved to the United States and opened an architecture firm in 2018 called Drams Design-Build. Then, after obtaining a general contractor’s license, he added a construction business in 2021.
Dram should have been satisfied. He wasn’t.
“I was saying, okay, maybe I can build new projects that change people’s life in that area, but it wouldn’t be a big impact,” he said. “What makes me very excited about technology is the impact, the hours saved, the energy saved of people doing the same thing over and over and over.”
Blueprints AI will unveil a more capable second-generation version of its software at Disrupt. Dram and Cao say it will make a big impact because it takes over the repetitive drafting work that fills most of an architect’s day.
“It will make better spaces for people because now architects have the time to design,” said Dram. He said architects spend about 80% of their time on drafting and only 20% on design. “I want to flip that to be 20-80.”
Dram and Cao met at an AI conference several years ago and combined their skills to build the company. Cao, a data scientist from Hong Kong, handles sales and go-to-market strategy as chief commercial officer.
The pair trained their models using eight years of approved drawing sets from Dram’s design and construction firm, which is still in business.
Its first-generation software produces architectural construction documents and costs between $3,200 and $8,500 a month, depending on the plan. Custom pricing for enterprises is also available.
The startup’s second-generation software will deliver a considerable upgrade. Customers can start with a description or sketch of a project and create blueprints for every aspect of a building at once, including architecture, structural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and interior design. Version 2 allows users to design and make changes to the project, an upgrade over the first iteration. Importantly, one design change updates the entire project and is checked against local building codes.
Early customers are already using the second version, and Dram said it will become publicly available this week. The startup is already working on a third version of its software that will add in structural analysis and electrical panel design.
The technology doesn’t replace licensed architects, according to the co-founders. Licensed professionals still review the documents and affix their seal before submitting them for permits. The judgment stays human, they say.
Blueprints AI is targeting two groups with its new software. Professional architecture, engineering, and design firms make up one group, while developers and real estate owners make up another. The startup offers its software as a subscription and may add a one-time flat-fee option for those who just want it for a single project.
To learn more about Blueprints, catch hundreds of other startups, and learn from headliners like RJ Scaringe of Rivian and Amjad Masad of Replit, join us at TechCrunch Disrupt, kicking off Tuesday in downtown San Francisco.

articles.title: Un nouveau Google TV Streamer est en préparation, avec ces 3 nouveautés
articles.text:
Lancé en août dernier pour remplacer le Chromecast 4K, le boîtier de Google à glisser sous la TV pourrait déjà avoir un successeur dans les cartons. Cette nouvelle génération conserverait le même format que le Google TV Streamer actuel, tout en affichant un design légèrement plus étroit, entre autres nouveautés.
Vers plus de commandes vocales et une détection de présence
La grande nouveauté de ce modèle résiderait dans l’intégration directe de microphones sur le châssis, équipés de découpes spécifiques pour écouter les commandes « Hey Google » sans avoir à utiliser la télécommande. Le boîtier intégrerait également une fonction de « détection de présence » capable de repérer l’arrivée de quelqu’un dans la pièce. Une technologie similaire à celle introduite par TCL sur ses téléviseurs plus tôt dans l’année, permettant d’afficher automatiquement l’économiseur d’écran Google Photos ou des informations météo dès qu’on s’approche de l’écran.
Sous le capot, Google mise évidemment sur de meilleures performances avec un processeur plus rapide et une capacité de stockage supérieure aux 32 Go actuels. La télécommande fournie recevrait, elle aussi, quelques ajustements mineurs, avec un design global inchangé, mais l’arrivée de deux boutons de raccourci supplémentaires aux côtés des touches dédiées à YouTube et Netflix. Le bouton physique « Trouver ma télécommande » logé à l’arrière du boîtier ferait également son retour.
Une date de sortie et un prix encore flous
Aucune date de sortie officielle n’a encore filtré pour ce nouveau modèle, ce qui laisse planer le doute sur le calendrier de sortie prévu par Google. Côté tarif, ces rumeurs d’un nouveau modèle arrivent en même temps que l’augmentation de 50 % du prix du Google TV Streamer actuel aux États-Unis, qui est passé de 99,99 dollars à 149,99 dollars (il est encore à 119 € chez nous au moment d’écrire cet article). Une hausse tarifaire énorme qui rend d’autant plus énigmatique le positionnement de cette future version.
Ce nouveau boîtier multimédia de Google devra également faire face à celui d’Apple, qui préparerait de son côté une nouvelle version de son Apple TV dotée de microphones pour utiliser Siri à distance, ainsi qu’une télécommande intégrant des haut-parleurs pour la retrouver facilement en cas de perte. articles.title: El Omoda 4 quiere asaltar la gama de entrada y se ha traído detalles de Lamborghini para ser el nuevo superventas
articles.text:
Salón de París de 2026.
Este ha sido el lugar elegido por Omoda para enseñar y desvelar su próxima gran esperanza en el mercado. El Omoda 4 llega para tener, en palabras de la compañía, “un verdadero coche de acceso a la gama por primera vez”.
No, no tenemos precio confirmado (sólo se ha señalado que llegará a lo largo del primer semestre de 2027 y después del Omoda 5) pero esa frase es una declaración de intenciones. Cuando llegó, el Omoda 5 lo hizo con un precio de salida que rozaba los 28.000 euros y sin versión electrificada. Es de esperar, por tanto, que el nuevo Omoda 4 se sitúe por debajo de esa barrera.
Ficha técnica del Omoda 4
|  | Omoda 4 shs y EV | 
|---|---|
| TIPO DE CARROCERÍA. | SUV de cinco plazas | 
| MEDIDAS Y PESO. | 4,424 metros de largo, 1,863 metros de ancho, 1,570 metros de alto. 2,700 metros de distancia entre ejes. Peso no confirmado. | 
| MALETERO. | Más de 400 litros (tamaño no especificado) | 
| POTENCIA MÁXIMA. |  | 
| CONSUMO WLTP. | Pendiente de homologación. | 
| DISTINTIVO AMBIENTAL. | ECO y Cero emisiones. | 
| AYUDAS A LA CONDUCCIÓN (ADAS). | 19 ayudas ADAS a la conducción, incluido control de crucero adaptativo. Cámara de 540º. | 
| OTROS. | Software propio compatible con Android Auto y Apple CarPlay. Pantalla de 13,2 pulgadas. Cuadro de instrumentos de 8,8 pulgadas y Head-Up Display. Carga inalámbrica para el teléfono móvil de 50W. Asientos delanteros eléctricos calefactables. | 
| HÍBRIDO ELÉCTRICO. | Sí, un motor de combustión 1.5 turbo de 143 CV y dos motores eléctricos. | 
| HÍBRIDO enchufable. | No. | 
| eléctrico | Sí, motor de 218 CV y batería de 67 kWh. | 
| precio y lanzamiento | Precio por confirmar. Comercialización primer semestre de 2027. | 
Otro modelo, misma filosofía
Que el Omoda 4 sea el vehículo de acceso a la gama no quiere que decir que la compañía haya descuidado su lanzamiento. Al contrario.
Primero porque la imagen por fuera del pequeño de los Omoda guarda la línea de sus hermanos mayores. Líneas tensas que fluyen por toda la carrocería y que con la renovación del Omoda 5 ayudan a crear una familia de modelos de imagen claramente definida.
Segundo porque la percepción de calidad por dentro sigue siendo igual de buena que en los modelos que ya están en el mercado. Los ajustes, los materiales escogidos, todo da la impresión de venir de un coche de precio superior. Detalle curioso que el botón de arranque se sitúe debajo de una pieza móvil roja en la consola central al estilo Lamborghini.
A falta de poder probarlo, en Omoda prometen que el sistema de infoentretenimiento se complementa con un control por voz más inteligente y el control a distancia de algunas funciones mediante una aplicación propia en el teléfono móvil.
Esto se completará con un equipamiento muy amplio, marca de la casa. De serie, llega con asientos delanteros y volante calefactados, control de crucero adaptativo y arranque sin llave. Apple CarPlay y Android Auto son compatibles de forma inalámbrica. Además, se puede añadir cámara 360º (Omoda lo llama 540º porque muestra lo que hay bajo el suelo del coche), sistemas avanzados de aparcamiento, asientos con ajuste eléctrico y maletero eléctrico, cuero sintético en la tapicería, techo panorámico de cristal y cargador inalámbrico de 50W.
En cuanto a sus motorizaciones, Omoda apuesta por la combinación que tan buenos resultados le está dando con el Omoda 5. La versión híbrida se suma a la tecnología SHS (Super Hybrid System). En este caso con la misma combinación que con su hermano mayor: 224 CV de potencia total, 295 Nm de par motor y un consumo homologado que debería situarse en los 5,2 l/100 km.
El motor de combustión es un cuatro cilindros 1.5 turboalimentado de 143 CV que funciona generalmente como generador eléctrico. Le acompaña un motor eléctrico dedicado a impulsar las ruedas en la mayoría de las ocasiones. Por último, un segundo motor eléctrico también ayuda a generar más electricidad. Todo este conjunto, jugando con una transmisión con un embrague, permite al coche funciona en los siguientes modos:
- Modo 100% eléctrico: funcionamiento a baja velocidad (hasta 40 km/h) cuando la batería cuenta con suficiente carga. Es el motor eléctrico principal el que mueve las ruedas delanteras.
- Modo híbrido en serie: el motor térmico proporciona carga a la batería utilizando el motor secundario, mientras que la tracción es 100% eléctrica a través del motor principal. Se utiliza en escenarios de velocidad media con baja carga de batería y baja carga de acelerador.
- Modo térmico: cuando la batería está completamente cargada y se circula a media o alta velocidad con baja carga de acelerador, el motor térmico es el encargado de propulsar el vehículo.
- Modo híbrido en paralelo: cuando el conductor demanda una gran potencia, tanto el motor eléctrico principal como el motor térmico proporcionan tracción.
- Modo carga estacionaria: cuando el vehículo está arrancado, pero sin movimiento y la batería no está cargada, el motor térmico alimenta la batería de tracción a través del motor eléctrico secundario.
- Modo regeneración: en fases de frenada o sin carga de acelerador, el vehículo recupera energía para cargar la batería a través del motor eléctrico principal.
En cuanto a la opción eléctrica, el pequeño de los Omoda estará disponible con batería LFP de 67 kWh y motor de 160 kW (218 CV) y 275 Nm de par máximo. La recarga queda en 120 kW en corriente continua, prometiendo pasar del 30 al 80% de capacidad en 22 minutos. El coche, por tanto, jugará en esa delgada línea entre las opciones puramente urbanas y aquellas que admiten pequeños viajes sin dolores de cabeza. O que, si el conductor lo asume, podrá hacer largos viajes asumiendo que el tiempo será un poco superior a si lo hiciera con un vehículo de combustión.
Como decíamos, de momento no tenemos datos de precios ni fecha exacta de lanzamiento. Debería llegar en la primera mitad de 2027 y podemos especular con un precio inferior a 28.000 euros. Al menos para su versión híbrida. Eso sí, esto son, de momento, meras especulaciones.
