articles.title: GTA VI vs. Zelda Ocarina of Time: exproductor de Fortnite afirma que solo Nintendo puede desafiar a Rockstar
articles.text:
GTA VI se acerca como uno de los lanzamientos más esperados en la historia de los videojuegos, y su sola presencia en el calendario ha bastado para que buena parte de la industria reacomode sus propios estrenos. Sin embargo, Nintendo rompió con esa tendencia: mantuvo la fecha de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a solo dos semanas del debut de Rockstar.
Para Aakash Gupta, especialista en estrategia de producto y crecimiento que trabajó en Epic Games, esa decisión confirma que Nintendo es la única compañía capaz de sostener su terreno frente al fenómeno que representa GTA VI.
Por qué Nintendo no movió el lanzamiento de Zelda
Gupta comparó el panorama de estrenos con un “juego de gallina”: cuando un proyecto de la magnitud de GTA VI toma una fecha, el resto de las compañías deben elegir entre sostenerse o apartarse para no quedar eclipsadas.
Según su lectura, casi toda la industria optó por correrse del camino de Rockstar para evitar competir por la atención del público. Nintendo fue la excepción y decidió avanzar con el lanzamiento de su remake sin modificar el calendario original.
“Son la única compañía en la industria con una base de fans lo suficientemente leal para hacer esa apuesta”, afirmó Gupta.
El experto explica que la jugada tiene fundamento porque GTA VI no llegará a las consolas de Nintendo, lo que reduce la superposición directa entre ambas audiencias. A eso se suma que el público de Zelda y el de GTA no coincide del todo, lo que le da a Nintendo margen para confiar en que los usuarios de Nintendo Switch 2 responderán sin necesidad de competir cara a cara con Rockstar.
Qué reveló el sketch de Saturday Night Live sobre la rivalidad
La coincidencia de fechas entre ambos títulos llegó incluso a la televisión. Saturday Night Live dedicó un sketch a construir una supuesta rivalidad entre los dos lanzamientos, pero la reacción del público terminó por desviar el guion previsto.
De acuerdo con el análisis de Gupta, el entusiasmo que generó Zelda entre los espectadores superó lo que el propio programa parecía anticipar. Ese momento funcionó como una muestra anticipada de cómo podría comportarse el público una vez que ambos juegos estén disponibles.
Para el especialista, la respuesta del público confirma que The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time no necesita enfrentarse directamente a GTA VI para despertar un interés masivo entre los jugadores.
El margen de dos semanas antes de que GTA VI domine la conversación
La diferencia de 15 días entre ambos estrenos le otorga a Nintendo una ventana propia antes de que Rockstar concentre la atención de toda la industria. Gupta considera que ese espacio, aunque breve, puede resultar determinante para el desempeño inicial del remake.
La distancia entre ambas fechas, sostiene el especialista, permite que Zelda construya su propio momento de conversación sin verse forzado a compartir protagonismo con el lanzamiento de Rockstar.
Con ambos títulos todavía sin llegar al mercado, el análisis de Gupta plantea una pregunta abierta: si la apuesta de Nintendo por sostener la fecha original terminará confirmando la confianza que la compañía deposita en su comunidad de jugadores.
GTA 6 revela sus primeras seis emisoras de radio confirmadas para el lanzamiento
Grand Theft Auto VI contará con la oferta de emisoras de radio más amplia y variada de la franquicia, abarcando desde rock clásico hasta programas de tertulia.
Hasta el momento, Rockstar ha verificado la presencia de seis estaciones para el lanzamiento del juego, previsto para el 19 de noviembre de 2026 en PlayStation 5 y Xbox Series, aunque confirmó que se añadirán más opciones posteriormente.
Entre las emisoras confirmadas destaca la icónica Flash FM (pop), que en esta entrega estará conducida por Robyn y Alex, acompañada por Cocoteo FM (música latina como reggaetón y bachata), Back Country Radio (country alternativo con reportes del tiempo) y AfroBank FM (música afro). La lista se completa con The Chamber 106.6 para los amantes del metal y Dirty South Classics, enfocada en el rap y hip-hop regional del estado de Leonida.

articles.title: After a 10-year redemption arc, No Man's Sky is coming to the iPhone and iPad
articles.text:
Just over 10 years after its initial release, space exploration and survival crafting game No Man’s Sky is making its way to the iPhone and iPad, Apple and developer Hello Games announced today.
It will run on devices as far back as the iPhone 11 and the third-generation iPad Air. No Man’s Sky might not have the most cutting-edge AAA graphics (though they’re still strong, and they’ve come a long way since launch via updates), but the game’s uncommon method of generating galaxies of incomprehensible scale on device consistently for all players from a single-seed happening on a phone is remarkable for those of us who remember phones performing far behind consoles or desktop PCs.
This version of the game includes all of the content and systems updates to the game that have been added over the years—the expansions that famously took the game from a rocky launch reception to a widely beloved redemption story.
There are a couple of compromises, though, and it’s similar to what we saw with No Man’s Sky on the Nintendo Switch. Hello Games says the ability to build and explore player-made planetary settlements is limited to the iPhone 15 Pro and later, and multiplayer is not supported on any iOS device. “We are excited to see player feedback on iOS, and will support it appropriately based on how many folks are playing,” the company says, leaving the door open to perhaps not supporting all future content updates if the player base isn’t there to justify it.

articles.title: Votre PC Windows pourrait être privé de mise à jour en 2027, mais il y a un moyen d'éviter ça
articles.text:
À partir du 17 mai ou du 19 juin 2027 (selon la version), votre PC sous Windows pourrait ne plus pouvoir se mettre à jour. Cela concerne les machines qui n’auront pas reçu les nouveaux certificats de Windows Update. Le moyen le plus facile d’éviter cette infortune : mettre à jour votre ordinateur.
Windows Update a besoin d’un certificat pour continuer à mettre à jour votre PC Windows
Windows Update utilise des certificats numériques pour vérifier qu’un PC communique bien avec les serveurs officiels de Microsoft. Cependant, certains d’entre eux doivent expirer le 17 mai 2027 et le 19 juin 2027, comme l’a rappelé le blog de Microsoft dédié aux administrateurs réseau. Leurs remplaçants sont bien intégrés aux mises à jour mensuelles de Windows : un appareil qui reçoit les correctifs nécessaires à temps devrait donc conserver l’accès à Windows Update.
Rassurez-vous, si les certificats de votre ordinateur ne sont pas renouvelés, vous pourrez quand même l’utiliser. Mais il ne pourra plus recevoir les mises à jour de sécurité, les correctifs de fiabilité et autres mises à jours de Windows proposés via Windows Update. Plus le temps avancera, plus le risque d’être visé par une vulnérabilité nouvellement découverte augmentera. Dans le cas où Windows Update ne proposerait pas le correctif, Microsoft précise qu’il peut être téléchargé depuis le Catalogue Microsoft Update.
Votre PC est-il concerné ?
Les exigences de Microsoft ne sont pas identiques selon les versions. Pour la plupart des PC personnels, l’échéance est mise au 19 juin 2027. Quant à certains modèles pour les professionnels, la date limite est fixée au 17 mai prochain.
Pour les propriétaires d’appareils sous Windows 11 24H2, installez la mise à jour de septembre 2025. D’ailleurs pour cette version, la fin du support est fixée au… 13 octobre 2026, c’est-à-dire aujourd’hui. Enfin, si vous avez une machine sous Windows 11 25H2, aucune action n’est à faire, mais il est toujours recommandé d’installer les dernières mises à jour.
Le cas particulier de Windows 10 : comment gagner quelques mois
Si vous avez un ordinateur encore sous Windows 10 qui est toujours pris en charge, il suffit d’installer au minimum la mise à jour de sécurité de juillet 2026, ou passer à une version ultérieure. Le cas de Windows 10 est un peu particulier : son support standard prend fin le 14 octobre 2026.
Microsoft a lancé un programme ESU, pour obtenir des mises à jour étendues ; programme gratuit réservé à certaines versions de Windows 10 22H2. Il permet d’avoir des mises à jour de sécurité jusqu’au 12 octobre 2027. Il faut donc que votre ordinateur sous Windows 10 soit inscrit à ce programme pour continuer à recevoir quelques mises à jour de sécurité. Mettre à jour son ordinateur permettra donc de continuer à recevoir des correctifs de sécurité après juin 2027, mais uniquement jusqu’en octobre de l’année prochaine. Après, tout sera terminé et il faudra passer à Windows 11 impérativement pour continuer à recevoir des mises à jour.

articles.title: When one robot learns, every robot knows if they can communicate
articles.text:
When one robot learns, every robot knows if they can communicate
The fastest way to transfer robot data in 2026 is still a person walking
The robots are among us. They’re carrying passengers through the streets of San Francisco, delivering parcels over the air, and working their way across farms, factories, mines, and industrial sites.
The collision we’re now witnessing between artificial intelligence and the physical world is often described as “Physical AI” – machines capable of perceiving their surroundings, making decisions, and taking action among us in the real world. But every new machine that clocks in has a second job we rarely see. It creates data. Lots of it.
Founder and CEO of Taara.
In the US, the Federal Aviation Administration expects the commercial drone fleet to grow from approximately 966,000 aircraft at the end of 2024 to around 1.18 million by 2029. And in factories around the world, there was an estimated 4.66 million industrial robots working in 2024, while another half a million were installed during the year – more than twice the number installed a decade earlier.
Today’s autonomous machines are vastly more capable, but moving all that accumulated experience off them can still be surprisingly manual. In 2026, the fastest way to move masses of data off a machine is still a person carrying a hard drive. And as autonomous machines spread further into our cities and industries, keeping that information moving could become one of the defining infrastructure challenges of the robotics age.
Data runs both ways
Imagine what an autonomous vehicle experiences. Cameras watch the roads from multiple angles, sensors and AI measure and make sense of the surrounding environment, while on-board systems track position and performance of the vehicle itself. Decisions are made and recorded in real-time as pedestrians cross roads, traffic lights change, and thousands of other vehicles and connected technologies move and exchange data around it.
Delivery drones, agricultural machinery, warehouse robots, and autonomous industrial equipment may operate in different environments, but the logic tracks. Every journey or task leaves behind a digital trail of sensor readings, video, telemetry, diagnostics, and operational logs.
And the information doesn’t travel in only one direction. These machines may also need fresh maps, software updates, configurations, AI models, and instructions from the computing infrastructure behind them. What they experience in the physical world flows back toward data centers, while the intelligence needed for their next task travels outward.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
Multiply that exchange across millions of machines and an interesting new layer of internet traffic begins to emerge that we’re only just beginning to think about.
The direction of travel was visible as early as 2019, when a landmark university paper on 6G identified mobile robots, drones, and autonomous vehicles would drive demand for ubiquitous wireless intelligence – its vision for the 6G era included networks capable of supporting a 10,000-fold increase in traffic. The US commercial drone fleet alone is now heading toward seven figures, while industrial robots already number in the millions globally.
Perhaps most notable to casual observers, autonomous vehicles are becoming far more prevalent on the streets of our capitals and major cities. In June of this year, machines surpassed 57% of web traffic globally – the first time that bots have outnumbered humans – and they use networks in a very different way. Cloudflare predicts that non-human traffic could eventually surpass human traffic by a factor 1,000 within the next five years.
And a lesson learned by one machine needn’t remain with that machine. There’s an opportunity here that only connectivity can unlock. Google DeepMind’s Gemini Robotics 1.5 showed skills transferring “zero-shot” between physically different robots – a task taught using a two-armed Franka robot was executed by a humanoid, without any data collected on the target machine.
Sit with that implication. A person who masters a technique carries that knowledge around in their head, and when they retire, much of that experience leaves with them. A robot can potentially hand what it has learned to every other robot on the network, which means experience stops being “local” and starts becoming a shared asset across the network, compounding intelligence for the company’s moat.
The physical footprint of robots is spreading outward, but the data traffic they create remains concentrated at central locations. AI may increasingly have wheels, wings, and arms, but their intelligence and interactivity with the world remain still wholly dependent on their relationship with the nearest data center hub, and that’s a problem we now have to solve.
What’s the hold up?
When a robot arrives back at the depot and “clocks out” for a while, it presents an ideal opportunity to recharge, undergo inspection, run self-diagnostics, download updates, and get the data it needs for its next shift. This is when potentially enormous volumes of data, depending on the fleet size, need to be moved both to and from the device.
Sites that house, charge, or service machinery can therefore find themselves functioning as miniature data hubs, dealing with bursts of traffic as machines arrive and depart. And as fleets grow, so does the strain on the network connecting all these hubs. When uploading and downloading take longer than charging or maintenance, the network becomes the operational bottleneck to scale.
A new layer of connectivity
A wired network simply can’t evolve at the same speed as the mobile economy. A fleet operator might need to open a new depot in another city, place drone nests closer to customers, or connect autonomous equipment at temporary industrial sites. Extending fiber to each location would involve trenching, permitting which are often cost and time intensive.
Wireless connectivity offers a faster and more flexible approach. Links can be installed without digging or waiting for permits, allowing operators to connect new sites quickly. Links can also be redeployed or expanded as fleets grow as their physical footprint expands dynamically.
Wireless optical communication (WOC) could provide that high-capacity bridge. Using narrow beams of light, it carries fiber-like capacity through the air between two points with a clear line of sight, up to 20 Gbps across distances of up to 20 kilometers. It can be installed on existing radio masts or buildings in a matter of hours.
For autonomous fleets, that creates a way to rapidly offload telemetry and operational data, upload new maps and models, and return high-value assets to work instead of leaving them waiting at the depot.
WOC isn’t magic though. Optical links still need line of sight, and heavy fog and rain can degrade their connectivity. That’s why serious deployments pair them with an RF path and engineer them for availability rather than simply assuming it. It won’t replace fiber, but it will extend fiber’s reach to the places fiber can’t go, and it’s getting smaller, faster, and more affordable as the technology moves from mechanical to solid-state beam steering with silicon photonics. Light is the answer.
The arrival of electric vehicles taught us to look beyond the machine and consider the infrastructure behind it. Autonomous machines will require us to do the same again, but this time what needs to be replenished isn’t just the machine’s battery – it’s the machine's experience, and from it, the shared intelligence of the entire fleet.
Robots are becoming extraordinarily good at navigating the physical world. We shouldn’t leave the final mile of their learning journey to someone carrying a hard drive across a parking lot.

articles.title: Orange transforme le téléphone de ses abonnés en roue de secours quand la fibre tombe en panne
articles.text:
Orange vient de lancer Reconnexion Flash, un service de la Livebox qui bascule sur le partage de connexion d’un smartphone en cas de panne internet. Une réponse aux coupures de fibre sans boîtier, pendant que la concurrence mise sur des box de secours.
Une panne de fibre, par définition, ne prévient jamais, voilà pourquoi Orange a dévoilé ce lundi 12 octobre Reconnexion Flash. Il s'agit d'une solution de secours en cas de panne de fibre optique, solution directement intégrée à la Livebox. Le principe repose sur un smartphone présent dans le logement, dont le partage de connexion permet de remettre en ligne l’ensemble des appareils de la maison en quelques minutes. L’opérateur historique s’invite ainsi sur un terrain déjà occupé par ses concurrents, mais avec une approche sensiblement différente.
Reconnexion Flash : un QR code et la Livebox d'Orange repart
Le dispositif Reconnaissance Flash a été pensé par Orange pour les moments où l'on n'a pas envie de réfléchir. Dès qu'elle détecte une coupure, la Livebox suggère d'elle-même d'activer Reconnexion Flash et affiche un QR code sur son écran. Un coup de téléphone portable, et une page web explique pas à pas comment lancer le partage de connexion. La box s'y raccroche ensuite toute seule. En quelques minutes, la connexion est rétablie.
L'astuce est que c'est toujours la Livebox qui distribue internet dans le logement. Il n'y a donc pas besoin de reconnecter la tablette, l'enceinte ou l'aspirateur robot à un nouveau réseau, chacun reprend sa place sans qu'on y touche. Et si le propriétaire du téléphone doit s'en aller, un autre membre du foyer peut prendre le relais avec son propre appareil. Laurence Thouveny, la directrice expérience client d'Orange France, évoque ce lundi une avancée « inédite sur le marché français ».
Pour en profiter, il faut être équipé d’une Livebox S ou de la Livebox 7 Wi-Fi 7, la version sortie en 2025, et habiter en métropole, en Guyane, aux Antilles ou à La Réunion. Le smartphone qui sert de relais peut dépendre de n’importe quel opérateur, mais faites attention : tout ce que la maison consomme pendant la panne est puisé dans son forfait mobile. Une petite enveloppe de data peut très vite être entamée par quelques visioconférences, films sur Netflix ou vidéos YouTube. Les abonnés mobiles Orange et Sosh sont forcément mieux lotis, avec 200 Go supplémentaires fournis par l'opérateur en cas de panne, mais en métropole uniquement. Enfin, le téléphone fixe, qui passe par la box, reste ici hors service, tout comme les chaînes regardées depuis le décodeur TV. Pour la télévision, il faudra se rabattre sur les applications, sur un téléviseur connecté par exemple.
Bouygues, Free et SFR misent sur un boîtier de secours
Les opérateurs n'ont donc pas tous forcément la même stratégie en cas de coupure fibre. Chez Bouygues Telecom, la réponse s'appelle l'Extra Bbox, disponible depuis le 26 janvier. Ce routeur 5G autonome, ouvert aux abonnés de tous les opérateurs, coûte 12,99 euros par mois sans engagement, pour 100 Go mensuels. Il faut compter 29 euros de frais de mise en service, et autant au moment de résilier. La box diffuse son propre réseau Wi-Fi, auquel il faut connecter ses appareils, idéalement avant que la panne ne survienne.
Chez Free, un module 4G Backup branché à la Freebox bascule sur le réseau mobile quand la fibre lâche. SFR propose de son côté une box de poche 4G avec son option Internet Garanti, incluse dans l'offre Premium ou facturée 5 euros par mois, avec 30 Go mensuels en cas de panne. Dans les deux cas, il faut un équipement dédié.
La parenté la plus évidente se trouve en Espagne où, fin septembre, MásMóvil, marque de MasOrange, la coentreprise espagnole d'Orange, a lancé Mi WiFi Auxiliar, qui permet à un smartphone sous Android 16 ou plus récent de reprendre le nom et le mot de passe du Wi-Fi de la box. Il faut toutefois éteindre le routeur au préalable, et les appareils branchés en Ethernet restent à quai. La version française, elle, garde la Livebox aux commandes, sans matériel supplémentaire, puisqu'un téléphone et un peu de data suffisent.

articles.title: Das Ende von Photoshop, Word & Co.? So schlagen sich KI-generierte Software-Kopien wirklich
articles.text:
Das Ende von Photoshop, Word & Co.? So schlagen sich KI-generierte Software-Kopien wirklich
„Software is over“, erklärte der US-amerikanische Entwickler Brandon Thomas Anfang Oktober 2026 im Online-Forum Hacker News. Wie als Beleg für diese These veröffentlichte Thomas nicht weniger als KI-generierte Kopien aller wichtigen Adobe-Programme. Darunter Photoshop, Lightroom, Illustrator, Premiere und Indesign.
Alle Programme sind gratis, Open Source und wurden mithilfe von Anthropics Opus-Modellen entwickelt. Als wäre das noch nicht genug, folgten seitdem auch KI-Kopien von den Microsoft-Produkten Word, Excel und Powerpoint, sowie der Programme Autodesk AutoCAD und Avid Pro Tools.
Damit bietet Thomas‘ Artcraft-Projekt mittlerweile Klone kommerzieller Produkte an, die bei einer Vielzahl von Firmen den Arbeitsalltag bestimmen. Und zwar in Versionen für Windows, Linux und macOS. Aber können die Kopien im Alltag wirklich überzeugen?

articles.title: IndianRaga founder Sriram Emani explores identity and belonging in Jam Boy
articles.text:
IndianRaga founder Sriram Emani explores identity and belonging in Jam Boy
After building IndianRaga into a global platform for Indian performing arts, Sriram Emani is turning to filmmaking to tell nuanced South Asian stories that challenge familiar stereotypes.
Sriram Emani, the founder of IndianRaga, a global platform for Indian performing arts, has an album on Facebook showcasing all the cups he’s collected from different Starbucks outlets in New York. Each of the 74 images shows his name being misspelt.
“It’s one of the most common names on the planet. But it was still spelt as ‘Syrian’, ‘Shadam’; not a single person got it right. If you can say Schwarzenegger, Saoirse Ronan, you can say Sriram,” says Emani.
This frustrating experience, commonly faced by immigrants, planted the seeds for Jam Boy, Emani’s first film as a writer, director, co-producer and lead actor.
Jam Boy is about a model immigrant who has done everything to be chosen but has not noticed what it costs him to choose himself.
Spanning 22 minutes 22 seconds, the film has already won Best Film and Best Web Series at DC Independent Film Festival, received Special Recognition at the Boston International Film Festival, and is now travelling through a growing international festival run. It will premiere on October 13 at the International Film Festival of South Asia, Toronto, North America's largest South Asian film festival.
In 2012, Emani started IndianRaga while at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. Fourteen years later, IndiaRaga has grown into a global performing arts organisation. Its online education programme, Raga Labs Academy, teaches Carnatic vocal music, Hindustani vocal music, Bharatanatyam, and Kathak through a structured syllabus with certification at every level.
IndianRaga, headquartered in Boston, Massachusetts, also offers a Raga Fellowship that selects artists through a competitive international panel to create professionally produced collaborative performances. Its artists have performed at the United Nations General Assembly, Lincoln Centre, Jacob’s Pillow, and TEDx.
When Emani first spoke about IndianRaga, the platform was just beginning its journey of taking Indian classical arts to new audiences. Since then, several moments have marked its rise.
When Shape of You - New Age Carnatic Mix crossed a million views in less than a day, critics who had questioned the blending of classical music with pop began to reconsider. “Maybe this actually works, and maybe this is what's required,” Emani recalls.
Another defining moment was Shiva Shambho, which went on to become the world’s most-watched Bharatanatyam video online.
The pandemic pushed IndianRaga to move its fellowships, collaborations, and education programmes online. Its artists have since performed at iconic venues, including Lincoln Centre, and at the World Government Summit in Dubai, where three young dancers earned an opportunity after someone in the organising team discovered their work on YouTube.
South Asian stories on the global stage
Emani is now embracing his own identity as an actor and filmmaker, with a desire to bring South Asian stories to the global stage. He explains, “I wanted IndianRaga to stand on its own, without my name overshadowing the brand. Over time, I realised people also wanted to know the person behind it, so I’m embracing that through acting and filmmaking, telling global stories with South Asian heritage at their centre.”
Emani's foray into acting got off to a great start.
“I played the first-ever South Asian Bob Cratchit in A Christmas Carol, with 20 shows for 20,000 people. We staged Tiny Tim's funeral in the Hindu tradition, and I did some Sanskrit chanting on stage,” he says.
With Jam Boy, Emani is beginning to explore his next chapter, combining his experience of building a platform for South Asian arts with a larger ambition to bring South Asian stories into mainstream global entertainment.
The origin of Jam Boy
Jam Boy has its roots in Emani’s experiences navigating the South Asian diaspora in the United States.
He often noticed that many Indian families stayed within their communities. Children hesitated to take familiar food, such as idli-sambar, to school for fear of being told it smelled. Even accomplished professionals were reluctant to assert their cultural identity. This hesitation percolated into the performing arts space as well, he observed.
After graduating from MIT, Emani spent a year hosted by 50 families across 50 cities. It shaped his understanding of how people engage with Indian performing arts beyond the stage.
“For IndianRaga, I wanted to see what people think of Indian performing arts when they’re at their least guarded: at dinner table conversations, during a hectic morning, when college applications are coming up, and they have to submit an art supplement,” he says.
While working as a summer intern at Lincoln Centre, he found that the Indian diaspora had no idea what they needed to present about South Asian culture on stage.
“Indians are building most of the tech in North America that powers the world’s technology and leading these companies, but they are just a simple face. Nobody knows anything behind it,” he says.
Hollywood was no different, Emani realised. Actors of South Asian heritage were often restricted to comic roles rather than romantic leads, detectives, or action heroes. He understood that this stemmed from the lack of stories that captured the complexity of South Asian lives.
“The diversity, richness and texture I want to portray can only come if I write the story,” he says. That conviction gave rise to Jam Boy.
Set in a near future where immigrant workers promised freedom are secretly indentured, Jam Boy follows an Indian coder who smuggles his mother’s forbidden tamarind rice into work and discovers why the company needs him to forget home.
Emani says Jam Boy is speculative fiction that plays on the theme that the model immigrant is rewarded for being impressive. “But being impressive is not the same as being fully seen. It’s a character who’s done everything possible to be chosen, but doesn’t realise the cost of choosing himself. He’s led to believe that if he just reaches the next milestone, he can go home or get certain things. But the goalpost keeps changing, because they know model immigrants just keep working, working, working,” he elaborates.
The sci-fi element in the film also lets audiences see something that might be happening in the present but isn’t being seen, by imposing boundaries through exaggerated worlds.
Emani points out that the film is based on the real-life stories of many of his friends, some of whom have had to refuse promotions to protect their positions because of their H-1B visas, which keep them in technical roles.
There’s also a segment about food racism that Indians experience in the US, and also internal gaslighting.
“There’s a scene that resonated most with kids growing up here: the protagonist opens his pressure cooker and wants to smell the food, but he’s worried the smell will get on his shirt. So he puts on a rain poncho and comes in to work like that. Every kid from age four to 18 who has watched it says, ‘Whoa, that’s so true.’ That’s what the next generation is taking from it.”
A personal connection
The film also brings a deeply personal connection—Emani's mother plays his mother in Jam Boy. She has already featured in two IndianRaga videos that garnered over 2 million views across platforms. “On a spiritual level, it feels like an ancestral blessing to have my actual mom in my first film about my culture,” he says.
The international premiere in Toronto is a meaningful milestone for Emani as the city has a large South Asian community.
“We are waiting to get into one of the festivals in India so we can come to the country through that route first. Then I have a plan to release it online next year,” he says.
Meanwhile, the short film is opening doors to larger possibilities: a feature-length version of Jam Boy. He is now working with the Rickshaw Film Foundation’s writers’ room to revise the script while exploring a web series adaptation.
Beyond Jam Boy, Emani is developing thrillers that place South Asian protagonists in global settings. As a Trust and Storytelling Fellow at Boston University, his mission is to use storytelling devices to build trust in institutions and people.
“I’m calling my umbrella Ancestors and Algorithms. It examines what we inherit and what happens to it as the world around us changes: inheritance through migration, technology, and cultural change,” he says.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Tras ver lo bien que funciona Ambilight, me lancé a comprar un kit de monitor para jugar. Resulta que es trabajando como más uso le doy
articles.text:
Nunca había probado lo que es un Ambilight hasta que estuve en una sesión de pelis en casa de unos amigos. Tengo que reconocerlo: salí impresionado de lo bien que le sienta a una tele. En casa no tenemos planes de renovar tele o monitores para comprar un Philips, pero hay sistemas para tener estas luces en cualquier pantalla (tanto de Philips como de terceros).
Como donde más iba a aprovecharlo es en un PC, me puse a buscar un sistema para monitores y di con este kit de Philips. Ahora que llevo unas semanas con él lo tengo bastante claro: funciona muy bien a la hora de jugar, pero donde más lo uso es para trabajar. Se puede comprar ahora mismo por 139,99 euros, aunque ha estado más barato en otras ocasiones.
Philips Hue Play Kit de Tira LED Inteligente PC 24-27" + Hue Bridge
Un kit de luces que se instala muy fácil
Este kit está compuesto en esencia de dos partes. La primera, obviamente, es la tira de luces LED, que se coloca en la parte trasera del monitor. Para ello, viene una serie de pequeños soportes que se adhieren a la superficie y que cuentan con unos pequeños ganchitos para dejar colocada la tira. Eso ya me gusta por dos razones: se instala muy rápido (y fácil) y se puede quitar si quieres en algún momento. A las luces, además, se les conecta un pequeño adaptador de corriente que también se adhiere al monitor.
El kit, además, incluye un Hue Bridge. Este se conecta al WiFi de casa y nos permitirá controlar las luces de dos maneras: con el móvil o directamente con el PC. En ambos casos, lo que necesitaremos es una app llamada Hue Sync App que será la encargada de sincronizar lo que estemos viendo en pantalla con las luces. O bueno, también configurar a nuestra medida la intensidad de la luz, los patrones y más.
Y a la hora de usarlas, lo que uno puede esperar. Para jugar, basta con sincronizar con la app y elegir la intensidad de luz que deseemos. Mejora mucho la experiencia en lo que a inmersión se refiere, especialmente cuando en pantalla hay mucho color. A la hora de trabajar, coloco una luz fija con una intensidad media. Con ello, consigo llegar al final de la jornada con menos fatiga ocular, algo que se agradece enormemente.

articles.title: Ledger confirme un implant espion dans un portefeuille vendu par son propre revendeur agréé — Frandroid
articles.text:
Ledger, le fabricant français qui domine le marché des portefeuilles physiques pour cryptomonnaies, a dû admettre ce que ses clients redoutent le plus.
Dans un message publié sur X le samedi 10 octobre, son support explique que l’appareil d’une victime contenait « un implant matériel non autorisé ». Toutes les victimes connues avaient acheté leur portefeuille chez CryptoBilis, un revendeur agréé présent en Indonésie, en Malaisie et aux Philippines.
Des chercheurs qui suivent les transactions sur la blockchain estiment que 86 à 93 millions de dollars ont été volés, soit environ 77 à 83 millions d’euros, dans plus de 300 portefeuilles, d’après CoinDesk. De son côté, Ledger n’a confirmé aucun montant. La marque juge « limité » le nombre d’appareils touchés.
Ce type d’appareil sert justement à empêcher ce genre de vol. Un portefeuille physique ressemble à une clé USB et garde hors ligne les clés privées, ces codes secrets qui permettent de dépenser des cryptomonnaies. À la première mise en route, il affiche une phrase de récupération de 24 mots. Toute personne qui connaît ces mots a accès aux fonds.
Un mouchard qui passe le contrôle d’authenticité
Ledger n’a pas décrit l’implant. Mark Karpelès, l’ancien patron de Mt.Gox (la plateforme d’échange de bitcoins qui a fait faillite en 2014), a publié sur X des photos d’un Ledger Nano X démonté qui contient un composant suspect. D’après son analyse, ce composant lit les données envoyées à l’écran et transmet les 24 mots vers l’extérieur.
Et le pire est que la puce d’origine reste en place. L’appareil peut donc réussir le test d’authenticité de Ledger sans rien montrer d’anormal à l’usage. Par contre, Mark Karpelès a acheté son exemplaire chez un autre revendeur. Rien ne prouve encore que les vols liés à CryptoBilis reposent sur le même montage.
Une fois la phrase volée, l’attaquant peut vider le portefeuille au moment de son choix. Gizmodo Japon s’appuie d’ailleurs sur la société d’analyse Bitquery pour décrire une fuite simultanée de 93,2 millions de dollars (environ 83 millions d’euros), depuis 315 portefeuilles. Le nombre de victimes reste inconnu, car une même personne peut posséder plusieurs portefeuilles.
Que garantit le label « revendeur agréé » ?
CryptoBilis était pourtant le revendeur agréé de Ledger en Asie du Sud-Est. Ce statut n’a pas empêché des appareils trafiqués d’arriver chez les clients. Ledger assure de son côté que ses systèmes internes et sa vente directe n’ont pas été touchés.
Comment des appareils piégés ont-ils pu passer par ce circuit ? Personne ne le sait encore. Changpeng Zhao, cofondateur de Binance, affirme sur X que les attaquants auraient racheté le revendeur et lui auraient imposé un accord de confidentialité. Cette accusation n’a été vérifiée par personne, et CryptoBilis n’a pas répondu à CoinDesk.
CryptoBilis a suspendu ses ventes de portefeuilles jusqu’à la fin de l’enquête. Ledger a aussi rappelé à ses distributeurs qu’ils doivent s’approvisionner uniquement par les canaux officiels, et leur interdit désormais de remettre en vente les produits retournés. La marque dit revoir les contrôles imposés à ses revendeurs agréés.
Ledger a déjà connu une crise de confiance. En décembre 2020, les noms, adresses et numéros de téléphone d’environ 272 000 clients volés à sa boutique en ligne s’étaient retrouvés sur un forum. Les concurrents ne sont pas épargnés non plus. En juillet 2026, une faille dans le logiciel du Coldcard, qui génère la phrase de récupération, a permis de voler 100 à 130 millions de dollars en bitcoins (environ 89 à 116 millions d’euros).
Si vous avez acheté un Ledger chez CryptoBilis ces 90 derniers jours, la marque demande de ne pas initialiser un appareil encore neuf.
S’il est déjà en service, transférez vos fonds vers une nouvelle phrase de récupération, créée sur un appareil acheté directement chez Ledger. Méfiez-vous aussi des faux services clients : Ledger rappelle qu’il n’appelle jamais ses clients et ne demande jamais les 24 mots.
Les bons plans n’attendent pas : abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp Frandroid Bons Plans ! (zéro spam, promis, juste de super bons plans).

articles.title: AMD debuts Helion reference design for agentic AI servers with up to 32,768 Zen 6 ‘Venice’ cores — rack design ships later this year in CPU-only and all-in-one configurations [Updated]
articles.text:
AMD debuts Helion reference design for agentic AI servers with up to 32,768 Zen 6 ‘Venice’ cores — rack design ships later this year in CPU-only and all-in-one configurations [Updated]
Helios, meet Helion.
Updated 10/12/26 at 12:01pm ET: AMD originally said the Helion rack would ship in the first half of 2027, but it has revised the release date to November 2026. We've updated the headline and featured image. We also corrected an error where OpenU trays were marked as 21mm wide instead of 21 inches wide.
AMD is bringing a new reference rack-scale design to the data center ecosystem with Helion. It’s a standardized, 21-inch rack reference design that will complement the Helios rack AMD revealed at OCP Global Summit last year. This year, we have Helion, which AMD says can house up to 32,768 Zen 6 cores in a CPU-only deployment using the dense 256-core design available with the EPYC ‘Venice’ 9996.
The rack design is standardized, based on the Open Compute Project’s ORv4 specification, which is slightly wider and taller than a standard IT rack. Helion is designed to support 44 OpenU trays, which are 21 inches wide and 48mm tall, slightly larger than a standard EA1-310 tray. AMD says the reference design supports both air-cooled and direct liquid-cooled deployments.
The design is also compliant with OCP’s DC-MHS (Data Center Modular Hardware System) standard. MHS is designed to bring “interoperability between key elements of data center, edge, and enterprise infrastructure,” according to OCP.
Although AMD has renders of the design you can see in the presentation below, it won’t actually sell racks. This is a reference design that AMD is contributing to OCP, and OEMs and ODMs will actually bring that design to market. AMD didn’t share partners supporting Helion during a pre-briefing with the press. The company says CEO Lisa Su will announce partners during the lead keynote at the OCP Global Summit later today.
AMD also didn’t share deployment partners, though it suggested that Helios customers will also deploy Helion racks.
Unlike Helios, which is built for AI training and inference, Helion is a more flexible rack solution primarily focused on CPUs. In a CPU-only deployment, the design can hold up to 128 EPYC 9996 CPUs, bringing that impressive 32,768 core count per rack. This configuration would likely look something like an agentic AI sandbox system, which is then connected to an inference system.
This model for personal AI agents is in use today, both in Meta’s Muse and OpenAI Dots. Each user has a sandbox with a slice of compute from the host system, with the backbone of an inference server. Some workloads are handled on those CPU-only servers, such as building software, but the heavy-duty AI inference happens elsewhere.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Presumably, this is the model AMD is aiming at with Helion as hyperscalers build out CPU capacity on the back of agentic AI. However, the design is flexible, supporting up to 16 MI350P GPUs and 102 Tbps of networking, though at the cost of CPU capacity. This hybrid configuration is targeted at enterprises, says AMD, giving them an all-in-one rack for data management, networking, and AI usage.
AMD says the Helion rack will be available starting in the first half of 2027, likely riding the wave of Zen 6 deployments that are expected to start ramping up later this year.

articles.title: KIOXIA Introduces Direct Liquid Cooling Support for Enterprise SSDs
articles.text:
Monday, October 12th 2026
KIOXIA Introduces Direct Liquid Cooling Support for Enterprise SSDs
KIOXIA America, Inc. today announced the addition of direct liquid cooling (DLC) models to its KIOXIA CM9 Series enterprise SSD lineup to support cold-plate-enabled server designs. The new E3.S DLC models also support traditional air-cooled environments.
As AI and other high-performance enterprise environments continue to advance, direct liquid cooling is becoming increasingly important to address growing computing power demands and associated cooling requirements. In order to fulfill the growing compute demands, increased power requirements are driving the need for innovative heat dissipation solutions. DLC infrastructure can offer significant energy savings compared with conventional air cooling, while enabling more servers to be cooled per rack.Ideal for SSD Context Caching, the new KIOXIA CM9-DLC models include read-intensive (1 DWPD) and mixed-use (3 DWPD) endurance options.
Maulik Sompura, Sr. Staff Director, Product Management, SSD business unit, KIOXIA America, Inc."The rise of AI infrastructure is driving a fundamental shift in data center design toward higher power densities and advanced cooling technologies. The KIOXIA CM9-DLC Series addresses these evolving requirements by combining industry-leading enterprise SSD performance with direct liquid cooling support in the E3.S form factor. This enables customers to deploy denser, more energy-efficient AI systems while providing the performance, endurance, and capacity needed for data-intensive workloads, including emerging AI architectures that rely on large-scale memory and KV cache resources."
KIOXIA CM9-DLC Series SSD highlights include:
- PCIe 5.0, NVMe 2.0, NVMe-MI 1.2c specification compliant
- Support for OCP Datacenter NVMe SSD v2.5 specification
- Dual-port support in the E3.S SSD form factor
- Capacities up to 30.72 TB read-intensive (1 DWPD) and 25.6 TB mixed-use (3 DWPD) endurances
- Sequential performance (128 kibibytes (KiB)/QD32) of up to 14.8 GB/s read and 11 GB/s write
- Random performance (4KiB) of up to 3,400 KIOPS (QD512) and 800 KIOPS (QD32)
KIOXIA CM9 Series drives are currently sampling to select customers and will be showcased at the 2026 OCP Global Summit, taking place October 12 - 15 in San Jose, Calif.

articles.title: Spotify More Than Doubled Monthly Code Changes as AI Accelerated Development
articles.text:
Spotify has expanded its use of AI-assisted development, more than doubling monthly merged changes from approximately 8,100 to 17,000 year over year in August. The company is adapting its quality and reliability controls to handle the higher volume of software changes across its production systems.
Spotify operates nearly 3,000 production services supporting 777 million monthly active users, around 100 million concurrent clients, and 11 to 12 million backend requests per second. Its review identified issues involving content processing, fleet changes, compute capacity, and mobile application quality. The company has responded with changes to monitoring, testing, rollout safeguards, rollback capacity, capacity planning, and quality measurement.
One incident involved Spotify's content processing pipeline, which handles more than 500,000 new songs, videos, podcasts, and audiobooks each day. On June 24, a scheduled batch workload competed with new episodes, a quality improvement increased processing requirements, and a scheduling bug reduced throughput by about 10%. Episodes that normally appeared within minutes were delayed for hours. Spotify subsequently added end-to-end monitoring, fixed the scheduler, moved batch jobs to lower priority, reworked workload prioritization, and increased capacity.
Fleet automation created a different challenge. Spotify's Fleet Management system has merged more than 2.5 million automated maintenance pull requests, with most automatically merged after safety checks. The company later added Honk, a background coding agent that runs Claude using the Agent SDK in Kubernetes pods. Fleetshift handles target selection, scheduling, and progress tracking, while Honk performs code modifications and can run builds in CI. Spotify reports that a recent Java migration across its backend services took three days.
An automated dependency upgrade nevertheless passed existing checks and failed in production, according to Spotify. The company is strengthening safeguards, expanding rollback capacity, and scheduling automated changes during owning teams' working hours.
Amit Jha, a software engineer at JumpCloud, in a LinkedIn post discussing Spotify's findings, said:
More changes meant greater pressure on testing, review and observability.
Alex Beck similarly focused on the verification challenge in a LinkedIn post,
Writing code got easier. The hard part now is making sure the work is actually good before it goes live.
The findings provide context for Google's 2025 DORA research, which found that AI adoption was associated with higher software delivery throughput and product performance, while also reporting a negative relationship with delivery stability. The research identified automated testing, version control, and fast feedback loops as practices relevant to managing software delivery as AI adoption increases.
Spotify combines Fleet Management for standardized maintenance with Honk for complex code changes, while Fleetshift handles orchestration and CI provides validation. Quality and optimization work rose from 27% to 31% of merged changes, while maintenance and configuration fell from 31% to 25%. Spotify reports no corresponding increase in rework, although pull request size and code complexity are rising. Its incident review found no material direct contribution from AI-authored code, but change volume had outpaced some verification controls.

articles.title: Bill Gates prevé ciberataques con IA el próximo año: “Serán el desafío más destacable”
articles.text:
Bill Gates advirtió que el próximo año estará marcado por una multiplicación de los ciberataques impulsados por inteligencia artificial. El cofundador de Microsoft señaló que ese riesgo, y no la posibilidad de que la tecnología se torne “incontrolable”, representa la amenaza inmediata más urgente para la seguridad global.
Las declaraciones se dieron el domingo durante una entrevista en el canal estadounidense ABC News, semanas después de que Gates ya hubiera alertado sobre la falta de preparación del mundo frente a las consecuencias de la inteligencia artificial.
Ciberseguridad y riesgos de la inteligencia artificial en 2027
Gates fue categórico al describir el panorama que se avecina. “Los ciberataques serán sin duda el desafío más destacable al que nos enfrentaremos en el próximo año”, declaró el empresario durante la entrevista.
El cofundador de Microsoft diferenció entre dos tipos de amenazas vinculadas a la inteligencia artificial. Por un lado, descartó que el peligro inminente sea la pérdida de control sobre la tecnología, aunque reconoció que ese frente “habrá que trabajar en ello” a futuro.
Por otro lado, ubicó el riesgo real en el uso malintencionado de estas herramientas. “El verdadero peligro, en este momento, no es que la IA se vuelva incontrolable”, sino “más bien que personas malintencionadas la utilicen”, explicó.
Gates fue enfático respecto al nivel de sorpresa que generarán estos episodios. “Durante el próximo año, especialmente en el ámbito de la ciberseguridad, nos llevaremos muchas sorpresas desagradables”, advirtió el multimillonario.
Un ciberataque basado en inteligencia artificial es aquel en el que actores maliciosos emplean herramientas de IA para automatizar, perfeccionar o escalar ataques informáticos, desde el robo de datos hasta la suplantación de identidad. Según Gates, este tipo de amenazas crecerá de forma marcada en el próximo año debido a la insuficiente protección actual.
Fallas en los sistemas de protección de las empresas tecnológicas
El multimillonario cuestionó la solidez de los mecanismos de defensa que actualmente implementan las compañías dedicadas a la inteligencia artificial. A su juicio, estos sistemas de seguridad no están preparados para contener las amenazas de piratería informática que se perfilan.
Esta debilidad estructural, según su planteo, es lo que explica por qué el próximo año podría traer sorpresas negativas en materia de ciberseguridad. La brecha entre el desarrollo acelerado de la tecnología y la capacidad de protegerla sería, en su visión, el núcleo del problema.
Propuestas de Bill Gates para regular la inteligencia artificial
Frente a este escenario, Gates planteó un conjunto de medidas para gestionar la transformación que implica la inteligencia artificial. Entre sus propuestas figuran la creación de un impuesto específico sobre esta tecnología y la conformación de un organismo internacional dedicado a su supervisión.
A estas iniciativas sumó la idea de reservar determinados empleos de manera exclusiva para humanos, como forma de amortiguar el impacto laboral que podría generar la automatización impulsada por la inteligencia artificial.
Gates no es el único ejecutivo del sector en manifestar inquietud. Varios altos directivos de empresas tecnológicas subrayaron recientemente la necesidad de extremar la vigilancia sobre esta tecnología. Entre ellos, Dario Amodei, de la compañía Anthropic, se comprometió a ralentizar de forma unilateral el desarrollo de sus propios sistemas.
Postura de Gates frente a la autorregulación impulsada por Trump
En su entrevista con ABC News, Gates también se pronunció sobre el debate regulatorio en Estados Unidos. El empresario rechazó la postura defendida por el presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, según la cual la autorregulación de las empresas de inteligencia artificial sería suficiente para garantizar la seguridad a nivel mundial.
“Está claro que no estamos haciendo lo suficiente”, declaró Gates, en una crítica directa a la falta de controles externos sobre el desarrollo de estas tecnologías.

articles.title: CEOs say AI is helping their businesses be more productive — even if they're not always sure what's going on
articles.text:
CEOs say AI is helping their businesses be more productive — even if they're not always sure what's going on
AI is boosting productivity – but we need metrics
- AI named as one of the three biggest factors to boost productivity
- Visibility over costs and ROI falls short, study finds
- Legacy tech and skills gaps are ongoing issues
Over half (50%) UK CEOs have credited AI with being one of the three biggest contributors to their productivity improvements over the past year, ranking ahead of more traditional aids like redesigning and simplifying business processes (40%) and reselling workers (38%).
But despite naming AI as one of the biggest influencers on productivity, business leaders aren't exactly sure how it's helping, and only 14% of UK CEOs have full real-time visibility over their AI costs, a new EY report has claimed.
As such, one in three (32%) say they're unable to properly asses AI's ROI, making it difficult for them to actually know whether its impacts are translating into financial value.
AI is probably boosting productivity, but we don't really know how
"UK CEOs now want clear evidence that their investment is delivering stronger productivity and measurable business value," UK&I Managing Partner Silvia Rindone explained, implying that companies need greater visibility across their AI spend and impacts.
However, it's not just difficulties quantifying ROI that's helping non-adopters back when it comes to AI. Legacy systems (34%) and organizational complexity (29%) are still considered major blockers four years after generative AI was considered to have gone ultra-mainstream with the public launch of ChatGPT.
Skills shortages also continue to plague businesses, with three in four (74%) UK CEOs anticipating these gaps to worsen over the next three years – more so than access to capital, proving they can't even buy their way out of difficulties.
While organizations are seeking solid evidence that their investments are delivering measurable ROI in terms of productivity and revenue growth, EY's report emphasizes the fact that they can't overlook the same blockers that have been reappearing in studies over the years – legacy tech and skills shortages.

articles.title: WHO report on Russian lab worker death highlights "key uncertainty"
articles.text:
Over the weekend, the World Health Organization released a disease outbreak report on the events surrounding the death of a Russian infectious disease researcher earlier this month, highlighting that Russia has yet to report a confirmed cause of death. With that “key uncertainty,” the United Nations health agency said it remains impossible to assess the risk of the event or whether the public health measures Russia took were adequate to prevent spread of the unknown disease.
The WHO reported that, so far, it has seen no evidence of ongoing transmission of the mystery disease. “However, confidence in the assessment remains limited by the absence of a confirmed etiological diagnosis, and the remaining uncertainty regarding the source and mode of exposure,” the agency wrote in its report.
The agency laid out the order of events as information trickled out from Russian authorities, noting that it only became aware of the death via media reports on October 2. The WHO subsequently made contact with Russian authorities and requested information on October 3, 6, 7, and 8.
Limited information released
Early media reports indicated that the lab worker had become ill on September 29, possibly following an incident at the lab, the Irkutsk Antiplague Research Institute (APRI) of Siberia and the Far East. Some early reports suggested that the researcher—who was identified by media as 28-year-old Darya Shipilova—died of the plague after breaking a test tube.
On October 2, the Irkutsk branch of Russian health agency Rospotrebnadzor (RPN) said in a statement that a “special sanitary-epidemiological expert commission” had already met over a suspected case of a high-threat pathogen. Sanitary and epidemic control measures were put in place, including identifying, monitoring, and testing all contacts. At the time, RPN said that all contacts had tested negative for high-threat pathogens.
On October 6, Russia’s National Focal Point for the International Health Regulations (NFP) first responded to the WHO’s information requests, saying that no case of plague had been recorded in Irkutsk Oblast. The NFP confirmed that an APRI lab worker had died from a severe case of pneumonia after developing symptoms compatible with an acute respiratory viral infection. The worker was tested for a number of high-threat pathogens, but all the tests had come back negative. Doctors categorized the cause of death as being from pneumonia of undetermined etiology.

articles.title: Anthropic's Claude AI submitted false murder tip to Philadelphia police
articles.text:
An Anthropic AI model submitted a false tip about an unsolved murder to Philadelphia police, the company and police department confirmed on Friday.
A Claude model sent the false tip on July 18 to the Philadelphia Police Department’s website for submitting information about unsolved murders, but it was flagged by a spam filter. Anthropic apparently discovered the incident on September 28 and informed the police department about it on October 8.
During internal testing, Claude Haiku 4.5 was instructed to complete various forms up to the final submission stage and to stop before submitting those forms. “Several times Claude mistakenly submitted the form instead, expecting there to be an additional confirmation page,” Anthropic said in a report describing “unintended model actions we’ve observed during evaluations and internal use of Claude.”
The false murder tip occurred when Claude Haiku 4.5 was instructed to complete tasks on randomly selected webpages, Anthropic said:
In one run, the model landed on a page referencing an unsolved homicide; that page contained a tip form run by a police department. Claude was instructed never to log in, create accounts, enter personal data, make purchases, or submit anything destructive, but the instructions did not rule out form submissions. Claude filled out the form with the following: “I may have information regarding this case. I recall seeing someone matching the description in the area around [the street named on the page] during that time period. Please contact me if this information is relevant.”
Anthropic said it also discovered Claude incidents involving state and federal agency websites. Claude reportedly submitted 20 visa applications to the US State Department in one of these incidents.
Police call two-month delay “unacceptable”
Anthropic confirmed that the false homicide tip was sent to the Philadelphia Police Department, and the department issued a lengthy statement on the incident to the ABC station in Philadelphia. The false tip left the name and contact fields empty. It was not reviewed by any person because the email message generated when the tip was submitted ended up in a spam folder, police said.

articles.title: Fitbit Edge is Google’s middle ground between Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google’s Fitbit lineup expanded on Monday with the introduction of the Fitbit Edge, a new wearable that’s positioned between the Fitbit Air and Pixel Watch.
Priced at $179.99, it combines the Fitbit Air’s slim band with an OLED display for checking map directions, notifications, weather, and music controls.
Like the Pixel Watch and Fitbit Air, the Edge works with Google Health Coach, powered by Gemini. (You’ll need a Google Health Premium subscription to use it.) The coach can use your fitness, health, and medical information to put together weekly routines and workout plans, then adjust them around your schedule.
It also comes with Google’s Health Guardian feature, which is designed to spot notable changes in health measurements over time, including indicators related to blood pressure and insulin resistance. (The company announced these features at the Pixel Watch 5 launch in August.)
Google says the Fitbit Edge can automatically recognize and log up to 100 activities, including runs, bike rides, and walks. The company explains it uses context from your movement to work out what you’re doing and add it to your weekly goals. Plus, the device supports more than 50 exercise modes and can offer on-screen prompts during workouts, such as a nudge to push harder or take a breather.
The Fitbit Edge’s built-in GPS is 40% more accurate than the previous generation, the company claims, which should make it easier to track outdoor runs. Google says sleep-stage detection is also 15% more accurate than on earlier generations, helping the device provide better sleep summaries and coaching tips.
Meanwhile, the battery is rated for up to seven days on a charge, and the wearable is water-resistant to 50 meters.
The Fitbit Edge is available to preorder through the Google Store, with store availability set for October 27.
Color choices include Obsidian, Fog, Olive, and Canyon. There’s also a Stephen Curry Special Edition, priced at $219.99.

articles.title: TrendForce expects declining global laptop shipments to slow manufacturing exodus from China — rising CPU, DRAM, and SSD costs will make up 68% of mainstream notebook BOM
articles.text:
TrendForce expects declining global laptop shipments to slow manufacturing exodus from China — rising CPU, DRAM, and SSD costs will make up 68% of mainstream notebook BOM
Laptop prices could rise further.
In its latest industry report, TrendForce has projected that global notebook shipments could witness a decline of a low single-digit percentage in 2027. Laptop manufacturers are also expected to reconsider their production strategies as rising costs make manufacturing outside China less attractive. The share of global notebook production outside China is projected to fall from 24% in 2025 to 21% in 2026 and potentially below 20% in 2027.
The biggest concern is expected to be the shift from component availability to weakening consumer demand, as manufacturers continue to tackle high CPU, DRAM, and SSD prices. The firm also added that if component prices continue to remain on the higher side, brands might pass more of these costs on to consumers.
Notebook shipments are expected to benefit from improved CPU availability and manufacturers stocking up on components in 2026. However, TrendForce warns that it does not directly translate into healthy demand. In anticipation of higher prices, certain customers have upgraded their devices earlier than planned. Essentially, fewer people will be looking forward to buying new laptops in 2027.
Additionally, once inventories purchased at lower prices gradually run out, manufacturers will face greater pressure to absorb higher component costs or pass them on to consumers. Increasing the retail price could further weaken demand, while absorbing the additional costs would squeeze profit margins. Manufacturers could also make changes to specifications, including memory capacity, to control production costs, potentially making their products less competitive.
It is estimated that the CPU, DRAM, and SSD account for approximately 68% of the bill of materials (BOM) cost for mainstream notebooks with a $900 manufacturer’s suggested retail price in the third quarter of 2026. TrendForce said manufacturers are unlikely to maintain pricing, specifications, and profitability simultaneously in 2027.
Rising component costs will continue to put pressure on manufacturers. While DRAM supply is likely to remain tight due to AI demand, NAND flash availability could improve in the second half of 2027. TrendForce says the key challenge will be whether consumers can absorb higher laptop prices. If manufacturers manage to limit price increases by adjusting specifications and absorbing some costs, shipments could decline by a small percentage in 2027. However, if higher costs are passed on to consumers, the decline could reach the high-single-digit range.

articles.title: Zetwerk sets IPO price band at Rs 143-151, aims to raise Rs 5,012 Cr
articles.text:
Zetwerk sets IPO price band at Rs 143-151, aims to raise Rs 5,012 Cr
Zetwerk has expanded the size of its IPO and is seeking a valuation of Rs 25,583 crore.
Zetwerk, the Bengaluru-headquartered manufacturing marketplace, has set a price band of Rs 143–151 per share for its initial public offering (IPO), targeting a valuation of Rs 25,583 crore.
The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares and an offer for sale (OFS). The company has expanded the size of the public issue to Rs 5,012 crore.
The fresh issue has been increased from Rs 2,600 crore to Rs 2,830 crore, while the OFS component has been expanded from 9.68 crore shares to 14.45 crore shares.
Early investors, including Peak XV Partners, Lightspeed Venture Partners, Accel India, and Kae Capital, have increased the number of shares they plan to sell. The proposed share sale by the founders remains unchanged.
Lightspeed Venture Partners plans to sell 2.51 crore shares, followed by Peak XV Partners with 2.34 crore shares and Accel India with 1.2 crore shares.
Zetwerk’s promoters, Amrit Acharya and Srinath Ramakkrushnan, will sell 1.42 crore shares, while promoter group entity Creovate Innovation will offload 2.30 crore shares.
The IPO will open for subscription on October 15 and close on October 19. The anchor investor book will open on October 14, and the shares are expected to list on the stock exchanges on October 23.
Zetwerk plans to use around Rs 2,160 crore from the fresh issue to repay debt. The remaining proceeds will be allocated towards acquisitions, strategic investments and general corporate purposes.
The company reported revenue of Rs 15,913 crore in FY26, a 40.4% increase from Rs 11,332 crore in FY25. However, its losses widened to Rs 1,606.2 crore in FY26 from Rs 370.7 crore in the previous fiscal year, largely due to a one-time charge.
Established in 2017, Zetwerk is a digital manufacturing marketplace that connects businesses, manufacturers and suppliers on one platform.
In Q1 FY27, its revenue from operations grew 55% year-on-year to Rs 4,118 crore, while losses from continuing operations narrowed to Rs 64 crore from Rs 881 crore in the year-ago quarter.

articles.title: La factura invisible del alzhéimer: las familias españolas soportan cada vez más el coste real de la enfermedad
articles.text:
El alzhéimer es una enfermedad que, por desgracia, tiene un impacto muy negativo sobre cualquier paciente y también en su entorno familiar, que tiene que sufrir las consecuencias y el cuidado. Y no hablamos de una patología banal, sino que tiene una incidencia muy importante en nuestro entorno, que conlleva a invertir una gran cantidad de dinero y tiempo.
El baile de las cifras. Cada año se hace un recopilatorio que nos pone en perspectiva para saber cómo nos encontramos en incidencia de alzhéimer, y como referencia tenemos a las estimaciones publicadas por la Sociedad Española de Neurología, que apuntan a que en España ya hay más de 800.000 personas con esta enfermedad. Y no es una cifra que se quede estática, puesto que cada año se diagnostican más o menos 40.000 casos nuevos. Y si profundizamos un poco más en estos datos, nos damos cuenta de que el 65% de los casos corresponden a las mujeres.
Sin embargo, estos 800.000 afectados es más una estimación institucional, puesto que si nos vamos a otros datos como los publicados en la revista PharmacoEconomics nos encontramos con que la prevalencia del Alzheimer en España está entre el 2,4% y el 6,9% en mayores de 65 años. Y si aplicamos esta incidencia ajustada a la población oficial, hablaríamos en realidad de entre 210.000 y 260.000 personas.
La mortalidad es otro punto muy importante para entender el impacto de la enfermedad, y aquí los datos del INE en 2025 nos apuntan a que se registraron 22.870 muertes por demencia, lo que supone un 3,9% más que en 2024. Y a esto hay que sumar 13.242 fallecimientos atribuidos de forma específica a la enfermedad de Alzheimer, lo que da una suma total de 36.112 muertes.
Con estos datos encima de la mesa, hay algunas voces que suelen apuntar a que el alzhéimer o la demencia representan la principal causa de muerte en nuestro país. Pero técnicamente esto es falso, puesto que el INE clasifica la demencia dentro del capítulo de trastornos mentales, mientras que al alzhéimer lo agrupa dentro de los trastornos neurológicos. Esta separación hace que la enfermedad isquémica del corazón sea la causa de muerte más prevalente, salvo en mujeres, donde la principal causa de muerte absoluta en España sí que fue la demencia.
Percepción del cuidado. Recientemente, el Estudio Sanitas sobre Alzheimer nos dejó un dato impactante al apuntar que el 47,7% de los españoles han cuidado en algún momento de su vida a una persona con Alzheimer y un 10,4% se declara cuidador principal en su hogar.
Algo que debemos tener en cuenta es que, si casi la mitad de la población afirma haber cuidado a un enfermo, esto apunta a que la definición de "cuidar" es tremendamente amplia y autodeclarada. Aunque si lo ponemos más en contexto, vemos que en la encuesta realizada en 2024 un 42,7% afirmaba simplemente conocer a alguien cercano con la enfermedad. Por tanto, debe interpretarse como una medida de la alta percepción y sensibilización social sobre la enfermedad, más que como un dato formal sobre la prevalencia real del cuidado continuado.
El coste oculto. Más allá del sacrificio que supone volcar una gran cantidad de tiempo en atender los cuidados de una persona con esta enfermedad, el gasto económico que supone también atisba una gran presión sobre muchas familias. Aquí la propia OMS apuntó a que la demencia costó 1.300 millones de dólares a la economía mundial con un problema bastante importante: la mitad de esta factura no la paga el sistema sanitario, sino que corresponde a las familias.
Y dentro de estas familias se distingue también que las mujeres asumen la peor parte del cuidado, y de esta manera ya no solo representan el 65% de las muertes por demencia, sino que también aportan el 70% de las horas mundiales de cuidado.
En España vemos esta misma foto, puesto que ya la encuesta EDAD 2020 del INE nos explicaba que el perfil principal de quien cuida a una persona con discapacidad es una mujer de 45 a 64 años que vive en el mismo hogar. Y si concretamos algo mejor, sabemos que el 63,7 % de quienes cuidan en nuestro país son mujeres, y en el caso de los pacientes mayores de 80 años, el cuidado principal recae de forma masiva sobre las hijas en el 41,1 % de los casos, frente a un lejano 18 % asumido por los hijos.
Este gran esfuerzo familiar no sale gratis, y aquí el cálculo más aproximado determina que el coste medio anual por paciente en España es de 42.336 euros en el escenario más conservador. De esta cantidad, la mayor partida es precisamente el trabajo invisible, puesto que el cuidado informal representa el 80 % de los costes directos no sanitarios y el 69 % de todo el coste global.

articles.title: La NASA publicó más de 800 gigabytes de datos de la misión lunar Artemis II
articles.text:
La NASA publicó más de 800 gigabytes de datos científicos de la misión Artemis II, la primera vuelta tripulada alrededor de la Luna en más de cinco décadas. El archivo difundido incluye imágenes, videos y audios recogidos por los cuatro astronautas durante el sobrevuelo lunar.
El conjunto quedó disponible en el Sistema de Datos Planetarios, el archivo público que la NASA usa para sus misiones planetarias. Incluye más de 11.000 fotografías y videos en resolución completa, 8,5 horas de audio con las observaciones científicas de la tripulación y una serie de imágenes con anotaciones manuscritas de los astronautas.
Junto con el material, la agencia difundió tres documentos: el Informe Preliminar de Ciencia Lunar de Artemis II, el Informe de Operaciones Científicas y una guía de uso de los datos. Según la NASA, es la primera vez en más de 50 años que se reúne un conjunto de datos planetarios capturado principalmente por personas y no por instrumentos robóticos.
Artemis II despegó el 1 de abril con cuatro tripulantes a bordo de la cápsula Orion y sobrevoló la Luna el día 6, acercándose hasta unos 4.067 millas (6.545 kilómetros) de la superficie antes de regresar y amarizar frente a la costa de San Diego. Cabe señalar que fue la primera misión tripulada en pasar cerca de la Luna desde el Apolo 17, en 1972.
Destellos en la cara oculta de la Luna
Entre los hallazgos más llamativos figuran los audios en los que el comandante Reid Wiseman reportó a la sala de control de la misión, en el Centro Espacial Johnson de Houston, haber observado destellos de impacto en la superficie lunar.
“Vimos tres destellos de impacto hasta ahora”, dijo Wiseman durante el sobrevuelo. “No fue un reflejo de alguna partícula de los propulsores ni de los tanques de purga. Fueron definitivamente destellos de impacto en la Luna”.
El Informe Preliminar de Ciencia Lunar, difundido junto con los datos, precisó que la tripulación terminó reportando cinco destellos en total, generados por el choque de pequeños fragmentos rocosos contra la superficie lunar durante un eclipse de 54 minutos observado desde la nave Orion.
El equipo científico descartó otras fuentes, como reflejos solares o rayos cósmicos, antes de confirmar las observaciones.
Los destellos de impacto ya habían sido reportados antes por tripulaciones del programa Apolo, hace medio siglo, y por telescopios terrestres en cientos de ocasiones. Nunca antes, sin embargo, una misión tripulada moderna los había confirmado desde tan cerca de la Luna.
El material incluye también los audios en los que la tripulación describió, en tiempo real, una variedad de colores en la superficie lunar que no se perciben desde la Tierra.
En una de las grabaciones difundidas, Christina Koch describió un tono amarillento en una zona de la Luna como “la mejilla curtida de la Luna”, mientras observaba las planicies volcánicas cercanas al cráter Aristarco.
La observación de los destellos y de los colores lunares ocurrió durante un eclipse solar de 54 minutos, cuando la Luna se interpuso entre la nave y el Sol.
Según relató Glover en los audios difundidos, la escena lo dejó sin palabras: “No creo que la mente humana esté preparada para ver esto”, dijo mientras fotografiaba el fenómeno desde la ventanilla de Orion.
Preparación para las próximas misiones
La tripulación estuvo integrada por el comandante Wiseman, el piloto Victor Glover, primer astronauta afroamericano asignado a una misión lunar, y la especialista de misión Christina Koch, poseedora del récord de vuelo espacial individual más largo logrado por una mujer.
También participó el especialista Jeremy Hansen, de la Agencia Espacial Canadiense, el primer astronauta no estadounidense en viajar más allá de la órbita baja terrestre.
Los cuatro habían recibido entrenamiento previo en geología y geografía lunar para reconocer, en tiempo real y sin ayuda de instrumentos, observaciones de interés científico durante el sobrevuelo.
El archivo también documenta diferencias de color y textura entre distintas regiones de la Luna, percibidas a simple vista por la tripulación, y detalles del terminador, la línea que separa el día y la noche lunares.
Según la NASA, esos registros ayudarán a planificar las próximas misiones Artemis, que apuntan al polo sur lunar, donde las condiciones de iluminación son más extremas que en la ruta que siguió Artemis II.
Todo el material quedó disponible de forma gratuita para científicos, instituciones académicas y el público general a través del sitio del Sistema de Datos Planetarios de la NASA.
Durante el sobrevuelo, la nave Orion llegó a ubicarse a más de 252.000 millas (unos 405.000 kilómetros) de la Tierra, la mayor distancia alcanzada por una tripulación desde las misiones Apolo.
La agencia aclaró que esta es apenas la primera entrega de datos de la misión. El paquete llamado SPICE, que contiene la información precisa de navegación y posición de la nave Orion durante el vuelo, todavía no fue incluido en esta publicación y se sumará al archivo más adelante.

articles.title: Astera Labs Unveils Orion: A Compute-Agnostic Rack-Scale Architecture
articles.text:
Monday, October 12th 2026
Astera Labs Unveils Orion: A Compute-Agnostic Rack-Scale Architecture
Astera Labs, Inc. (Nasdaq: ALAB), a leader in semiconductor-based connectivity solutions for rack-scale AI infrastructure, today announced Orion: a modular rack-scale reference design with production-grade connectivity that allows customers to choose their own GPU and CPU. To be offered through Astera Labs' ODM and OEM partners, the Orion production-grade reference designs are expected to help enable neocloud and enterprise customers to deploy AI infrastructure faster and run it more efficiently, turning racks built on open standards into token-efficient AI factories.
For neoclouds and enterprises to economically serve inference at scale, they must secure sufficient accelerator and CPU capacity while delivering predictable, low-latency performance across increasingly complex AI infrastructure. But because they must commit to that capacity long before they know which accelerator will be available or affordable for their workloads, tying early investment to a single platform carries unnecessary cost and risk. At the same time, ODMs and OEMs are forced to repeatedly solve complex integration, validation, and software challenges for every new accelerator platform—slowing deployments when inference capacity is in critical demand.Orion addresses these challenges with a production-grade reference architecture that decouples rack-scale designs from accelerator and CPU selection. Built on open standards to support industry-leading inference accelerators and CPU ecosystems, Orion is designed to enable operators to deploy infrastructure once and scale inference workloads across the most cost-effective and readily available compute resources—via PCIe plug-in cards—without redesigning racks as technology and market dynamics evolve. At the core of Orion is a high-performance, standards-based, scale-up fabric engineered to connect up to 160 accelerators per pod and deliver predictable, low-latency communication and expanded memory capacity across racks and pods. Orion's optimized PCIe connectivity and composable infrastructure are additionally designed to help accelerators extract more tokens-per-second across AI inference workloads. Orion is delivered as a complete modular rack-scale reference design—including system configurations for the compute tray, fabric tray, memory tray, link board, and compute board—all integrated with COSMOS Rack Manager and COSMOS Fabric Manager orchestration software for management, fleet-wide telemetry, diagnostics, and AI infrastructure intelligence.
Pravin Patel, vice president and general manager of the AI Platform Solutions Group at Astera Labs"We're entering a new era of AI inference, where operators are judged on the tokens they deliver per dollar, not the hardware inside their racks. Orion gives AI inference cloud providers a production-grade, compute-agnostic architecture so they can quickly bring inference capacity online, provide outcome-based pricing for their customers, and adapt as the industry and compute landscape evolves."
Orion rack reference and system designs are on track for availability through Astera Labs' OEM and ODM partners beginning in Q1 2027. Astera Labs will showcase a powered Orion rack—featuring interchangeable, pre-validated compute trays with different CPU and accelerator configurations at the 2026 Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit, taking place October 12-15 in San Jose, California.
