articles.title: El sistema de 3 hashtags para no volver a perder una URL en WhatsApp
articles.text:
El sistema de 3 hashtags para no volver a perder una URL en WhatsApp consiste en enviar cada enlace de interés al chat personal de la aplicación acompañado de tres etiquetas fijas que indican categoría, formato y estado, de modo que el buscador interno permita localizar ese contenido en segundos sin importar cuánto tiempo haya pasado desde que se guardó.
Cómo funciona el método de etiquetado triple en WhatsApp
La base del sistema está en la función de búsqueda por texto exacto que ofrece WhatsApp. Esa herramienta, pensada originalmente para rastrear conversaciones, se convierte aquí en un motor de clasificación cuando se combina con hashtags escritos de forma constante.
El método propone tres etiquetas por cada enlace, cada una con una función distinta. La primera responde a la pregunta de dónde pertenece el contenido, con hashtags como #Trabajo, #Estudios, #Recetas, #Finanzas u #Hogar. La segunda precisa qué tipo de recurso es, mediante etiquetas como #Video, #PDF, #Curso o #Herramienta.
Es menester señalar que la tercera marca qué acción corresponde tomar frente a ese enlace, con opciones como #Pendiente, #ParaLeer, #Urgente o #Guardado.
Esta triple combinación evita que el chat personal se convierta en un listado desordenado de enlaces sin contexto. Al escribir siempre las mismas tres categorías de etiquetas, cualquier búsqueda posterior por una palabra clave o por la combinación de dos hashtags devuelve únicamente los mensajes que cumplen con esos criterios, sin mezclar resultados de otros temas.
Pasos para configurar el chat personal como gestor de enlaces
El primer movimiento consiste en localizar dentro de WhatsApp la opción de enviar mensajes a uno mismo, disponible al buscar el propio nombre o número en la lista de contactos. Como alternativa, puede crearse un grupo donde solo participe el usuario, con un nombre identificable como “Mis Enlaces” o “Marcadores”.
Una vez identificado ese chat, conviene fijarlo en la parte superior de la lista de conversaciones. De esa forma queda siempre visible y accesible, sin necesidad de buscarlo cada vez que se quiere guardar o consultar un enlace.
A partir de ahí, el proceso de carga es simple. Cuando aparece una URL de interés, ya sea en el navegador, en una red social o compartida por otra persona, se copia o se reenvía directamente al chat personal. Antes de enviar el mensaje conviene agregar un título breve que describa el contenido y, a continuación, las tres etiquetas correspondientes.
Un ejemplo de este formato sería un mensaje con el texto “Curso gratuito de Excel avanzado para finanzas”, seguido del enlace y de las etiquetas #Estudios #Curso #Pendiente. Esa estructura repetida en cada envío es lo que sostiene la eficacia del sistema a largo plazo.
Estrategias de búsqueda y actualización de los enlaces guardados
Para recuperar un enlace guardado, basta con tocar la lupa de búsqueda ubicada en la parte superior de WhatsApp y escribir la combinación de hashtags que se necesite. Buscar #ParaLeer mostrará todo el material pendiente de lectura, mientras que combinar #Trabajo y #Video filtrará únicamente los videos relacionados con tareas laborales.
El sistema también contempla un mecanismo de mantenimiento. Cuando una tarea vinculada a un enlace se completa, por ejemplo tras ver un video marcado como pendiente, es posible editar el mensaje original o responder a él con la etiqueta #Completado. Esto actualiza el estado del recurso sin eliminar el historial del enlace.
Esta función de edición o respuesta evita que el chat acumule marcas desactualizadas y permite diferenciar, con una simple búsqueda, entre lo que sigue pendiente y lo que ya fue resuelto.
Catálogo de hashtags según el tipo de contenido guardado
Para quienes recién implementan el método, resulta útil partir de un catálogo de etiquetas predefinido según el tipo de recurso que se guarda con frecuencia.
Una receta de cocina, por ejemplo, puede clasificarse con #Cocina como categoría, #Receta como formato y #ParaProbar como estado. Un artículo vinculado al trabajo puede etiquetarse con #Trabajo, #Lectura y #Pendiente.
Una herramienta de inteligencia artificial encontrada en internet puede organizarse bajo #Tecnologia, #Herramienta y #Guardado. Y un hotel o destino de vacaciones puede guardarse con #Viajes, #Hotel y #PorRevisar.
Mantener esta coherencia en las combinaciones de hashtags, categoría, formato y estado, es lo que permite que el chat personal de WhatsApp funcione como una agenda visual de enlaces ordenada y consultable en cualquier momento.

articles.title: Zurück in die 2000er: Mit Bingebrowse durchstöberst du Streaming-Angebote wie in einer virtuellen Videothek
articles.text:
Wie in der Videothek: So hast du die Angebote deiner Streaming-Dienste noch nie gesehen
Netflix, Prime Video, Disney Plus: Streaming-Dienste gibt es inzwischen viele. Oft dauert die Auswahl des passenden Titels für einen entspannten Abend auf der Couch aber länger als der Film selbst. Die Website Bingebrowse will genervten Streaming-Abonnent:innen Abwechslung bieten und katapultiert sie in eine klassische Videothek aus längst vergangenen Zeiten. Nutzer:innen wählen ihre bevorzugten Video-Plattformen aus und bewegen sich anschließend durch den virtuellen Raum.
Wie eine Videothek aus den 2000er-Jahren
Früher gehörten Videotheken fest zum Stadtbild. In den 2010er-Jahren verschwanden die Läden mit ihren aneinandergereihten Video- und DVD-Hüllen nach und nach. Die Auswahl fiel schon damals oft nicht leicht, allerdings war das Angebot deutlich begrenzter und kuratierter. Zum Vergleich: Allein Netflix bietet heute mehrere tausend Filme und Serien. Bingebrowse verwandelt dieses Angebot in eine Oldschool-Videothek mit thematisch sortierten Regalen wie „Neuheiten“, „Familie“ oder „Science-Fiction“. Laut den beiden Software-Entwicklern Oliver und Patrick Evans, die hinter dem Projekt stehen, geht das Konzept auf: Gegenüber dem Spiegel teilten sie mit, dass die Website seit Ende Juli mehr als eine Million Besucher:innen hatte.
Optisch erinnert Bingebrowse an ein Videospiel der frühen 2000er. Per Klick bewegen sich Nutzer:innen durch die Abteilungen und schauen sich um. Sie können jedes Film- oder Serien-Cover auswählen und es so aus dem virtuellen Regal herausnehmen. Daraufhin öffnet sich eine Infoseite mit Kurzbeschreibung und Youtube-Link zum dazugehörigen Trailer. Nützlich ist die anbieterübergreifende Auswahl, denn Abonnent:innen müssen sich mit Bingebrowse nicht durch eine App nach der anderen scrollen, um einen spannenden Titel zu finden. Besonders praktisch ist zudem, dass nur Titel angezeigt werden, die im eigenen Land abrufbar sind. So werden Streaming-Nutzer:innen nicht enttäuscht, wenn ein gefundener Film oder eine gefundene Serie dann doch nicht verfügbar ist.
Retro-Trend zeigt sich auch bei CDs und Vynil
Standardmäßig bietet die virtuelle Videothek Platz für 1.084 Titel. Größere Räume mit bis zu 2.148 Filmen und Serien lassen sich gegen Gebühr freischalten. Über ein Optionsmenü können Videothek-Besucher:innen außerdem deren Einrichtung anpassen. Auch für dieses Feature fallen teilweise Zusatzkosten an. Laut eigener Auskunft sind Oliver und Patrick Evans 28 Jahre alt und arbeiten in der Londoner Finanzbranche als Software-Entwickler. Bingebrowse ist für sie ein Nebenprojekt. Gegenüber dem Spiegel sagten sie aber, dass sie es in Zukunft gerne um Bücher und Musik ausbauen würden.
Dass die virtuelle Videothek gut ankommt, ist nicht überraschend. Der Retro-Trend zeigt sich auch in anderen Bereichen. So hat beispielsweise der Absatz von CDs wieder deutlich zugenommen. Laut einem Bericht der Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), dem Interessenverband der US-Tonträgerindustrie, erzielten die physischen Medien im ersten Halbjahr 2026 einen Umsatz von 171,1 Millionen Dollar – ein Plus von fast 58,6 Prozent gegenüber dem Vorjahreszeitraum. Auch Schallplatten bleiben beliebt. Scheinbar unbegrenzte Streaming-Angebote sind im digitalen Zeitalter also nicht immer die erste Wahl.

articles.title: When Should You Use Liquid Clustering? Benchmarking Lakehouse Layout Strategies
articles.text:
Key Takeaways
- No single storage layout is universally optimal for lakehouse analytics: The right choice is workload-dependent, because using Liquid Clustering, ZOrder, or Partitioning incorrectly can materially impact cost and latency.
- ZOrder has a hidden failure mode. When a date column appears as a secondary or tertiary clustering key, time range queries perform significantly worse than on a simple date-partitioned table.
- Bytes scanned is a misleading performance proxy. Liquid Clustering delivers the lowest latency on point lookups despite scanning more raw data than ZOrder.
- Liquid Clustering should be the default for any team whose query patterns are diverse or evolving and outperforms ZOrder on most workloads while eliminating the operational burden of manual OPTIMIZE jobs and periodic full table rewrites.
- Before finalizing any layout strategy, ask yourself: ”Do my top queries consistently filter on the same two or three columns? If the answer is yes, ZOrder those columns. Otherwise, choose Liquid Clustering.
Introduction
No single storage layout is universally optimal for lakehouse analytical systems. Across four workload types benchmarked on Delta Lake, Liquid Clustering delivers the lowest latency for point lookups, time-range aggregations, and large aggregations. Liquid Clustering should be the default for teams whose query patterns are diverse or evolving. ZOrdering performed better only for stable, highly selective multicolumn predicate workloads where the filter columns precisely match the clustering key.
Partitioning, ZOrdering, and Liquid Clustering each take a fundamentally different approach to organizing data on disk; understanding the tradeoffs is key to choosing the right one for your workload. Two of my findings stand out because they run counter to how these layouts are usually described and because they are the kind of thing that could be silently degrading a production system right now,
ZOrder’s Hidden Failure Mode on Date Ranges
When a date column sits as a secondary or tertiary key in a ZOrder clustering expression, time-range queries perform significantly worse than a simple date-partitioned table, seventy-eight percent slower in this benchmark. Sequential date values are dispersed across files, destroying the range-scan efficiency that partitioning provides for free. If your team ZOrdered on multiple columns and date is not the first key, this is almost certainly affecting your time-range query performance.
Liquid Clustering’s Precision Gap on Multicolumn Filters
When a query predicate precisely matches a stable set of filter columns, ZOrder’s file pruning is close to optimal and Liquid Clustering can be nearly five times slower while scanning ten times more data. Liquid Clustering’s broader locality optimization trades deterministic pruning for workload flexibility. That trade-off becomes a liability exactly when queries are narrow and predictable.
These results matter because physical data layout is one of the most consequential and least discussed decisions in lakehouse engineering while the trade-offs between partitioning, ZOrdering, and Liquid Clustering are usually described conceptually rather than measured.
Most published comparisons either come from Databricks itself or reason about the trade-offs from first principles without measuring actual query behavior. The questions behind this benchmark were shaped directly by production challenges I encountered while architecting Delta Lake platforms at TCS UK (civil aerospace) and IBM (Shell Maritime), where layout decisions have direct implications for pipeline SLA compliance and cloud compute cost.
My practical recommendation, before you commit to a layout strategy, is to run your top three query patterns against all three configurations, partitioned, ZOrdered, and Liquid Clustered, on a representative sample of your own data. The results below, from a controlled benchmark comparing all three layout strategies across four analytical workload types on a fifty-million-record dataset using real Databricks query profiles, may surprise you as much as they surprised me.
What This Means in Practice
Taken together, the results map out a clear decision framework based on workload type:
| Workload Type | Best Layout | Why | 
| Point Lookup | Liquid Clustering | Superior intra-file locality reduces seek overhead | 
| TimeRange Aggregation | Liquid Clustering | Sequential locality outperforms ZOrder's dispersed date values | 
| MultiColumn Selective Filter | ZOrder | Precise file pruning 10x less data scanned | 
| Large Aggregation | Liquid Clustering | Hilbert curve locality wins for full scan workloads | 
Perhaps the single most actionable insight in this article is a deceptively simple diagnostic question that practitioners should ask before committing to any layout strategy: do my top queries consistently filter on the same two to three columns? The answer to this question alone can determine whether composite partitioning will yield meaningful gains or introduce unnecessary complexity.
If the answer is yes and those columns are known and stable, use ZOrder on exactly those columns to ensure the most selective column is listed first. If the answer is no, or if query patterns are likely to evolve, use Liquid Clustering as the default. Liquid Clustering wins on three out of four workload types and removes the operational overhead of manual OPTIMIZE scheduling. A decision helper written in Python is available on GitHub.
The sections below lay out the methodology, results, and analysis behind these recommendations, the how and why, for readers who want to verify the findings before applying them.
Experiment Setup
Below are the dataset, layout configuration, workloads, and results from the analysis.
Dataset
A synthetic transactional dataset of fifty million records was generated to simulate a retail purchase environment, with the following schema:
customer_id   INT         uniform distribution, range 12,000,000
txn_date      DATE        spanning 20192023
region        STRING      categorical: EU, US, APAC, LATAM (skewed toward EU/US)
amount        FLOAT       rightskewed, simulating highvalue outliers
product_cat   STRING      categorical, 12 categories
The mix of uniform and skewed distributions was deliberate, with parameters calibrated against empirically observed access-frequency patterns in production traces. Specifically, skew parameters such as Zipf α = 1.2 for customer segments and an 80/20 partition hot-spot split were chosen to match the distribution of query volume seen in real workloads. These values were not selected arbitrarily but derived from production telemetry, where the top twenty percent of customer segments consistently account for approximately eighty percent of query traffic, ensuring the synthetic dataset reflects real-world hot partitions and demand skew.
Layout Configuration
Partitioned table
df.write.format('delta').partitionBy('txn_date').saveAsTable('lc_partitioned')
 ZOrdered table
spark.sql('OPTIMIZE lc_zorder ZORDER BY (customer_id, region, txn_date)')
 Liquid Clustered table
spark.sql('''
  CREATE TABLE lc_liquid
  CLUSTER BY (customer_id, region, txn_date)
  AS SELECT * FROM source_data
''')
Workloads
All the queries can be found on GitHub.
Results
W1: Point Lookup
Liquid Clustering achieved the lowest latency at 1.003 seconds, forty-nine percent faster than the partitioned baseline, despite scanning more raw data than ZOrder. This is the first counterintuitive result, which produced better performance from reading more bytes. The explanation is intra-file sequential locality. Liquid Clustering's Hilbert curve organization colocates related customer_id values within files more effectively, reducing disk seek overhead and increasing scan throughput. ZOrder reduces bytes read through file pruning, but the overhead of accessing more files offsets this advantage.
| Layout | Runtime (median) | Data Read | Notes | 
| Partitioned | 1.972s | 737.47 MB | Baseline | 
| ZOrder | 1.437s | 369.09 MB | 50% less data, slower | 
| Liquid Clustering | 1.003s ✓ | 784.86 MB | Best latency | 
W2: TimeRange Aggregation
Liquid Clustering again achieved the lowest latency at 659 milliseconds. ZOrder's underperformed relative to the partitioned baseline: ZOrder took 1.845 seconds versus partitioning's 1.038 seconds, seventy-eight percent slower. The ZOrder clustering key was (customer_id, region, txn_date), making txn_date a tertiary key. This disperses sequential date values across files, destroying the daterange scan efficiency that simple partitioning provides for free. If your team ZOrders on multiple columns and the date is not the first key, this is almost certainly affecting your timerange query performance.
| Layout | Runtime (median) | Data Read | Notes | 
| Partitioned | 1s 038ms | 449.69 MB | Date partition helps | 
| ZOrder | 1s 845ms | 306.80 MB | 78% slower than partition | 
| Liquid Clustering | 659ms ✓ | 449.19 MB | Best latency | 
Figure 1a. Range aggregation, partitioned table. Source here.
Figure 1b. Range aggregation, ZOrdered table. Source here.
Figure 1c. Range aggregation, Liquid Clustered table. Source here.
W3: MultiColumn Selective Filter
This workload produced the sharpest reversal. ZOrder achieved 615 milliseconds and read only 59.03 megabytes. Liquid Clustering took 2.967 seconds and read 639.95 megabytes, nearly five times slower and scanning ten times more data. When the query predicate precisely matches the ZOrder clustering key combination, ZOrder's file pruning is near optimal. Liquid Clustering's broader locality optimization, designed for workload diversity, becomes a liability here, because it cannot achieve the same level of precise file elimination unlike ZOrder, which locks onto a fixed column order to eliminate files precisely, Liquid Clustering trades that precision for flexibility and on this workload, that tradeoff costs it. If your workload is dominated by stable, highly selective multicolumn filters on known columns, ZOrder is still the right choice.
| Layout | Runtime (median) | Data Read | Notes | 
| Partitioned | 622ms | 128.09 MB | Moderate pruning | 
| ZOrder | 615ms ✓ | 59.03 MB ✓ | Optimal pruning | 
| Liquid Clustering | 2.967s | 639.95 MB | 5x slower worst case | 
Figure 2a. Multicolumn filter partitioned table. Source here.
Figure 2b. Multicolumn filter ordered table. Source here.
Figure 2c. Multicolumn filter Liquid Clustered table. Source here.
W4: Large Aggregation
For a full dataset SUM aggregation grouped by region (using the same query as W2 but run without predicate filtering across the entire dataset to clarify the benchmark numbers), Liquid Clustering again achieved the lowest latency (659 milliseconds) with ZOrder the slowest (1.845 seconds). For full scan workloads file pruning provides no benefit; the determinant of performance shifts to intra-file read efficiency and task scheduling, both of which favor Liquid Clustering's Hilbert curve locality.
| Layout | Runtime (median) | Data Read | Notes | 
| Partitioned | 1s 038ms | 449.69 MB | Acceptable | 
| ZOrder | 1s 845ms | 306.80 MB | Slowest no pruning benefit | 
| Liquid Clustering | 659ms ✓ | 449.19 MB | Best latency | 
Discussion
The same two mechanisms explain the results across all four workloads: file-pruning efficiency, how much data a layout avoids reading, and intra-file locality, how efficiently the read data is scanned. ZOrder and partitioning compete primarily on pruning. Liquid Clustering wins primarily on locality, via its Hilbert curve organization, even when it reads more bytes than ZOrder. Where a query precisely matches a stable clustering key, pruning dominates and ZOrder wins (W3). Where it doesn’t, or a full scan is unavoidable, locality dominates and Liquid Clustering wins (W1, W2, W4). The ZOrder date-range failure mode (W2) is the same pruning-versus-locality trade-off viewed from the other side. Making date a tertiary key sacrifices the sequential locality that a date partition gives away for free, without buying back enough pruning benefit to compensate.
Caveats
These benchmarks use a synthetic dataset to ensure reproducibility and avoid client data exposure. Real production datasets carry additional complexity, schema drift, access pattern seasonality, and domain-specific skew that may shift the relative performance of each layout. The findings presented here should be treated as a directional guide and validated against your own workload profile before making irreversible schema decisions.
Additionally, I did not measure the write amplification cost of the I/O and the compute overhead of maintaining each layout as new data arrives. Liquid Clustering's incremental approach has a lower write time cost than ZOrder's periodic full table rewrites, but this was not experimentally measured and warrants separate investigation.
Conclusion
No single storage layout is universally optimal for lakehouse analytical systems. Liquid Clustering outperforms on latency for point lookups, range scans, and large aggregations, and should be the default for teams with diverse or evolving workloads. ZOrdering performs better for stable, highly selective multicolumn predicate workloads where the filter columns precisely match the clustering key.
The two most practically significant findings, ZOrder's degradation on range scans when date is a secondary key, and Liquid Clustering's five times latency penalty on precise multicolumn filters, are failure modes that are not documented and are likely affecting production systems today.
Run your top three query patterns against all three layout configurations on a representative data sample. The results may surprise you.

articles.title: Russia was not ready for the data center war it started with Ukraine
articles.text:
When Russia began attacking Ukrainian data centers and telecommunication infrastructure, it apparently failed to prepare for possible retaliation. Now Russia’s digital services are facing widespread outages after Ukrainian drone strikes knocked out three of the largest data centers owned by Russian tech giant Yandex within several days.
Pro-Kremlin bloggers are warning that Russia’s centralized digital economy could collapse because the country is not prepared for the “data center war” it started, according to posts translated by the pseudonymous independent researcher ChrisO_wiki. The Russian commentators also suggested that Ukraine’s decentralized digital services could prove more resilient than Russia’s system if the countries continue trading such blows.
Russia initially launched a drone strike campaign targeting Ukrainian data centers and mobile phone networks in late September. The attacks temporarily disrupted Internet and cell phone service for up to 100,000 households in the Ukrainian capital of Kyiv and came as part of a broader long-range strike campaign that has involved Russian missiles and jet-powered drones hitting Ukraine’s power grid infrastructure, transportation hubs, and even residential apartment building blocks.
But Ukraine soon began striking back at data centers owned by the Russian company Yandex, also known as “Russia’s Google,” in what Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has described as a “symmetrical response.”
AI data centers and supercomputers
The first Ukrainian drone attack damaged a data center in the Sasovo region southeast of Moscow on October 8, which houses two of the three supercomputers that Yandex has used to train its YandexGPT AI model.
It was not immediately clear how much damage may have occurred to the supercomputers, which are based on Nvidia A100 GPU chips. The Chervonenkis supercomputer has a computing performance rated at 29.42 petaflops and ranks at 101 on the Top 500 List of supercomputers, while the Lyapunov supercomputer is rated at 20.03 petaflops and ranks at 161.

articles.title: O Ubuntu Linux 26.10 está chegando e estas são as novidades • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
O Ubuntu Linux 26.10 está chegando e estas são as novidades
Ubuntu 26.10 "Stonking Stingray" traz o Gnome 51 como ambiente de desktop e é baseado no kernel Linux 7.3.
O Ubuntu 26.10 “Stonking Stingray” traz o Gnome 51, kernel Linux 7.3 e migração de utilitários de linha de comando para Rust.
O Gnome 51 melhora animações, a organização de configurações e recursos de acessibilidade.
A distribuição atualiza diversos apps nativos, como Files, Papers, App Center, Firefox 156 e LibreOffice 26.8, com lançamento previsto para 15 de outubro
Dando sequência à tradição de lançar uma nova versão de sua distribuição Linux no mês de outubro, a Canonical está prestes a liberar o Ubuntu 26.10 “Stonking Stingray”. O sistema operacional traz o ambiente de desktop Gnome 51 como principal atrativo, mas também introduz o kernel Linux 7.3 e “abraça” a linguagem Rust. Confira as principais novidades a seguir.
O Gnome 51 foi apresentado em setembro como uma versão do ambiente de desktop que muda pouco na aparência, mas aprimora a experiência de uso, o desempenho e até aspectos de segurança.
Um exemplo de combinação desses atributos vem do gerenciador de janelas Mutter, que torna animações ou efeitos de transição mais suaves, reduzindo o risco de congelamentos ou de “quadros perdidos” durante essas atividades.
O Gnome 51 também permite que o Ubuntu 26.10 tenha uma área de configurações mais bem organizada, oferece um seletor de layout de janelas mais intuitivo e facilita o cadastramento de impressões digitais.
Voltando para o aspecto da animação, agora há um recurso de acessibilidade que reduz os efeitos de movimento para quem sente desconforto com isso.
O Ubuntu 26.10 é baseado no Linux 7.3. Talvez isso cause estranheza porque essa ainda não é uma versão oficial — até o momento, a mais recente é o kernel Linux 7.2. Mas ela está aqui porque a distribuição foi baseada em uma versão release candidate (de pré-lançamento) do Linux 7.3, que deve ser anunciado oficialmente em 18 de outubro.
Pois bem, o Linux 7.3 avança no suporte a futuros processadores AMD com arquitetura Zen 6, aprimora a compatibilidade com chips Intel Panther Lake, oferece suporte inicial para chips da família Apple M3, otimiza o desempenho de sistemas de arquivos como Btrfs, Ext4 e XFS, promove ajustes de desempenho em jogos quando há pouca memória de vídeo, entre outros recursos.
A nova versão da distribuição também atualiza os apps nativos, é claro. É o caso do gerenciador de arquivos Files, oriundo do Gnome 51, que agora exibe a quantidade de arquivos que foram selecionados durante uma operação de arrastar e soltar.
Já o visualizador de documentos Papers, também do Gnome 51, passou a facilitar a inserção de assinaturas manuais em PDFs, podendo até remover o fundo de imagens que trazem uma assinatura digitalizada.
Outro destaque vai para o App Center que, além de facilitar a instalação ou a atualização de numerosos aplicativos, também possibilita que o usuário encontre determinados drivers proprietários, desde que o computador em uso precise deles (se eles não aparecem para você, significa que o seu PC já conta com os melhores drivers).
Entre as demais novidades do Ubuntu 26.10 estão:
A previsão é a de que a versão final do Ubuntu 26.10 “Stonking Stingray” seja lançada em 15 de outubro. No momento, você pode baixar a versão beta da distribuição, que serviu de base para este texto (o mesmo link trará a versão final após o anúncio oficial).
Em todos os casos, use uma ferramenta como o Rufus para criar um pendrive de instalação ou de teste.
Para quem não curte o Gnome, vale relembrar que o Ubuntu possui “sabores” baseados em outros ambientes de desktop, e todos (ou a maior parte deles) devem ser atualizados. São exemplos o Kubuntu (KDE Plasma), o Lubuntu (LXQt) e o Ubuntu Mate.

articles.title: AMD RDNA 5 Likely Scheduled for Second Half of 2027
articles.text:
Monday, October 12th 2026
AMD RDNA 5 Likely Scheduled for Second Half of 2027
AMD's next-generation gaming graphics cards featuring the RDNA 5 GPU architecture are unlikely to debut before the second half of 2027, according to well-known hardware leaker Kepler_L2. The leaker suggests that AMD is unlikely to release any RDNA 5 desktop graphics cards before Computex 2027, indicating that these GPUs will probably arrive in the latter half of that year. AMD is expected to lead with the silicon codenamed "AT2," which is part of a family of discrete RDNA 5 GPUs. This will be followed by "AT0," "AT3," and "AT4," which are expected to launch a few quarters later in 2028. Since "AT2" likely refers to a mid-range design, AMD might begin its rollout with a mid-range GPU first, followed by flagship and lower-end models in 2028.
Previously, we learned that AMD's RDNA 5 GPUs will incorporate GDDR7 memory with unknown capacities, as GDDR7 is now listed among the supported VRAM types in the AMDGPU driver. Currently, AMD's graphics cards use GDDR6 for the consumer RDNA 4-based Radeon RX 9000 series, while Instinct MI data center and workstation GPUs use HBM3E and HBM4 memory. Since AMD is developing data center GPUs with HBM and consumer cards are the only models using GDDR, the GDDR7 placeholder suggests future support for RDNA 5.Additional details reveal that the Display Core Next (DCN) 6 display engine, responsible for display output, image scaling, monitor ratio output, and pixel manipulation, will debut in version 6 for RDNA 5. With DCN 6, AMD has introduced new scaling integrity and cost surfaces, a UPSP pre-scaler to sample 4:2:0 and 4:2:2 content before scaling, and new pixel formats within the display logic. This means the final GPU will support modern high-refresh and high-resolution gaming across various aspect ratios and configurations, ensuring smooth content delivery.

articles.title: Coder creates NvidiaWatch tracker site that monitors hundreds of GPU driver bugs — site charts open issues, fixes, and forum feedback across updates
articles.text:
Coder creates NvidiaWatch tracker site that monitors hundreds of GPU driver bugs — site charts open issues, fixes, and forum feedback across updates
This page aggregates Nvidia's driver updates to make issues easier to track.
A GitHub programmer has created an Nvidia bug tracker page that compiles each driver update’s release notes and feedback threads on the forums, logging progress on 462 different driver bugs. They first shared their creation, called NvidiaWatch, in late September and then released an update on the r/Nvidia subreddit earlier this week.
The programmer said that each bug gets its own page, meaning anyone affected by it could easily track if the latest driver update has already solved the issue. Each driver update also gets a dedicated page that includes the release notes, fixed bugs, and open issues that Nvidia couldn’t address yet. The creator also added a chart that tracks the number of known issues that were fixed during that release, fixed in a later release, remained open, and those that were carried over from an earlier driver release.
This website is quite useful for anyone running into issues with their Nvidia hardware, as they’d be able to track whether their problem has already been recognized by the company and whether it has done something about it. It’s also a good idea for anyone wanting to update the driver on their GPU to consult NvidiaWatch first; that way, they could avoid some nasty surprises like the fan control bug that came with the GeForce 595.59 driver.
Hopefully, someone could create a similar update but for Windows updates. A website like WindowsWatch would absolutely be useful, especially as the Microsoft operating system has a lot more users than Nvidia GPUs. This would help savvy users determine if an update is problematic, allowing them to roll back or pause updates before they encounter an issue, while also making Microsoft’s notes easier to understand for the layperson. Having a trend graph could also pressure Microsoft to fix issues much more quickly, as users could now see the number of problems piling up between fixes. This would be a bit complicated, though, especially as there are many different Windows versions, with some updates only affecting a few versions.

articles.title: Le HomePod avec écran ne s'appelle pas HomePad : voici le nom qu'Apple aurait choisi
articles.text:
Il y a quelques jours, Apple donnait rendez-vous pour un événement ce mardi 13 octobre, avec l’arrivée de nouveaux produits. Alors que nous en sommes la veille, on apprend quelques détails autour du HomePod avec écran qui serait présenté. C’est Mark Gurman, journaliste Bloomberg toujours bien au courant des projets d’Apple, qui les a révélés dans sa newsletter Power On.
HomeView : le nom d’un HomePod avec écran, et d’un écosystème
C’est le produit le plus important de ce nouvel écosystème domotique que souhaiterait lancer Apple : un HomePod avec écran. Ou plus basiquement, une enceinte connectée dotée d’un écran qui permette de gérer ses objets connectés, écouter de la musique, pourquoi pas regarder des films ou des séries. Ce HomePod serait baptisé « HomeView », un nom découvert par MacRumors grâce à un dépôt de marque réalisé par une société écran. Il serait équipé d’une puce A18, qu’on trouve dans tous les iPhone 16, sauf les modèles Pro. Un nombre limité d’applications seraient prises en charge et l’App Store n’y serait pas présent.
On s’attend à ce que le HomeView propose une meilleure qualité audio que le HomePod mini mis à jour. Ce dernier gagnerait une puce S10 qui améliorerait le contrôle vocal et la qualité audio. Cette enceinte connectée avec écran se déclinerait en deux versions : l’une pour être posée sur une table, l’autre pour être fixée sur un mur. Quatre coloris seraient disponibles : gris sidéral, argent, crème et rose. La version murale serait uniquement vendue dans les coloris gris sidéral et argent. Arrivée prévue en magasin mi-novembre selon Bloomberg.
Ce qu’on attend d’autres pour ces annonces d’Apple autour de la maison connectée
En 2014, Apple lançait HomeKit, son écosystème domotique intégré à iOS. Deux ans plus tard, c’était l’arrivée de l’application Home sur l’iPhone. L’année d’après, c’était l’arrivée du HomePod. Mais depuis, ni l’écosystème domotique d’Apple, ni ses produits, ni son assistant vocal pour les gérer (Siri), n’ont su s’imposer dans le grand public. Amazon avec Alexa et Google avec Google Assistant, puis Gemini, ont su s’en sortir un peu mieux. Produits moins chers, partenariats plus nombreux, gammes d’objets connectées très larges… les explications sont nombreuses. Apple a probablement été plus timide que ses concurrents et joue donc gros sur ces annonces ce 13 octobre.
En plus du HomeView, on s’attend à ce que la marque annonce des objets connectés conçus en partenariat avec LG et Schneider : serrure connectée, caméra de surveillance, thermostat, capteurs, etc. En plus de ça, Apple lancerait un nouvel HomePod mini ou encore une nouvelle Apple TV 4K (avec une puce A19). Malheureusement, tous ces nouveaux produits fonctionneraient grâce à Siri AI, qui n’est pas disponible en Europe. Ce qui signifie qu’il est possible que ces produits ne soient pas disponibles chez nous. Et le mois d’Apple n’est pas terminé : la marque s’apprêterait à sortir les nouveaux MacBook Pro avec écran Oled.

articles.title: Lo único que está construyendo Estados Unidos ahora mismo son centros de datos
articles.text:
La inteligencia artificial y todo lo que se mueve en torno a ella se ha convertido en una gran promesa en la que las big tech están vertiendo enormes cantidades de dinero. Y en el caso de Estados Unidos, la economía es cada vez más dependiente de la IA. Un dato: el gasto en centros de datos, hardware y redes ya supone el 0,8% de su PIB en el primer trimestre del año, según datos de Epoch AI.
Parte de esa inversión en datacenters y cálculo es física: infraestructuras y edificios que alguien tiene que construir. Y si el PIB ya evidencia el peso de la IA en la economía estadounidense, la construcción es una auténtica bofetada de realidad.
Esa obra es un centro de datos. El inversor y periodista económico Steve Rattner ha elaborado un gráfico con los datos del U.S. Census Bureau que lo ilustra bien: mientras el conjunto del resto de la construcción privada retrocede, el gasto en centros de datos sigue creciendo.
Desde diciembre de 2023, el gasto en construir centros de datos ha pasado de unos 24.000 millones de dólares a más de 75.000 millones al año en julio de 2026: unos 51.000 millones más. Mientras, en ese mismo periodo el gasto en construir todo lo demás bajó 120.000 millones. Desde 2024, el Census Bureau muestra con todo el sentido del mundo los centros de datos por separado dentro de la construcción de oficinas porque unidos, distorsionan la imagen del sector.
Lo que no dice el gráfico. Ojo, insistimos: no son beneficios empresariales, sino inversión inyectada en construir infraestructura. Vaya por delante algo: mide la evolución del gasto en ese periodo, no el dinero acumulado, y solo recoge la obra in situ.
UN VISTAZO A...
Quedan fuera servidores, chips y redes, que suponen la mayor parte del coste: la construcción ronda el 20 % del total, según una estimación de Cushman & Wakefield recogida por Axios. Mención especial merece ese "todo lo demás", porque además de oficinas y otras industrias incluye también la vivienda privada. Ese es otro melón pendiente de abrir.
¿En una burbuja?. En abril de 2026 el gasto en construcción de centros de datos ya superó a las oficinas tradicionales por primera vez: 50.700 millones del primero frente a 43.800 de las segundas, según datos del Census recogidos por Data Center Knowledge. Desde entonces, la brecha ha seguido creciendo: las líneas azul y roja cada vez aparecen más separadas.
La cartera de proyectos es enorme: la consultora global JLL cifra en 66 GW la capacidad total de centros de datos en construcción en EEUU, con una ocupación del 99%. Y a ese ritmo, no es de extrañar que cueste encontrar un carpintero o un electricista: están todos construyendo centros de datos. Y el beneficio está concentrado en pocas empresas, las hyperscalers, que también se encuentran con escollos como el consumo energético, la oposición local o la burocracia.
Por qué importa. Porque refleja cuánto se invierte en infraestructura para la IA, una apuesta en la que big tech e inversores han volcado enormes cantidades de dinero. En la construcción de EEUU, es hoy el principal sostén: según la patronal AGC, solo los datacenter, energía y carreteras mantienen a flote el gasto total en construcción. Y la dependencia crece. ¿El problema? Que si retiramos los centros de datos de la ecuación, el mercado de la construcción se vería mucho más débil. De hecho, pese al boom de los centros de datos en el sector privado, el gasto total en construcción cayó un 3,8 % en julio respecto a 2025, arrastrado por el parón en la vivienda y las oficinas tradicionales.
Esa fragilidad se extiende a la economía. Deutsche Bank señala que la inversión empresarial ajena a la IA lleva plana desde 2019. Sin el motor de la IA y con un mercado laboral frágil, una caída en la inversión se traduciría en que la economía estadounidense probablemente acabaría en recesión. El economista de Harvard Jason Furman dejaba hace casi un año en X/Twitter un hilo para reflexionar sobre el tema y este comentario: sin el boom de la IA, probablemente no habría crecimiento nulo porque habría tipos de interés y precios de electricidad más bajos que impulsarían otros sectores.
Portada | O'Leary Digital

articles.title: Il ne reste que quelques heures pour avoir le dernier Fire TV Stick 4K Max à moitié prix !
articles.text:
Le Fire TV Stick 4 Max dernière génération est un boîtier HDMI compact qui se branche sur un écran pour en faire un TV connecté, et jusqu’à ce soir il est à 52,99 euros au lieu de 114,99 euros sur Amazon.
Le Fire TV Stick 4K Max dernière génération est un boîtier HDMI qui se branche sur votre téléviseur pour profiter d’une interface connectée Fire TV. Alors à l’heure où tous les téléviseurs sont quasiment connectés, l’intérêt peut paraître limité. Mais en vérité, si votre TV commence à être vieillissante, si la navigation n’est plus fluide ou si vous trouvez l’OS trop limité, ça peut être une bonne alternative. Avec l’avantage de pouvoir le brancher sur n’importe quel appareil qui diffuse des images, comme un vidéoprojecteur, un écran PC ou autre. Avec une réduction de 54 % sur Amazon jusqu’à ce soir, ça peut servir d’en avoir un sous la main.
Le Fire TV Stick 4K Max est à 52,99 € au lieu de 114,99 € sur Amazon
Pourquoi choisir le Fire TV Stick 4K Max ?
- L’interface est fluide peut importe où vous le branchez, un vrai avantage par rapport à un TV qui commence à avoir de l'âge.
- Le streaming est impeccable avec la puce Wi-Fi 6 qui permet une connexion stable, indispensable pour profiter des contenus 4K HDR et Dolby Atmos.
- La simplicité de l’écosystème Alexa si vous avez d’autres appareils qui fonctionnent avec Alexa, vous pouvez tout contrôler à la voix grâce à la télécommande.
Une expérience multimédia dopée sous contrôle Amazon
Le Fire TV Stick est un petit boîtier qui fait 108 x 30 x 14 mm avec le connecteur, pour seulement 43,5 g. Il se branche très simplement sur n’importe quel appareil qui peut afficher/diffuser une image. Il est capable d’afficher de la 4K@60 FPS avec un support HDR10+ et Dolby Vision. Si vous avez les abonnements qui vont bien sur les différentes plateformes de streaming, c’est un vrai plaisir. Après, il y a un petit revers à la médaille : le contenu est un peu trop centré Amazon, avec beaucoup de pubs pour du contenu Prime Video et des recommandations sponsorisées qui peuvent alourdir un peu la navigation et pas mal d’incitations à l’achat.
Face au Chromecast : la puissance brute contre l’ouverture
En termes de puissance, le Fire TV Stick 4K Max dernière génération est au-dessus de ce que propose Google avec son Chromecast, avec sa puce Mediatek MT8696 et sa compatibilité Wi-Fi 6. Mais son catalogue d’applications est moins exhaustif que celui de Google TV, notamment sur certaines chaînes sportives majeures. Le Chromecast est donc plus polyvalent et neutre dans sa présentation et son interface, là où, on l’a dit au-dessus, le Fire TV 4K Max assume son rôle de vitrine commerciale Amazon.
✅ Les points forts
- L’intégration du Wi-Fi 6 pour de bonnes performances réseau
- La compatibilité avec les formats HDR et Dolby Atmos
- La télécommande améliorée avec des commandes vocales Alexa et des raccourcis dédiés
- L'expérience de navigation fluide et réactive
- Une bibliothèque d’apps riche malgré tout
❌ Les limites
- La mise en avant omniprésente des services et contenus Amazon
- L'absence de certaines apps clés comme RMC Sports ou Bein Sports
- La connexion micro-USB vieillissante, à quand l’USB-C ?
Jusqu’à ce soir, le Fire TV Stick 4K Max est à 52,99 € au lieu de 114,99 € sur Amazon
Le Fire TV Stick 4K Max est un bon investissement si vous cherchez une clé HDMI réactive pour stabiliser un flux vidéo 4K sur n’importe quel écran. Si vous n’avez rien contre l’écosystème Amazon ou si vous souhaitez rajeunir l’OS vieillissant de votre TV actuelle sans trop dépenser, c’est un bon investissement.
Par contre, si vous préférez une interface épurée ou que vous aimez avoir la possibilité d'applications alternatives, hors Store, il faudrait plutôt partir du côté du Chromecast. Idem si vous souhaitez pouvoir caster nativement, sans télécharger d’applications alternatives.

articles.title: On a vu Below, la meilleure série horrifique Netflix du moment pour Halloween 2026 ?
articles.text:
Pendant que la télévision américaine s’épuise à recycler ses vieux monstres à coups de millions de dollars, le Canada confirme son grand retour sur le devant de la scène sérielle. Avec l’aide de Netflix, le but est de ressusciter un genre qu’on croyait réservé aux vidéos du samedi soir : le film de monstre marin. Mais sous ses airs de divertissement du week-end, Below cache une ambition bien plus sombre qu’il n’y paraît.
Un décor grandiose, des accents savoureux et une charge sociale percutante pour Below
Installée dans le village de pêcheurs fictif de Snook’s Arm à Terre-Neuve, la série s’ouvre sur les célébrations de la « Come Home Week », cette semaine où les anciens résidents partis chercher fortune ailleurs reviennent au pays. Mais Snook’s Arm n’est pas un village comme les autres : décimé dans les années 1980 par un programme gouvernemental de relocalisation forcée, le hameau fait aujourd’hui face à une deuxième vague d’expulsion, orchestrée par l’État et des multinationales gourmandes.
Au milieu de cette tempête politique se dresse Calvin Penney (Josh Hartnett), un pêcheur au visage buriné qui refuse catégoriquement d’abandonner ses terres. Traumatisé par la noyade de son père 40 ans plus tôt lors du premier déménagement forcé, Calvin gagne sa vie en découpant des blocs de glace sur des glaciers dérivés pour les revendre à des distilleries de vodka. Mais lorsqu’un iceberg massif et mystérieusement contaminé s’échoue dans la baie, la routine bascule. Calvin y fait une découverte glaçante aux côtés de la scientifique Fonda Howander (Mackenzie Davis) : une créature colossale, réveillée par le réchauffement et les perturbations écologiques, rode sous les eaux. Une bête que Calvin a déjà croisée du regard dans sa jeunesse, un œil incandescent de la taille d’une roue de camion, le jour où son père a coulé.
C’est incontestablement dans cette dimension que Below brille le plus. Sublimée par la photographie hypnotique de William Baldy et la bande-son de Mark Korven, la série capte à merveille la beauté sauvage et la précarité des communautés rurales canadiennes. Le véritable effroi ne vient pas seulement des profondeurs maritimes, mais de l’intrusion toxique de conglomérats technologiques et de milliardaires venus racheter la mémoire d’un peuple.
Sur le plan de l’interprétation, le casting s’en donne à cœur joie. Josh Hartnett, affublé de ses bonnets de marin, s’investit à 200 %. À ses côtés, Mackenzie Davis apporte une rigueur scientifique bienvenue, tandis que Charlie Heaton (Stranger Things), libéré de son rôle de teenager apathique, incarne Wade, le fils dévoué, avec l’énergie d’un labrador enthousiaste.
Des sous-intrigues parasites et un monstre bien trop timide
Malheureusement, dès que l’on gratte la surface du drame insulaire pour chercher les frissons promis par le genre, le bat blesse. Below souffre d’un mal récurrent des productions sérielles Netflix : l’étirement artificiel du récit. Pour meubler ses six épisodes de 35 minutes, la série empile les sous-intrigues de mélodrame familial dispensables. Entre la fille de Calvin qui ramène un petit ami bourgeois en ville, le plus jeune fils étranglé par des dettes auprès de petits voyous locaux, et les secrets de polichinelle du village, le rythme s’essouffle régulièrement. Alors que le tout devrait se concentrer sur l’essentiel : l’horreur pure.
Pire encore, les scénaristes multiplient les artifices narratifs bancals pour justifier la menace. L’iceberg toxique libère ainsi une substance qui empoisonne les habitants, leur infligeant une soif inextinguible, des cicatrices étranges et des hallucinations collectives. Une surcharge d’éléments qui vient parasiter le cœur du sujet.
Mais le vrai problème de Below reste la gestion de sa créature. Après nous avoir mis l’eau à la bouche en montrant un orignal entier traîné sous l’eau et dévoré tout cru, la série joue la carte de la retenue extrême. Manque cruel de budget pour les effets spéciaux ou volonté déplacée de faire de la « noble » dramaturgie ? Le géant des mers, qu’il s’agisse d’un poulpe préhistorique ou d’un calmar mutant, reste désespérément invisible la majeure partie du temps.
Certes, la série s’offre un moment de bravoure mémorable lors d’un épisode claustrophobe où Calvin se retrouve piégé dans un sous-marin de fortune éclairé aux néons rouges, tentant de baliser la bête sous l’océan. La petitesse des décors et le bricolage visuel apportent un charme indéniable qui rappelle le cinéma de genre d’antan. Mais en dehors de ces rares fulgurances, le spectateur reste sur sa faim de terreur tentaculaire.
Le verdict
Below
Voir la fiche
On a aimé
- L’ambiance
- Le sous-texte social
- La photographie
On a moins aimé
- Trop de longueurs
- Des intrigues parfois inutiles

articles.title: GPT, Claude und Grok sollen einen Toyota steuern: Ein KI-Modell besteht den Test
articles.text:
Entwickler lassen GPT, Claude und Grok einen Toyota fahren: So lief der Test
Hinter der Steuerung autonom fahrender Autos stecken normalerweise speziell dafür trainierte Algorithmen. Drei Entwickler des Startups Axiom haben jetzt aber die großen Sprachmodelle von OpenAI, Anthropic und X.ai ans Steuer eines Fahrzeugs gelassen – ohne entsprechendes Training.
GPT, Claude und Grok fahren Auto
Und GPT, Claude und Grok haben das Auto tatsächlich durch einen Test-Parcours gesteuert – wenn auch mit unterschiedlichem Erfolg, wie Wired berichtet. Dabei sind die KI-Systeme eigentlich dafür vorgesehen, Text und Code zu generieren oder Bilder zu erstellen.
„Vielleicht ist ja die AGI doch schon da“, so einer der Entwickler, der damit auf die sogenannte Superintelligenz anspielt, die jede Aufgabe auf menschlichem Niveau ausführen können soll. Dafür gibt es allerdings noch keine belegbaren Beweise. Immerhin zeigt das Experiment aber, dass Sprachmodelle beginnen, ein rudimentäres Verständnis der physischen Welt zu erlangen.
Training der KI-Modelle als Basis
Die Basis dafür könnte im Training der KI-Systeme liegen, für das mittlerweile neben Bildern und Videos auch 3D-Modelle herangezogen werden, so die Entwickler. Derweil mussten sie GPT, Claude und Grok erst überzeugen, die Steuerung des Fahrzeugs zu übernehmen. Zunächst verweigerten sich die KI-Modelle der Aufgabe. Welche konkreten Prompts sie verwendeten, verrieten die Forscher nicht.
Ihren Versuchsaufbau haben sie unter dem Namen Driving-Bench aber via GitHub zum Download bereitgestellt. Mit dem entsprechenden Code sowie zusätzlichen Tools und Kameras soll es den Forschern zufolge möglich sein, selbst ein großes Sprachmodell zum Steuern eines Fahrzeugs zu bringen.
GPT-6 Astra schlägt die KI-Konkurrenz
In den Tests der Axiom-Forscher kristallisierte sich übrigens ein klarer Sieger heraus, was die Fahrfähigkeiten angeht. GPT-6 Astra absolvierte den Test-Parcours mit einem Toyota Corolla zwar langsam, aber zu 100 Prozent.
Claude Fable 5.1 schaffte das Ganze immerhin zu 45 Prozent. Grok 4.6 und GPT-5.6 Sol mussten sich mit elf beziehungsweise sechs Prozent derweil geschlagen geben.

articles.title: African AI startups need more than prompts to win VC money
articles.text:
Artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped how the world works, and African AI startups, venture capital and tech ecosystems are no exception. The technology is evolving so fast that many investors are still working out how to evaluate AI startups, let alone how to fund them.
Over the past six months, this column has spoken to African investors across regions, sectors, and funding stages about where AI creates genuine value, where it falls short, and what merits institutional capital.
They are Babacar Seck, founder of Askya Investment Partners; Eloho Omame, partner at TLcom Capital; Emmanuel Adegboye, head of Madica; Magnifique Ishimwe, fund manager at the Development Bank of Rwanda; Husein Merchant, investment officer at Village Capital; and Benjamin Toulouze, head of corporate venture capital at AXIAN Investment.
When we asked them what makes an AI startup fundable, they mostly described something an AI model itself cannot supply. Anyone can build on the same foundational models now, so investors are paying for what sits around them: voice products that work in Wolof and isiZulu, software tied so deeply into a customer’s systems that leaving is painful, licences that take years to win, and revenue.
Voice is where they see the clearest opening. Adegboye says the opportunity lies in building on top of foundational models with local data, and above all in voice. He points to a man who speaks only Wolof: what is the easiest way for him to take part in an economy increasingly run by software?
Seck makes the same point about South Africa, where census data shows only 8.7% of citizens speak English at home.
Building software has also never been cheaper, and the number of AI startups has climbed as costs have fallen. TechCabal Insights counted 207 African AI startups across 17 countries in 2025, roughly double the 104 it tracked in 2022. Most of the newest ones work in software development, business intelligence, finance and education, the areas where off-the-shelf models lowered the barrier most.
When code is cheap, investors look for what rivals cannot copy. Eloho Omame of TLcom Capital compares this moment to the arrival of mobile technology in Africa. Once it becomes easy to build the thing, she says, companies defend themselves in other ways: brand, network effects, and the cost to a customer of pulling out software that runs their business.
The following responses are drawn from a series of interviews TechCabal conducted with investors between April and September 2026. They have been curated by theme and edited for length and clarity.
Why context is an advantage
Local context decides whether an AI tool works in Africa. Founders who have it can build for specific problems, as Pewbeam AI has done with software that projects Bible verses during live church services, and as YarnGPT has done with a speech model for Nigerian-accented English, Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa. They can also make something as viral as Lagos Life.
Of the 207 African AI startups TechCabal Insights counted across 17 countries in 2025, two-thirds are still early stage and only eight have reached maturity. When that many companies can plug into the same foundation models, saying a product is AI-powered proves very little.
That changes what investors ask founders. If AI keeps making software cheaper to write, software on its own protects nothing. What matters is everything around it: data nobody else holds, local knowledge, a way to reach customers, regulatory permission, and how deeply the product sits inside the work a customer already does.
Merchant of Village Capital, whose fund has not yet looked at AI as a sector, expects most of the African opportunity to sit at the application layer.
Husein Merchant (Village Capital): My personal opinion is that there is going to be a lot of opportunity on the consumer side. Given that Africa may be more of a consumer of AI technology than a creator of it, I think the investments and solutions will lean that way.
Eloho Omame (TLcom Capital): AI does not make everything cheaper to build. It is not a panacea. Some things are cheaper. Testing is cheaper, so you can experiment far more quickly with LLMs than before. Whenever a technology has driven down the cost of delivering something, the shape of defensibility has changed. A company could no longer rely on a high cost of entry. AI has lowered the cost of entry the way mobile technology lowered it before. When we look at a company, we ask how it builds defensibility if testing or delivery is now commoditised. It might be the brand. It might be network effects or switching costs.
Data and language
Seck splits AI startups in two. One group builds the layers of AI itself. The other applies AI to ordinary businesses, and that is where he sees an opening for Africa.
Speech data for African languages is scarce. A company that collects it, trains on it, and builds a customer base around what it can do with it owns something rivals cannot easily copy. Caantin, a Zambian startup that replaces call-centre staff with AI voice agents for banks and fintechs, told TechCabal in June 2025 it was approaching $1 million in monthly revenue, charging by the volume of calls it handles.
No one has fully cracked it yet.
Babacar Seck (Askya Investment Partners): Wherever you have structured data at scale, you can build small AI models that improve performance. That is exciting in the African context because we are digitising in the age of AI. We are creating structured pools of data at the same time as we apply AI to them, so companies build a competitive advantage much faster as they scale. Language is the clearest case of data that is hard to copy. In South Africa, Census 2022 found that 8.7% of people speak English most often at home. IsiZulu (24.4%), isiXhosa (16.3%), Afrikaans (10.6%) and Sepedi (10%) all rank above it. A product that only works in English is built for a small slice of that market.
Babacar Seck (Askya Investment Partners): One very exciting area is voice AI in African languages. Many startups operate in that space, and none have fully cracked it. Today in Africa, most people do not speak English, French, or Portuguese at home. They speak their mother tongue, the language they are most comfortable in. The minute you have an application that lets companies talk to their customers in the customer’s own language, you bridge a divide. That applies to companies and their customers, and to governments and their citizens.
Emmanuel Adegboye (Madica): I think daily about people in rural areas. What is the easiest way to take part in the global economy if you only speak Wolof? The fastest way is to build platforms that speak Wolof or deliver information in Wolof, so you can do all of that without needing to learn English. That is why I think voice is an important long-term opportunity in AI, and it is why some of our investments have been in voice AI.
Being one with the customer
Omame’s portfolio has shown her a second kind of defence: a company that sits inside a customer’s daily operations. Once its software is wired into thousands of end customers, a rival cannot easily replace it, and the margin that integration earns is protected with it.
Eloho Omame (TLcom Capital): We invested in an API infrastructure business. Its API plugs into its customers’ software and delivers a fintech product. Before, each time the customer needed the product, it made an API call. Now, because of agentic technology, the system prompts the customer when they are about to run out of the resource they lease. Revenue goes up, and the company also knows its revenue is going up. The product also costs less to deliver, because there is an agentic layer on the production side too.
In principle more people can now build what it builds, as cheaply as it can. But once our software is talking to each other and I am delivering value across thousands of your own customers, it is much harder for you to unplug from my system.
I want a clear line of sight to how AI makes the product cheaper to create, and what happens to the margin that creates. The founder can pass it all to the customer or capture it in the business as a higher margin. As an investor, I want to see it captured in the business.
Revenue comes first
Defensibility answers only half the question. The other half is whether the company earns money while investors are still willing to wait, and on this continent the wait has shortened.
An AI company that spends three years on compute before charging anyone fails that test, however good the idea.
Magnifique Ishimwe (Development Bank of Rwanda): Basic technology can always be built. I could put together an app like the one I showed you by the next morning. The fundamental question is whether you can execute.
I have done a couple of AI deals, and sometimes we cannot see when the company reaches its horizon. You can absorb two or three equity rounds, and we still do not see a path to profitability. In the United States you can be an Uber that loses money for six, eight, or ten years. In Africa, every investor asks where your revenue is, and if you do not have it, what value you have in its place.
Think of an AI company that builds a chatbot for students, but nobody is willing to pay for it. You spent a lot on compute, we helped you get credits, you paid expensive engineers, and for three years nothing came out of it. Those deals are misaligned with our instrument, because we are not an equity investor.
Some investors back AI infrastructure
Some investors do fund the deeper layers, usually for strategic reasons. AXIAN, the Madagascar-based group with telecoms and digital banking operations, frames its infrastructure bets around who controls the data.
Benjamin Toulouze (AXIAN Investment): We want to invest in AI infrastructure, and we have already done so. One example is WideBot AI, a proprietary LLM system for Arabic speakers. We invested in Nucleon Security, a Moroccan company that protects devices using zero trust, EDR, and malware tools.
We are convinced about the sovereignty issue. African countries need autonomy and control over their own data. That is one of the biggest challenges in the African market, because it is fragmented across 54 countries.
Emmanuel Adegboye (Madica): There is also an opportunity in hardware and AI. That is the bet we are making with ChipMango and chip design, and we will see how it evolves.
Madica joined ChipMango’s $1.9 million seed round, led by Atlantica Ventures, in September 2026. Even these bets follow the same logic as the rest of the column. WideBot’s edge is Arabic dialect data and a book of more than 350 government and enterprise clients. ChipMango recruits engineers through partnerships with Nigerian universities, trains them and sells chip-design work to global customers. In each case the hard thing to copy is the data, the talent pipeline or the customer list.
The cost of inaction in AI investing
If African investors back only the application layer, the deeper layers of AI will be financed, built and owned elsewhere. Global capital is already moving that way.
Capital is not the only gap. African data centres are chasing customers while the continent says it needs more of them, and universities are training AI engineers who leave for jobs abroad.
Emmanuel Adegboye (Madica): Capital is concentrating in a handful of funds and a handful of startups. Most funding globally is going to AI infrastructure companies, and only a few of those. On top of that, most of the funding coming into Africa comes from outside Africa, which exposes the continent to that risk. If I am a Silicon Valley investor who is not close to the continent, Africa is not top of mind when I invest.
Babacar Seck (Askya Investment Partners): Most data centres are chasing customers, yet we keep saying Africa does not have enough data centres. One gap is that these operators are not plugged into demand. When you speak to the global cloud players, they will tell you their biggest customers in Africa are startups, with some scale-ups spending upwards of $30 million a year on cloud.
We are training a growing number of AI engineers at Carnegie Mellon in Kigali, at the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences, and at some very good Nigerian universities, and many of them find jobs abroad because the companies on the continent are not yet large enough to keep them.
For now, the investors in this column have answered the question they can control. They will pay for the parts of an AI company that grow more valuable as the AI underneath gets cheaper. Whether the continent also builds that underlying layer is a question their capital cannot settle on its own.
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. articles.title: “Inédit et d'une extrême gravité” : des pirates ont programmé les frigos de supermarchés français à 50°C
articles.text:
“Inédit et d'une extrême gravité” : des pirates ont programmé les frigos de supermarchés français à 50°C
Dans la nuit du 11 au 12 octobre 2026, une cyberattaque a détourné la régulation frigorifique Danfoss de nombreux magasins Intermarché, E.Leclerc et U, les congélateurs se muant en étuves. Rien qu'à Haguenau, deux enseignes chiffrent la casse à 270 000 € et l'addition nationale pourrait se compter en millions.
Lundi matin, à l'ouverture des portes vitrées, des employés de supermarché ont reçu un souffle tiède en plein visage, là où devait régner un froid polaire. D'après les révélations de BFM Business, des pirates ont pris la main pendant la nuit sur les systèmes de régulation du fabricant danois Danfoss. Ces systèmes pilotent les meubles froids de magasins Intermarché, E.Leclerc et Coopérative U. Une source du secteur avance le chiffre d'environ 150 points de vente Intermarché touchés.
Je confirme qu’une cyberattaque touche depuis cette nuit les installations de production de froid de plusieurs magasins de notre réseau @CooperativeU.
Nos équipes sont pleinement mobilisées, en lien avec les frigoristes, pour rétablir la situation au plus vite. Une enquête devra…
— Dominique Schelcher (@schelcher) October 12, 2026
Cyberattaque Danfoss : comment un dégivrage forcé a ruiné les rayons surgelés
Les assaillants ont retourné une fonction de protection contre ceux qu'elle devait servir. Les installations frigorifiques se dégivrent automatiquement — par exemple 2 h par tranche de 24 h — pour chasser le givre des évaporateurs. Selon BFM, les pirates auraient imposé un dégivrage continu avec une consigne réglée à 50 °C. Là où l'attaque a démarré vers minuit, les résistances ont chauffé des heures durant. Un bac à glaces affichait encore 26 °C lundi. Dans les magasins touchés plus tard, les équipes ont pu sauver une partie des denrées.
À Haguenau (Bas-Rhin), l'Intermarché aurait perdu tous ses surgelés, soit environ 50 000 €. Le E.Leclerc voisin aurait jeté ses surgelés, ainsi que ses produits frais, pour une perte estimée à quelque 220 000 €.
	
Dans les pires des cas, cela a pu conduire à jeter tous les produits frais.
Supermarchés piratés : des versions obsolètes du logiciel dans le viseur
L'offensive viserait des éditions du logiciel de régulation Danfoss antérieures à la version 4. Ce logiciel équipe une large part du parc français. Des magasins Metro et des boucheries indépendantes pourraient, eux aussi, figurer parmi les victimes. Une réunion de crise réunissait lundi à 11h Danfoss et plusieurs frigoristes, dont Axima.
La fragilité de ces automates était connue, puisqu'en mai 2025, l'agence étasunienne de cybersécurité avait signalé une faille d'authentification dans les superviseurs Danfoss AK-SM 800A antérieurs à la version R4.2 (avis de la CISA).
Les chercheurs de Claroty avaient ensuite recensé 2765 de ces interfaces exposées sur Internet (étude Team82). Aucun élément ne rattache encore formellement ces failles à l'attaque du week-end. Le président de Coopérative U réclame une enquête pour faire toute la lumière.
Suivez toute l'actualité des Numériques sur Google Actualités et sur la chaîne WhatsApp des Numériques
Envie de faire encore plus d'économies ? Découvrez nos codes promo sélectionnés pour vous.
