articles.title: La meilleure feature des Pixel 11 s'invite sur tous les Android grâce à cette app
articles.text:
Les Google Pixel 11 ne sont pas des smartphones très enthousiasmants lorsqu'on les compare à leurs prédécesseurs directs. En revanche, la fonctionnalité "Rambler", exclusive à ces nouveaux modèles, fait figure de game changer. Un petit malin s'est amusé à l'exporter sur tous les mobiles Android du marché.
PixelBoard, c'est son nom, est une application tierce développée par Akshay Kadam et distribuée gratuitement sur GitHub, qui se propose d'apporter la fonction Rambler ainsi que les outils d'écriture intelligente des Pixel 11 à n'importe quel smartphone Android.
- Toujours fan du design
- Un bel écran, plus lumineux
- Des fonctions exclusives intéressantes (Rambler, Téléprompteur)
Les meilleures features des Pixel 11, maintenant sur tous les Android
De quoi parle-t-on exactement ? D'une version modifiée du Gboard de Google, dont les fonctionnalités intelligentes comme Rambler (la dictée vocale dopée par IA) et les outils rédactionnels ont été fondus dans le code, de façon à pouvoir fonctionner sur n'importe quel mobile.
En clair, PixelBoard vient remplacer Gboard sur votre smartphone, et vous permet d'utiliser la nouvelle dictée vocale et les autres fonctions inédites aux Pixel 11 sans plus de cérémonie ou blocage quelconque. Ça fonctionne sur tous les smartphones Android, sur toutes les applis, et ça ne nécessite pas de rooter son téléphone.
Dans un post Reddit, le développeur explique avoir utilisé comme base le Gboard moddé de Jason Wu, un APK déjà prisé par la communauté des bidouilleurs Android. Si l'installation d'un fichier tiers ne provenant pas du Play Store représente évidemment toujours un risque de sécurité, le développeur donne de bons gages de confiance, et assure par ailleurs vouloir maintenir à jour PixelBoard aussi longtemps que possible, en intégrant au fil de l'eau les nouveautés du Gboard officiel.
Un projet en sursis ?
Que le développeur souhaite maintenir son projet à jour est une chose… mais, Google le laissera-t-il faire sans sourciller ? Rien n'est moins sûr. Même si Android est, de fait, une plateforme encore assez ouverte, il est possible que le géant du web voie d'un mauvais œil que l'un des atouts majeurs de sa dernière génération de smartphones lui échappe. Par ailleurs, on sait qu'Android 17 va progressivement serrer la bride sur les applis tierces, et rendre de plus en plus compliquée l'installation de fichiers APK. J'espère me tromper, mais je ne donne pas cher de la peau de PixelBoard dans les prochains mois.
Il faut aussi garder en tête que, même si le développeur assure qu'il calquera les versions de son appli sur celles publiées par Google, la mise à jour d'un APK est loin d'être aussi intuitive qu'une simple pression sur le bouton idoine sur le Play Store. Ici, il faut manuellement re-télécharger le bon fichier pour mettre à jour l'appli. Il est bon de rappeler que l'utilisation d'applications non mises à jour représente un risque de sécurité potentiellement important — à plus forte raison lorsqu'il s'agit du clavier numérique d'un smartphone que l'on tapote à longueur de journée.
Reste que le projet est un joli pied de nez au gatekeeping logiciel toujours plus prononcé chez les constructeurs, qui verrouillent derrière des smartphones hors de prix des fonctions qui, factuellement, peuvent parfaitement s'exécuter sur d'anciens modèles. De quoi s'amuser un peu en attendant le déploiement de Gemini 4, qui ne devrait plus tarder.

articles.title: Mediamarkt verliert vor Gericht: Wer bei defekten Geräten wirklich zuständig ist
articles.text:
Defekte Geräte: Mit dieser beliebten Ausrede kommen Händler nicht mehr durch
Es ist ein Klassiker im Online- und stationären Handel: Wer ein defektes Gerät beim Händler reklamiert, bekommt oftmals gesagt, dass er sich doch bitte direkt an den Hersteller wenden möge, weil man ihm dort schneller helfen könne und man das Gerät ja ohnehin einschicken würde. Doch der Reparaturservice des Herstellers, der sich um solche Probleme kümmern soll, ist in diesem Fall nicht die erste Anlaufstelle, wie ein neues Urteil zeigt.
Klar, für den Händler ist es praktisch, wenn sich die Kund:innen mit dem Service herumärgern müssen, doch für diese bedeutet es oftmals zusätzlichen Aufwand. Es ist aber vor allem rechtlich problematisch, wenn damit die Verantwortung für die gesetzliche Gewährleistung auf den Hersteller abgeschoben werden soll.
Mediamarkt wurde nun seitens des Landgerichts Ingolstadt dieses Vorgehen untersagt. Im Verfahren des Verbraucherzentrale Bundesverbands (vzbv) gegen die MMS E-Commerce GmbH – das ist die Onlinetochter besagter Elektronikmarktkette – entschieden die Richter, dass die Aufforderung gegenüber den Kund:innen, Gewährleistungsansprüche direkt beim Hersteller geltend zu machen, irreführend ist. Das Urteil vom 24. Juli 2026 (Az. 1 HK O 1352/25) wurde in der vergangenen Woche veröffentlicht und ist noch nicht rechtskräftig.
Ein lästig piepsender Kühlschrank
Im konkreten Fall ging es um eine Kühl-Gefrier-Kombination. Die hatte der Kunde gut ein Jahr davor im Mediamarkt-Onlineshop erworben. Das Gerät entwickelte im Laufe der Zeit aber die unangenehme Eigenart, dass der Alarm, der normalerweise vor einer zu lange geöffneten Tür warnt, auch bei geschlossener Tür ausgelöst wurde.
Als sich das nicht mehr abschalten ließ und zu lästig wurde, wandte sich der Kunde daher an Mediamarkt, um im Rahmen der gesetzlichen Gewährleistung eine Lösung zu finden. Mediamarkt verwies ihn daraufhin an den Vor-Ort-Reparaturservice des Herstellers und forderte ihn auf, sich zur Durchsetzung seiner Garantie- beziehungsweise Gewährleistungsansprüche mit diesem direkt auseinanderzusetzen. Die Kontaktdaten finde er im Gerätehandbuch.
Das Gericht befand, die Antwort erwecke den Eindruck, Mediamarkt sei für die Reklamation nicht zuständig. Denn tatsächlich steht bei gesetzlichen Gewährleistungsansprüchen immer zunächst der Verkäufer als Vertragspartner in der Pflicht. Er ist – und darin wurde die Rechtslage bestätigt – Ansprechpartner für den Käufer oder die Käuferin. Dass sich der Kunde in diesem Fall nicht abwimmeln ließ und weiterhin auf eine Abwicklung über Mediamarkt bestand, änderte für das Gericht nichts an der irreführenden Aussage des Unternehmens.
Was das Urteil für den Handel bedeutet
Die Entscheidung betrifft einmal mehr die grundsätzliche Frage im E-Commerce (ebenso wie im Handel vor Ort), wer für die Bearbeitung einer Reklamation verantwortlich ist. Zwar können die Händler durchaus den Hersteller oder einen weiteren externen Dienstleister mit einer Reparatur beauftragen. Allerdings lässt sich daraus nicht ableiten, dass sie ihre gesetzlichen Verpflichtungen gegenüber den Käufern auf diese Unternehmen übertragen könnten.
Doch wie immer geht’s dabei um den Unterschied zwischen Gewährleistung und Garantie. Während sich die gesetzliche Gewährleistung grundsätzlich gegen den Verkäufer richtet und bei Neuwaren im Verbrauchsgüterbereich in aller Regel zwei Jahre beträgt, ist eine zusätzliche Herstellergarantie eine freiwillig eingeräumte Leistung, deren Bedingungen sich nach der jeweiligen Garantieerklärung richten. Entscheidend wäre hier lediglich noch die Beweislastumkehr, die nach einem Jahr in Kraft tritt, aber die ist hier nicht Gegenstand des Falls gewesen.
Das bedeutet, dass Kunden innerhalb der gesetzlichen Voraussetzungen vom Händler Nacherfüllung verlangen können, also eine Reparatur oder Ersatzlieferung. Allerdings kann der Verkäufer die gewählte Form unter bestimmten gesetzlichen Voraussetzungen verweigern. Er darf aber nicht pauschal seine Zuständigkeit abstreiten. Insofern ist das Urteil keine Neuregelung, sondern eher eine Erinnerung an bestehende Pflichten.
Es geht dabei aber vor allem auch um die klaren Hinweise an den Kunden: Reklamationsprozesse, automatisierte Serviceantworten und Hinweise auf Herstellerservices müssen deutlich machen, dass die gesetzlichen Ansprüche gegenüber dem Verkäufer oder der Verkäuferin bestehen bleiben.
Immerhin erklärte eine Mediamarkt-Sprecherin gegenüber Medienvertretern, man respektiere die Entscheidung des Landgerichts und arbeite an der adäquaten Umsetzung. Auf seiner Hilfeseite empfiehlt Mediamarkt bei defekten Großgeräten weiterhin die direkte Kontaktaufnahme mit dem Hersteller und begründet das damit, dass dieser Weg in der Regel schneller sei. Ein solcher Hinweis muss nicht grundsätzlich unzulässig sein, sollte aber im Hinblick auf die nächsten Maßnahmen der Verbraucherschützer nicht ohne Weiteres da stehen. Entscheidend ist nämlich, dass nicht der Eindruck entsteht, Kunden müssten ihre Gewährleistungsrechte beim Hersteller statt beim Händler geltend machen.

Galaxy S26 Plus (512 GB) com tela ampla atinge menor preço desde maio na Amazon • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy S26 Plus (512 GB) com tela ampla atinge menor preço desde maio na Amazon
Samsung Galaxy S26 Plus (512 GB) com tela de 6,7", maior e com mais resolução que a do S26, tem redução de 55% no preço em oferta na Amazon
O Galaxy S26 Plus de 512 GB está saindo por apenas R$ 4.887 no Pix na Amazon. O smartphone premium da Samsung, com tela AMOLED de 120 Hz maior e com mais resolução que o S26 padrão e câmera de 50 MP, alcança o menor preço desde maio de 2026, com desconto de 55% sobre o original de R$ 10.799.
O Galaxy S26 Plus possui uma tela LTPO AMOLED Dinâmico 2X de 6,7″ e resolução de 3.120 x 1440 pixels, maior e mais nítida que a do S26 padrão (6,3″ e 2.340 x 1.080 pixels). A taxa de 120 Hz e o brilho de até 2.600 nits permitem ao display reproduzir cores vibrantes com fluidez e garantir a visibilidade em qualquer lugar.
Seu chip Exynos 2600 e os 12 GB de memória RAM sustentam a execução de apps pesados em multitarefa e soluções do Galaxy AI. Para quem adora fotografar e filmar, os 512 GB de armazenamento disponibilizam espaço interno de sobra.
O kit principal de câmeras grava vídeos em 8K. Ele é composto de uma wide de 50 MP com OIS e uma ultrawide de 12 MP, que captam belas situações em lugares abertos, e uma telefoto de 10 MP com zoom óptico de 3x para aproximações. A frontal de 12 MP tira ótimas selfies e filma em 4K a 60 fps.
O corpo de alumínio do S26 Plus é revestido de ambos os lados pelo vidro Gorilla Glass Victus 2, resistente contra acidentes diversos. Já a certificação IP68 confere proteção extra em cenários como ambientes empoeirados e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 4.900 mAh resiste a até 31 horas de reprodução de vídeo, contra 4.300 mAh e 30 horas da presente no S26, segundo a fabricante. O suporte ao carregamento rápido de 45 W via cabo USB-C e sem fio de 20 W garante o uso por um dia inteiro.
O Galaxy S26 Plus de 512 GB (apenas R$ 4.887 no Pix) será atualizado até o Android 23. O celular da Samsung possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: HyLight raises €13 million for its autonomous airships inspecting Europe's critical infrastructure | EU-Startups
articles.text:
HyLight, the French startup specializing in aerial inspection of critical infrastructure using autonomous hydrogen-powered airships, has just raised €13 million from Rubio Impact Ventures, DRW and Teampact Ventures, joined by existing investors Y Combinator and Ring Capital.
Founded in 2022, the young company has already reached a milestone few industrial startups achieve: designing, building, industrializing and operating its own aircraft in France, while developing the software and artificial intelligence that turn the data they collect into directly actionable insights. In four years, its HyLighters have inspected thousands of kilometers across France, flown in several European countries and begun replacing helicopter missions for major infrastructure operators. The fresh funding will now enable HyLight to scale: industrializing its fleet, strengthening its automated data analysis capabilities and deploying a new data infrastructure across Europe to help monitor and protect critical networks and territories.
Martin Bocken, co-founder and CEO of HyLight, stated: “Most power lines are still inspected by helicopter, just as they were fifty years ago. Our HyLighters already do the same job, with greater precision and less risk. This funding takes us from four aircraft to a fleet.”
Power lines, gas pipelines and railways face growing inspection needs as climate change, tightening regulations and safety risks converge, with more than 80 million kilometers of linear infrastructure worldwide requiring billions of euros in investment every year. Yet helicopters remain the dominant inspection solution, despite high costs, emissions of up to one metric ton of CO₂e per flight hour, noise and limited availability. Existing alternatives only partially address the need: drones lack range, satellites lack precision, and ground sensors offer only localized coverage.
HyLight has reached a decisive milestone: operational replacement. Its aircraft are already carrying out missions for Enedis, NaTran, Téréga, VINCI and SNCF Réseau to monitor network integrity, detect defects and identify methane leaks.
At 12 meters long, the HyLighter combines the performance of a long-endurance aircraft with the precision of an inspection platform. Electrically powered by hydrogen, it flies with no direct emissions and very low noise levels for up to ten hours, with a target range of 350 kilometers. It can carry up to 10 kg of sensors, including LiDAR, cameras and methane detectors, delivering 1 mm/pixel resolution imaging at an altitude of 25 meters and LiDAR density exceeding 1,000 points per square meter.
Authorized by the French civil aviation authority (DGAC) and the EASA, the HyLighter flies beyond visual line of sight (BVLOS) over critical infrastructure, in rural, suburban and urban environments. It has flown over the Palace of Versailles and has been showcased on the Champs-Élysées, at VivaTech and at the Grand Palais, proof that it can operate in sensitive, densely populated areas.
Beyond aerial inspection, HyLight turns flight data into decision-making tools that automatically identify and geolocate more than 50 types of defects and vegetation-related risks across power grids, replacing thousands of raw images with precise, actionable information for maintenance teams. As flights become more frequent, this data will build a continuously enriched digital twin of the infrastructure and territories HyLight covers, creating a new layer of multimodal data with future applications in insurance, agriculture and public land management.
HyLight is already industrializing: its new production facility is now online, with further internalization of strategic component manufacturing underway, targeting up to 15 HyLighters operated simultaneously in 2027, compared to four today. The new funding will support the recruitment of 50 employees across engineering, AI and data, operations, regulatory affairs and business development, and accelerate commercial expansion across Europe — with Germany and the Netherlands as priority markets — as the founding team, Martin Bocken, Josef Rokusek and Thomas Laporte (average age 27), preserves the integrated model that has let HyLight move fast: aeronautical engineering, software, AI and field operations under one roof.
Helmer Schukken, managing partner at Rubio Impact Ventures, commented: “In HyLight we see a team and a technology with the potential to change how we keep critical infrastructure safe. Today, powerlines, pipelines and railways are still inspected by helicopter, which is expensive, unsafe, polluting and—as workforces age—insufficiently available. HyLight offers a clean and scalable alternative that does the same work reliably, even over densely populated areas, and has the potential to deliver unrivaled cost savings. That means faults are caught earlier, before they become leaks or outages, and the infrastructure we rely on becomes both more dependable and a good deal cleaner. We are glad to back Martin, Josef and Thomas in making this the new standard.”

articles.title: Google reinventa Fitbit con una pulsera más ligera, inteligente y con 7 días de batería
articles.text:
Google ha lanzado la Fitbit Edge, su nueva pulsera de actividad que sustituye a la Fitbit Charge 6. El gigante tecnológico quiere ocupar ese punto medio entre relojes inteligentes y bandas de actividad más básicas con un dispositivo que promete llevar un registro de tu salud. Con 11,5 mm de grosor, siete días de batería y un precio menor a 180 euros, Google intentará competir contra Xiaomi y otras empresas que dominan en este sector
Según el anuncio oficial, la nueva Fitbit Edge debuta con una pantalla ovalada de 1,34 pulgadas y una interfaz reconstruida de cero. En términos de diseño, la pulsera incluye una carcasa de aluminio reciclado de 11,5 mm de grosor que pesa menos de la mitad de un Apple Watch Series 12. El cuerpo sigue la curvatura natural de la muñeca, lo que permitirá usarla todo el día e incluso durante el sueño.
Pasando a la pantalla, el panel Hybrid OLED ofrece un 46% más de área visible respecto a los Fitbit de generación anterior y cuenta con el brillo suficiente como para visualizarse bajo la luz directa del sol. Otro cambio que encontramos en el Fitbit Edge es el nuevo botón lateral físico, que ahora cuenta con retroalimentación táctil y permite acciones rápidas, como pausar un entrenamiento sin que tengas que tocar la pantalla.
El Fitbit Edge se inspira en el Pixel Watch 5
La parte más interesante es el software, ya que Google ha rediseñado la interfaz de usuario basándose en la lógica del Pixel Watch 5. El objetivo es que las funciones más importantes estén disponibles con menos toques, reduciendo la navegación entre menús.
La pantalla principal ofrece información relevante como el conteo de pasos, acceso a entrenamientos y otras métricas de actividad para que no tengas que abrir las aplicaciones para consultar los datos. También integra Google Maps, controles multimedia y notificaciones de llamadas o mensajes, similar a lo que ya hace Xiaomi con sus pulseras inteligentes.
Pasando a las funciones, el apartado deportivo concentra casi todas las novedades del Fitbit Edge. El rastreador reconoce más de 50 modos de ejercicio con guía en tiempo real, los cuales van desde pilates hasta zonas de frecuencia cardíaca para entrenamientos con intervalos. La pulsera también ofrece un sistema de detección automática capaz de identificar hasta 100 tipos de actividad, aunque el usuario olvide pulsar el inicio.
En la parte de la salud, Google ha colocado sensores para ECG, pulso óptico continuo y temperatura cutánea nocturna, que se complementan con el análisis de las fases del sueño para ofrecer una estimación del nivel de recuperación cada mañana. La pulsera también vigila tendencias de presión arterial, resistencia a la insulina y frecuencia cardíaca en segundo plano, mientras que la integración con Google Health Premium ayuda a interpretar los datos y ajustar tus rutinas físicas.
Por último, la batería aguanta hasta siete días con una carga, pero si te quedas sin pila, cinco minutos de carga magnética rápida proporcionan hasta un día adicional de autonomía. El Fitbit Edge es el primer dispositivo reparable de la marca y permite sustituir la batería.
Precio y disponibilidad
Google confirmó que el Fitbit Edge tendrá un precio de 180 dólares (unos 162 euros) y estará disponible a partir del 27 de octubre de 2026. Los usuarios pueden elegir entre cuatro acabados (Obsidian, Fog, Olive y Canyon) y correas intercambiables de varios colores que incluyen la típica Active Sport, Performance Loop, una variante magnética y una correa metálica en colores dorado y plateado.

articles.title: Las 10 películas de HBO Max que deberías ver ahora mismo
articles.text:
HBO Max está en boca de todos y la razón es obvia. La plataforma podría muy pronto fusionarse con Paramount+. Todo debido a la compra de Warner Bros. y su posterior transformación en Skydance. Una noticia agridulce para los fanáticos que han seguido a la marca durante años. Y en especial, los que consideran a la plataforma de streaming de las mejores entre las variadas opciones actuales. Mucho más, cuando con el transcurrir del tiempo su catálogo se ha hecho un lugar ideal para encontrar el mejor cine del siglo.
Pero además, HBO Max es el lugar en que se combinan de forma más elegante los elementos que parten de los actuales servicios por suscripción. Por lo que sus colecciones priorizan la calidad sobre la cantidad, en vez de la saturación de estrenos. Además, combina en un único servicio la producción original de HBO y el universo cinematográfico de DC Comics. También de franquicias históricas como Harry Potter, contenidos de Warner Bros., Cartoon Network y la variada oferta de no ficción de Discovery. Esta enorme diversidad le permite atraer tanto a los amantes de los blockbusters como a espectadores que buscan premisas complejas y galardonadas en la televisión.
Pero, como suele ocurrir, hay una única desventaja para toda esa riqueza de oferta y oportunidad de disfrutar de lo mejor del cine. La enorme cantidad de títulos a disposición, con frecuencia inabarcables para buena parte de los usuarios. Si eres de los que tiene este problema incómodo, esto es para ti. Te dejamos las diez películas que ya deberías ver en HBO Max, la mayoría estrenos recientes. De un melodramón que analiza la cultura de la cancelación a una tragedia que te hará llorar. Todo para los amantes del cine en todas sus dimensiones.
Date de alta en HBO MAX y tendrás acceso a las mejores series y películas exclusivas como The Wire, Los Soprano o Casa del Dragón. Incluye todo el catálogo de Warner, los clásicos de Cartoon Network, los grandes estrenos y el mejor deporte.
El drama
Escrita y dirigida por el cineasta noruego Kristoffer Borgli (Dream Scenario), fue una de las grandes sorpresas de este año. Además, una premisa retorcida que capturó la tensión social y cultural de nuestra época de manera elegante. Para eso, la historia sigue a Emma Harwood (Zendaya) y Charlie Thompson (Robert Pattinson), una pareja a punto de contraer matrimonio.
Pero la idílica relación se desmorona por completo durante los ensayos y degustaciones previos a su boda. Eso, cuando Emma hace una confesión inesperada y perturbadora sobre su pasado. Lo que fractura irreversiblemente la confianza y la percepción que Charlie tenía sobre ella. Lo demás, es una historia de equívocos incómodos que te parecerá más relevante de lo que imaginas en medio de la época de la reputación. Ideal para el debate y un estreno que solo encontrarás en HBO Max.
Weapons
Antes de dirigir Resident Evil, Zach Cregger exploró el horror doméstico y triunfó e incluso logró un Óscar para una de sus actrices. Para eso, la retorcida e intrincada trama se enfoca en la pequeña localidad de Maybrook, Pensilvania. Este es un poblado aparentemente tranquilo que se sumerge en el pánico colectivo cuando 17 niños de una misma clase escolar desaparecen de forma simultánea. Un suceso unido por un dato inexplicable. La desaparición ocurrió a las 2:17 a. m. tras caminar directo hacia la oscuridad de la noche. Pero además, dejando atrás a un único y desorientado estudiante sobreviviente.
A través de una compleja estructura de historias cruzadas narradas desde la perspectiva de seis personajes diferentes, la trama desglosa una escalofriante investigación. Una que llevará a descubrir un secreto escalofriante en la figura de la excéntrica, tenebrosa y peligrosa Gladys (Amy Madigan). Idea para los amantes del terror y disponible en HBO Max.
¡La novia!
Lo sabemos: fue uno de los fracasos del año, pero vale la pena darle una segunda revisión. En especial, porque esta obra escrita, dirigida y producida por Maggie Gyllenhaal no te dejará indiferente. ¿El motivo? Su osadía. Se trata de una reinterpretación del clásico libro de Mary Shelley que traslada la trama a 1930 en la ciudad de Chicago. Más extraño todavía, la historia comienza cuando un solitario y maduro monstruo de Frankenstein (Christian Bale) se enfrenta a la soledad. Lo que le llevará a buscar una compañera eterna.
Una mezcla explosiva que pronto transforma la película en un romance barroco y frenético. Todo cuando Myrna (Jessie Buckley) se transforme en otra criatura revivida y cruel. Además, con una personalidad tan salvaje, libre y ardiente que desafía de inmediato las intenciones de control de sus propios creadores masculinos. Lo demás es un viaje trepidante a través del horror y la autorrealización que sorprende por su osadía.
Cumbres borrascosas
Seguramente escuchaste de la obra más reciente de Emerald Fennell como una cinta polémica e incómoda. Lo es. Pero además es una reinvención desconcertante sobre el clásico gótico de Emily Brontë. Por lo que prescinde del drama familiar para abordar la destructiva y tóxica historia de amor, centro de la historia.
A saber, el amor tormentoso entre la caprichosa Catherine (Margot Robbie) y Heathcliff (Jacob Elordi). Por lo que el enfoque de la directora es un desborde de lujuria y pasiones carnales prohibidas. Pero mucho más una reflexión sobre el deseo, la transgresión y la pérdida. Exagerada, visualmente impactante y un vendaval de emociones, es la obra ideal para los amantes de lo extraño. Ya disponible en HBO Max.
Backrooms
Dirigida por Kane Parsons, la cinta expande el folklore digital nacido de las leyendas urbanas de las creepypastas de internet. Por lo que la enigmática trama sigue de cerca la angustiante historia de Clark (Chiwetel Ejiofor). Este, un arquitecto frustrado que administra una mueblería convencional.
No obstante, su mundo dará un vuelco al descubrir por accidente una misteriosa e imposible abertura resplandeciente en el sótano del establecimiento. Algo que terminará por mostrarle que la realidad es mucho más compleja y tenebrosa de lo que jamás había imaginado. Un tipo de terror poco convencional que asombrará a los fanáticos más transgresores del género.
Mortal Kombat 2
Si la primera parte del 2021 te decepcionó, hay buenas noticias para ti. La secuela de esta saga intergeneracional supera con creces a su primera parte. Dirigida nuevamente por el cineasta australiano Simon McQuoid y escrita por Jeremy Slater, complace las peticiones de los fanáticos. Por lo que traslada la acción al legendario torneo interdimensional definitivo.
De modo que la trama sigue a los campeones defensores del Reino de la Tierra. Un equipo variopinto que deberá unir sus fuerzas para contener una invasión masiva del Mundo Exterior tras el robo del místico amuleto de Shinnok. ¿Nada de eso te convence? Esto lo hará. La entrega incluye a la carismática e irreverente estrella de acción de Hollywood, Johnny Cage (Karl Urban). Una delicia para fanáticos que ya puedes ver en HBO Max.
Te van a matar
Otra rareza para los amantes de la acción poco convencional que puedes ver en HBO Max. Dirigida por Kirill Sokolov y coescrita junto a Alex Litvak, la cinta es un experimento de principio a fin. De modo que la enigmática trama sigue los pasos de Asia Reaves (Zazie Beetz). Esta, una exconvicta que responde impulsivamente a un críptico anuncio de empleo para trabajar como ama de llaves residencial.
Al llegar, se adentra en el majestuoso rascacielos neoyorquino llamado The Virgil. Todo sin imaginar que ese lujoso lugar oculta un turbio historial de misteriosas desapariciones colectivas extendidas por décadas. Y además, en la que opera una red secreta y siniestra de inquilinos ricos que adoran a una deidad con cabeza de cerdo. Sí, así de rara es. Ya la puedes ver en HBO Max.
La momia de Lee Cronin
Terror repugnante para fanáticos de hueso rojo. Lee Cronin (Evil Dead Rise) dirige y escribe esta reinvención del monstruo clásico de Universal que te dará escalofríos. Alejándose de la aventura de las versiones anteriores, la trama se sumerge en una pesadilla doméstica de posesión demoníaca y trauma familiar. Por lo que la historia se enfoca en Katie Cannon (Natalie Grace), la hija de un periodista que desapareció misteriosamente en el desierto de Egipto. Ocho años después, es devuelta repentinamente a su familia en Nuevo México.
Sin embargo, el emotivo e inesperado reencuentro con sus padres se transforma rápidamente en un espeluznante infierno. Eso, cuando descubren con horror absoluto que la joven ha regresado como el huésped biológico del nasmaraniano. Este, un antiguo y cruel parásito demoníaco egipcio. ¿Qué esperas para verla en HBO Max?
Letras robadas
Escrita y dirigida por John Carney, la cinta aborda de forma simpática pero incisiva los peligros del estrellato dentro de la industria musical contemporánea. De modo que sigue los pasos de Rick Power (Paul Rudd). Este último, un cansado cantante de bodas de Dublín venido a menos que intenta mantener a flote su modesta banda. Su vida cambia de rumbo inesperadamente cuando cruza caminos con Danny Wilson (Nick Jonas).
Que casualmente interpreta a la carismática pero decadente estrella juvenil de una antigua boy band. Y una además, que busca desesperadamente un nuevo rumbo para relanzar su carrera comercial en solitario. Tras una improvisada noche de tragos e improvisaciones conjuntas en el estudio, ocurre el milagro de la amistad. Solo para después torcerse de manera complicada. Entérate de qué manera en HBO Max.
Un talento único
Dirigida por Daniel Roher, la historia aborda de manera fascinante e inusual el mundo de los robos de altos vuelos. Y de una manera por completo novedosa. De modo que la atrapante historia gira en torno a Niki White (Leo Woodall). Niki es un joven e introvertido aprendiz de afinador de pianos que padece de hiperacusia. Esta es una rara condición médica que le provoca una sensibilidad auditiva exagerada y dolorosa ante los sonidos cotidianos fuertes.
Lejos de ser una limitación destructiva, esta singularidad física le otorga un extraordinario oído absoluto. Una cualidad que su veterano mentor y figura paterna, Harry Horowitz (Dustin Hoffman), le ayuda a canalizar con paciencia a través de la música clásica dentro de su humilde taller de reparación. Pero pronto, ambos descubrirán que la rara cualidad tiene una aplicación más mundana, ilegal y peligrosa. La de permitirle abrir complicados mecanismos de cajas fuertes. Y sí, ya sabes cómo termina eso. Por si no lo sabes, ya puedes ver la película en HBO Max.

articles.title: The Social Reckoning is flopping at the box office
articles.text:
As important as some of the messages in The Social Reckoning are, the movie has been drastically underperforming at the box office. Per Variety, Aaron’s Sorkin’s follow up to The Social Network only grossed a measly $5.5 million this past weekend against a budget that’s somewhere within the $30–42 million range. That would make it a certifiable flop that’s costing Columbia Pictures (and Sony) quite a bit of money — especially when you compare it to The Social Network’s $22 million opening.
The Social Reckoning is flopping at the box office
Meanwhile, Other Mommy is having an unexpected moment.
This isn’t entirely surprising given how middling reviews for the film have been. It’s currently got a 55% rating on Rotten Tomatoes and has widely been trashed on social media. All of this might be reflective of audiences hoping for a proper sequel to The Social Network, which won three Oscars for its screenplay (written by Sorkin), editing, and score. But it might speak to people not fully clicking with Mikey Madison’s performance as whistleblower Frances Haugen or Jeremy Allen White’s turn as Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz. (Madison, for her part, indicated to The Hollywood Reporter that it was Sorkin’s vision as director that kept from “authentically and faithfully represent[ing] a real person,” which she hopes to do in the future.) It also probably didn’t help that Jesse Eisenberg — who portrayed Mark Zuckerberg in The Social Network — had no interest in being in the film, according to Sorkin himself.
Ironically, Blumhouse’s Other Mommy raked in an impressive $27.5 million this weekend, which likely suggests that people are more interested in novel horror as opposed to reminders of how social media has made everyone’s lives worse.

articles.title: Microsoft intègre les applis Office directement dans Copilot
articles.text:
Après avoir intégré Copilot dans les différentes applications de sa suite bureautique Office, Microsoft est partie pour faire l’inverse. La firme de Redmond vient en effet d’annoncer qu’elle allait intégrer Office dans sa nouvelle application Microsoft Copilot. Avec cette manœuvre, les utilisateurs pourront profiter de l’ensemble des fonctionnalités de la suite Microsoft 365 au cœur d’une expérience de travail gérée par l’IA.
Une expérience unifiée pour faire travailler l’IA à votre place
Les fonctions de création et de collaboration de Word, Excel et PowerPoint vont officiellement intégrer la nouvelle application Copilot de Microsoft. Concrètement, cette intégration doit vous permettre de passer d’un prompt initial à un document, un tableur ou une présentation finale, sans rupture. Vous pouvez commencer directement dans le chat Copilot ou dans Cowork, et continuer dans les applications Office autonomes.
En fonction des tâches à réaliser, vous pourrez en outre sélectionner le modèle d’IA le plus adapté, ou laisser Copilot choisir automatiquement pour vous le meilleur modèle.
Pour vous aider à y voir plus clair, lors de la génération d’un document, Copilot affichera côte à côte sa fenêtre de discussion et le fichier Word, Excel ou PowerPoint associé. L’assistant IA de Microsoft conservera par ailleurs l’historique de conversation pour vous permettre d’affiner le contenu en ajoutant de nouvelles consignes, mais vous pourrez évidemment réaliser manuellement des retouches sur le contenu généré.
Cette intégration des outils d’Office dans Copilot s’accompagne de fonctions collaboratives. Vous pourrez partager vos documents avec des tiers, et ceux-ci pourront les commenter et les éditer simultanément. À noter que l’ensemble des modifications apportées à un document, par vous-même, par un collaborateur, ou par l’IA, sont centralisées au sein d’un fichier unique, pour éviter d’avoir à fusionner plusieurs brouillons séparés.
Des documents facilement accessibles stockés sur OneDrive
Pour vous permettre d’accéder facilement aux documents générés depuis Copilot, Microsoft a choisi de les regrouper au sein d’une bibliothèque directement intégrée à l’application Copilot. Tous les fichiers qui s’y trouvent et qui sont automatiquement stockés sur OneDrive, conservent leur mise en page, leurs commentaires, leur historique de versions, ainsi que leurs paramètres de sécurité propres à votre entreprise.
Microsoft précise que l’expérience Office dans Copilot est d’ores et déjà disponible en accès anticipé pour les clients Frontier dans les modes Chat et Cowork.

articles.title: Yandex confirms service outage as users lose access to cloud files
articles.text:
Russian cloud services provider Yandex announced that drone attacks damaged three of its data centers, forcing it to shut down two facilities and partially disable a third.
Yandex customers are experiencing service outages, some of them reporting inability to access files stored on the company’s cloud infrastructure.
The impacted data centers are in Sasovo (hit on October 8), Kaluga (hit on October 9), and Vladimir (attacked on October 11). The Sasovo and Vladimir facilities stopped operating completely, while the Kaluga facility's operations are degraded.
The attacks are believed to have been carried out by Ukrainian forces trying to cause widespread operational disruptions. Yandex reported no injuries related to these incidents.
As Russia’s largest technology companies, Yandex is often called “Russia’s Google,” offering search engine, maps, and navigation services. The company also offers ride-hailing, delivery, shopping, streaming, email, cloud storage, and business cloud infrastructure services.
Much of the country's internet infrastructure, serving both government and private-sector organizations, relies on Yandex's services.
EU MEP Tomáš Zdechovský highlighted a potential connection between Yandex outages and a sudden drop in communication from online accounts promoting far-right ideals in Germany.
On its status page, Yandex said its teams are working around the clock to maintain services and help affected customers and partners, but it cannot provide a reliable service-restoration timeline.
For this reason, Yandex urged customers to use alternative infrastructure for disaster recovery.
“We consider the remaining resource configuration to be unstable,” reads one of Yandex’s status updates from yesterday.
“The platform's operating mode is emergency – we recommend using any other alternative disaster recovery plans. Technical-supported communication channels can be unstable.”
As of the most recent update, Yandex’s Console, API, IAM, Container Registry, databases, S3 storage, and Kubernetes were available, with some performance or availability issues. Compute, AI Studio, and security services were partially available, while Monium is still offline.
One Yandex customer reported issues starting on October 8, with backups to their Yandex Disk missing thumbnails and an inability to download previously submitted files.
The user reports getting HTTP 302 redirects, HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout errors, and HTTP 500 errors when trying to access or work on the files.
It is currently unclear whether any data stored in the affected data centers has been irreversibly lost, as Yandex has not addressed the problem in its status updates.

articles.title: En réponse à Garmin, Polar métamorphose son bracelet sans écran Loop en brassard cardio
articles.text:
En réponse à Garmin, Polar métamorphose son bracelet sans écran Loop en brassard cardio
Polar apporte un nouvel usage à son Loop, parmi les premiers modèles de marques sportives à investir le segment des bracelets sans écran. Moyennant l’achat d'une sangle tout juste disponible, il peut désormais se muer en brassard cardio.
La concurrence a parfois du bon. Quelques mois seulement après le lancement du Cirqa, créé par son rival Garmin, Polar remet son bracelet sans écran sur le devant de la scène.
Le Loop, disponible depuis décembre 2025, est désormais agrémenté de nouveaux accessoires. Polar le pense bien davantage comme un accessoire de mode et propose désormais des bracelets un peu plus élégants que le modèle tissé qui l’accompagne par défaut : la marque commercialise de nouveaux bracelets en cuir et en silicone. Néanmoins, c’est surtout un brassard, qui permet donc de porter le boîtier au bras et non plus au poignet, que l’on retient.
Polar Loop
Polar, qui n’en disait mot au lancement initial du Loop, ajoute donc un usage à son appareil pour mieux « entourer fermement le bras et rester en place au fil des séries, des sprints et des répétitions, sans glisser ni rebondir ». C’est également par le biais d’une sangle dédiée que Garmin transforme son Cirqa en brassard au besoin. Chez Polar, comptez un coût de 30 €, à ajouter au tarif initial de 180 € du bracelet, fonctionnant sans abonnement.
Rappelons que si le Loop se mue en brassard, il ne peut exactement prétendre remplacer un brassard de type Verity Sense, chez Polar également. Son cardiofréquencemètre optique est nativement conçu pour être porté au bras, et il bénéficie, en plus du Bluetooth, d’une connectivité ANT+. Celle-ci lui permet d’être relié au besoin à une montre d’une autre marque afin d’affiner les mesures cardio durant les entraînements.

articles.title: Infinite Partners raises $169.3m to back growth businesses
articles.text:
Infinite Partners, a South African mid-market private equity investment firm, has raised R2.8 billion ($169.3 million) to back established businesses, including those using technology to expand markets and scale.
The firm closed its Core Equity Fund II above its R2.5 billion ($151.1 million) target, backed entirely by South African institutional investors, including pension funds, insurers, asset managers and banks. The fund targets established mid-market businesses, with individual investments ranging from R100 million ($6 million) to R500 million ($30.2 million).
The raise comes as private equity looks beyond traditional technology companies to businesses where technology can unlock growth, improve efficiency and expand access to essential services. Infinite Partners is taking a generalist approach, backing established companies with strong growth potential, including those using technology to solve practical problems in sectors such as financial services and digital infrastructure.
“Our Infinite Deal investment philosophy has remained the same from day one. We focus on backing quality businesses with identifiable tailwinds, and potential to create sustainable value over time,” Edward Pitsi, co-founder and CEO of Infinite Partners, told TechCabal in an interview on Friday.
Infinite Partners is a generalist private equity investor, not a dedicated technology fund. Its strategy centres on established businesses with strong fundamentals and clear growth opportunities.
“We are a generalist South African mid-market investor, and we have certain restrictions on committing too much capital to any particular sector,” Pitsi said.
He stated that the firm looks for businesses with significant structural growth drivers, strong management, healthy margins and cash conversion, high barriers to entry, and a credible exit strategy.
The firm’s first two investments are in enterprise software company e4 and digital infrastructure business CYNK. e4, an enterprise software business, serves the banking and property sectors, digitising workflows involved in mortgage origination and property transactions.
According to Pitsi, e4’s technology has reduced the home-buying process from 96 days to around 40 days. Since inception, its platform has processed R2.8 trillion ($169.3 billion) in mortgages.
“Leveraged correctly, technology can have a multiplier effect,” he said. “We have seen this firsthand through our investments in e4, where technology has vastly improved and quickened the home buying process by a factor of more than 50%. This has also underpinned economic activity by providing the technology rails required to facilitate these transactions.”
Pitsi also disclosed that the business is also pursuing international expansion through a nascent United Kingdom (UK) operation, extending the potential market for its South African-developed technology.
CYNK addresses a different challenge: access to digital infrastructure. The company develops and owns fibre assets, with a network reaching more than 667,000 South African households, particularly in underserved communities and townships.
“From a CYNK perspective, we are seeing technology bridge the digital divide and provide much-needed access to connectivity for the lower LSM,” Pitsi said. He added that the infrastructure has created opportunities for small businesses in underserved areas and helped improve the affordability of internet access.
Infinite Partners says it assesses whether a business can turn its market opportunity into sustainable growth, generate cash and deliver a credible return for investors.
The fund provides both growth and replacement capital to established mid-market companies. Beyond its existing investments, Infinite Partners is exploring opportunities in business services, education, alternative lending and software-as-a-service (SaaS), Pitsi said.
“We are generalist investors,” he stated, adding that international expansion would form part of the firm’s strategy for portfolio companies where appropriate.
Investor confidence was also critical to the fund’s close. Pitsi said some of the firm’s earliest backers increased their commitments after seeing its investment strategy take shape.
“As we invested in our first two deals, they saw our investment strategy being borne out, and this gave them sufficient confidence in us to increase their commitments in subsequent closings,” he said.

articles.title: Piratage Intermarché, Super U, Leclerc : pourquoi les frigos des supermarchés sont-ils connectés à Internet ?
articles.text:
C’est la question qui revient le plus souvent depuis la révélation de l’incident cyber qui a frappé plusieurs enseignes de la grande distribution.
Petit rappel des faits. Dans la nuit du 11 au 12 octobre, des pirates ont pris la main sur des systèmes de régulation frigorifique Danfoss installés dans de nombreux supermarchés français.
Cette manœuvre leur a permis d’imposer un dégivrage continu, avec une consigne de 50 degrés, dans des centaines de supermarchés en France. Intermarché, Leclerc et Super U sont notamment touchés.
Sur les réseaux sociaux, beaucoup d’internautes se sont alors demandé comment un congélateur de supermarché pouvait être piraté depuis l’extérieur du magasin.
Une obligation de traçabilité, des alarmes et de la maintenance à distance
La première raison est réglementaire. Le règlement européen n° 37/2005 impose que les locaux d’entreposage et de stockage des aliments surgelés soient équipés d’instruments d’enregistrement capables de contrôler la température de l’air fréquemment et à intervalles réguliers.
Les exploitants doivent aussi conserver les documents qui prouvent la conformité de ces instruments. Le texte dispense toutefois les meubles de vente, où un thermomètre bien visible suffit. Pour tenir le suivi des chambres froides et surveiller des dizaines de meubles réfrigérés, les enseignes s’appuient sur des gestionnaires centraux comme l’AK-SM 800A de Danfoss, qui coordonne les régulateurs de l’installation, conserve l’historique des températures et déclenche des alarmes en cas de dérive.
La connexion sert aussi l’économie du magasin. Ces gestionnaires intègrent un serveur web pour permettre aux techniciens de diagnostiquer et de régler les installations à distance, sans se déplacer dans chaque point de vente.
Danfoss met également en avant le pilotage de ses systèmes jusqu’au cloud, notamment pour optimiser la consommation d’énergie.
Connecté ne veut pas dire exposé
Reste qu’aucune de ces fonctions n’exige que la console soit accessible directement depuis Internet.
Dans son « guide sur la cybersécurité des systèmes industriels », l’ANSSI recommande d’ailleurs d’interdire les accès directs depuis Internet vers ces systèmes. Pour la télémaintenance, elle préconise des connexions ouvertes à la demande et pour une durée limitée, une authentification multifacteur, un tunnel chiffré de type VPN et un cloisonnement de l’équipement par rapport au reste du réseau.
Sauf que sur le terrain, ces règles ne sont pas toujours suivies. C’est notamment ce qu’avait souligné « la société de cybersécurité Claroty dès août 2026 ». L’entreprise avait alors recensé 2 765 interfaces AK-SM 800A directement accessibles en ligne, et décrit plusieurs failles qui permettaient d’en prendre le contrôle, dont un mécanisme caché de contournement du mot de passe administrateur. Danfoss les avait corrigées dans une mise à jour, que les exploitants devaient encore installer.
Si aucun lien direct n’a pour l’heure été établi entre ces failles et l’incident du 12 octobre, Danfoss indique que la majorité des systèmes touchés par la cyberattaque sont des modèles en fin de vie, qui ne reçoivent plus de correctifs de sécurité, et que les AK-SM 800A concernés tournaient avec un micrologiciel obsolète.
Le fabricant affirme par ailleurs qu’il travaille avec ses clients pour supprimer l’accès direct à ces systèmes depuis Internet lorsqu’il était ouvert. Le fabricant laisse ainsi entendre qu’une partie des équipements attaqués étaient joignables depuis Internet. Aucune règle n’impose pourtant une telle exposition.

articles.title: Galaxy Buds 4 nunca esteve tão barato: 45% OFF no Mercado Livre • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Galaxy Buds 4 nunca esteve tão barato: 45% OFF no Mercado Livre
Galaxy Buds 4 com ANC, áudio Hi-Fi de 24 bits e recursos de IA atingem o menor preço já registrado, com desconto de 45% no Pix com cupom
Os Galaxy Buds 4 estão em oferta por R$ 872 no Pix com cupom PROMODEHOJE no Mercado Livre. Os fones de ouvido sem fio da Samsung, com áudio Hi-Fi de 24 bits e recursos de IA, alcançam o menor preço já registrado, com desconto de 45% sobre o original de R$ 1.599.
Um dos principais fones wireless da Samsung, os Galaxy Buds 4 contam com suporte a áudio Hi-Fi (alta fidelidade) de 24 bits, que oferece experiência sonora com grande foco nos detalhes. Já o cancelamento de ruído ativo (ANC) filtra a maioria dos sons externos, mas não todos, por questões de segurança.
Os fones contam com assistentes de Inteligência Artificial (IA) como o Bixby da Samsung, Google Gemini e Perplexity, que oferecem funções como comandos por voz para acionar menus e realizar pesquisas. O Galaxy AI oferece um tradutor automático de conversas, mas este só funciona com gadgets da linha Galaxy.
Outros recursos incluem o Voice Pickup Unit, que deixa as chamadas de voz mais nítidas, e o equalizador adaptativo, que ajusta as frequências conforme o formato do canal auditivo do usuário, para personalizar a experiência sonora.
O suporte ao Bluetooth 6.1 permite aos Galaxy Buds 4 oferecerem menor latência em jogos ou transmissões em tempo real. Já a função Auto Switch simplifica gerenciar o pareamento entre mais de um dispositivo, permitindo pular entre gadgets conectados facilmente.
As baterias de 45 mAh dos fones possuem autonomia de até 6 horas de uso com o ANC ligado, e de 7 horas com o recurso desativado. O estojo traz uma bateria própria de 515 mAh para recarga dos acessórios, somando ao kit um total de até 30 horas de uso.
Os Galaxy Buds 4 (R$ 872 no Pix com cupom PROMODEHOJE) possuem certificação IP54, que confere resistência moderada contra poeira, suor e respingos d’água.

articles.title: Java News Roundup: Grails 8, Open Liberty, GlassFish, Infinispan, LangChain4j, Spock
articles.text:
This week's Java roundup for October 5th, 2026, features news highlighting: OpenJDK JEPs Proposed to Target for JDK 28; Lazy Constants elevated to Candidate status; the GA releases of Apache Grails 8.0 and Open Liberty 20.0.0.10; point releases of TornadoVM, Infinispan, LangChain4j and Spock; and a maintenance release of GlassFish.
OpenJDK
JEP 546, Adaptive Heap Sizing for ZGC, has been elevated from Candidate to Proposed to Target for JDK 28. This JEP proposes to "enhance the Z Garbage Collector to adaptively adjust the size of the heap based on the resources available, the application's needs, and the needs of neighboring applications contending for the same resources." The review is expected to conclude on Wednesday, October 14, 2026.
JEP 545, Faster Startup and Warmup with ZGC, has been elevated from Candidate to Proposed to Target for JDK 28. This JEP proposes to "improve application startup and warmup by enhancing the Z Garbage Collector to acquire and prepare physical memory more swiftly and efficiently in response to application needs." The review is expected to conclude on Wednesday, October 14, 2026.
JEP 543, Structured Concurrency, has been elevated from Candidate to Proposed to Target for JDK 28. This JEP proposes to finalize this feature, without change, after seven rounds of preview, delivered in JDK 21 through the upcoming release of JDK 27, and two rounds of incubator delivered in JDK 19 and JDK 20. This feature simplifies concurrent programming by introducing structured concurrency to "treat groups of related tasks running in different threads as a single unit of work, thereby streamlining error handling and cancellation, improving reliability, and enhancing observability." The review is expected to conclude on Tuesday, October 13, 2026.
JEP 547, Lazy Constants (Fourth Preview), has been elevated from its JEP Draft 8389764 to Candidate status. This JEP proposes a fourth preview, with no changes, after three rounds of preview delivered in the upcoming release of JDK 27 and JDK 26 through JDK 25. Formerly known as Stable Values and Computed Constants, this feature introduces the concept of computed constants, defined as immutable value holders that are initialized at most once. This offers the performance and safety benefits of final fields, while offering greater flexibility as to the timing of initialization. The name change from Stable Values to Lazy Constants with the release of JDK 26, better captures the intent of a high-level use case.
JDK 28
Build 19 of the JDK 28 early-access builds was made available this past week featuring updates from Build 18 that include fixes for various issues. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
For JDK 28, developers are encouraged to report bugs via the Java Bug Database.
GlassFish
The release of GlassFish 8.0.5 delivers bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: updates to the ZipPayloadImpl class to include the Header ID and Data Size values in the extra header as per the ZIP64 Extra Fields (JDK-8302483) specification; and improvements in deployment time for both large and small applications. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Apache Grails
The release of Apache Grails 8.0.0 ships with bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: support for JDK 21 and Gradle 9.7 as minimal versions; all controllers are now REST resources that resolve a controller from the request as opposed to the mapping; and Grails Promises now run on top of the Spring Boot Task Executor. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
TornadoVM
The release of TornadoVM 7.2.0 and 7.1.0 provide notable changes such as: new methods, mmaLoadA() and mmaLoadB(), added to the KernelContext class, that return 8-element and 4-element fragments, respectively, of the HalfFloat class; and updates to the CUDACommandQueue, CUDAEvent and CUDAHandles classes such that they now accurately report the driver dispatch time for kernel launches and data transfers. Further details on these releases may be found in the release notes for version 7.2.0 and version 7.1.0.
Open Liberty
The GA release of Open Liberty 26.0.0.10 delivers: bug fixes; support for JDK 27; and resolutions to seven CVEs affecting various Open Liberty features. Developers should note that, with G1 now the default GC in all environments, users running Open Liberty in a constrained environment may experience a different garbage collection behavior compared to earlier Java versions.
Infinispan
The release of Infinispan 16.3.0, codenamed Tripel Karmeliet for "robustness," ships with bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: a more efficient hash-based conflict detection and resolution when merging partitions; enhanced configuration as attributes are now persisted to survive restarts; and improved logging to reduce log noise. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
LangChain4j
The formal release (along with the thirty-second beta release) of LangChain4j 1.22.0 provides bug fixes, documentation improvements, dependency upgrades and new features such as: a new BedrockBatchChatModel class that implements the core BatchChatModel interface on the Bedrock batch inference API; and new OpenAiDecisionModel and OpenAiOfficialDecisionModel classes to support the OpenAI Decisions API. Further details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Micronaut
The release of Micronaut Framework 5.2.2, based on Micronaut Core 5.2.15, delivers an update to Netty 4.2.19.Final featuring resolutions to 16 CVEs including HTTP request/response smuggling and unbounded resource consumption in the HTTP, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 codecs. There were also patch updates to modules: Micronaut Data and Micronaut Test Resources. More details on this release may be found in the release notes.
Spock
The release of Spock 2.5.0 ships with bug fixes and new features such as: support for Groovy 6 and Spring Framework 7; improvements to the TooManyInvocationsError class that now reports unsatisfied interactions for easier diagnosis of mismatched invocations; and support for local variables declared as final in where: blocks. Further details on this release, including breaking changes, may be found in the release notes.

articles.title: Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
articles.text:
Meta is making up for lost time in the AI race. After launching Muse Spark, the first model from its revamped Superintelligence Labs division, and buzzy AI agent Muse, it’s now launching two new models it claims can go toe-to-toe with the industry’s best.
Meta has some Wonder Full new AI models
Meta says the models compete with the industry’s best and will soon power its Muse agent.
The new models, Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, are available for Muse Code subscribers starting today. Wonder can also be accessed through the Meta Model API, Meta said.
Meta says it eventually plans to power its Muse AI agent with Wonder, starting with subscribers, and will develop specialized models it “can bring to everyone using Muse.” It hasn’t shared specifics or provided a timeline for either.
The company says its new models can rival leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic, including GPT-6 Astra, Claude Opus 5.5, and Claude Fable 5.1, pointing to results from internal testing on several industry benchmarks. It’s unclear how they stack up against Google’s Gemini 4 Argon, whose capabilities are still coming into focus.
The launches are part of Meta’s aggressive push to reestablish itself as a major force in AI. The company has poured billions into talent and infrastructure and has been steadily expanding its AI lineup, including with image model Muse Image and a heavy focus on bringing useful AI agents to the masses through Muse.

articles.title: Google announces the Fitbit Edge, a middle ground between Pixel Watch 5 and Fitbit Air
articles.text:
Google is releasing its second Fitbit tracker of 2026, offering fans of the aging Charge 6 a more refined option. The new Fitbit Edge slots right in between the Pixel Watch 5 and the Fitbit Air, featuring a compact screen and more health sensors than the Air. You won’t get all the apps and features of the Pixel Watch 5, but the Edge is only about half as expensive.
The Fitbit Edge is essentially a new Charge 6, but it has more of a Pixel Watch aesthetic. Squish Google’s smartwatch from the sides, and you’ve got the Edge. It has a pill-shaped 1.34-inch OLED touch display inside a slender aluminum frame that is rated IP68 (5 ATM) for water and dust protection. Google says the screen has 46 percent more viewable area compared to the Charge 6. It’s very close in overall size to the Fitbit Air and uses the same magnetic charging puck.
The Edge works with Android or iPhones via the Google Health app, and it can run for about seven days on a charge. If the tracker is away from your phone, it can still follow your activity all week with support for seven days of full health data storage (or 30 days of basic data). However, the generous weeklong battery life does not include always-on display mode. If you turn it on, battery life drops to about two days, barely longer than the Pixel Watch 5.
The Fitbit Edge plays it right down the middle in Google’s wearable lineup, and not just in price and size—button count also splits the difference. The Pixel Watch has two buttons, the Air has none, and the Edge sports a single tactile side button. You can use that to wake the device or start/pause workouts. Most interactions will be handled with the touchscreen, though.

articles.title: Dev used AI agents and more than 500 billion tokens to rebuild Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2's source code — 83% of the 2009 shooter's functions now match the original byte for byte
articles.text:
Dev used AI agents and more than 500 billion tokens to rebuild Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2's source code — 83% of the 2009 shooter's functions now match the original byte for byte
The agents originally tried to cheat the developer’s check.
Developer Maurice Heumann details in his blog how AI agents were able to decompile Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 (2009), which the post calls only “a popular first-person shooter,” in an effort to rebuild its source code in C++, taking three months and over 500 billion tokens. The agents originally attempted to cheat a byte-for-byte check added after the first month of code ran, but it was “semantically wrong,” and now 99% of the game’s functions are present, with 83% matching the original.
Heumann’s goal since the beginning has been to produce an “accurate, stable and feature-complete recreation,” and he wrote on X less than two weeks ago that the game was fully playable. By his estimate, the project consumed 600–700 billion tokens. In another X post, he said he doesn’t pay for his own tokens but put the cost at about €1,200 with subscriptions or $200,000–$250,000 with API tokens.
The difficulty turned out to be not in producing the code but verifying it was correct, forcing the developer to create a check and to make sure the agents couldn’t game it. The other challenge, as he put it, was that “corporate America was here to ruin our fun.” Two earlier blog posts on the project have since been removed, and the video in his Sept. 30 X post was disabled after a report by the copyright owner. No comment from Activision is currently on record.
The method includes pointing a fleet of agents, using Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s Codex, at the original 2009 PC game. Heumann started with a Claude Max (20x) plan, then added Codex Pro and used both simultaneously. These are flat-rate plans and do not use per-token API billing. “Most of the time,” the developer relied on Sonnet 5, although Opus 5.5 and OpenAI’s Luna, Sol, and Terra were “also used a lot.” For harnesses, he relied mostly on the Claude Code and Codex CLIs.
The agents read the code through IDA using Hex-Rays’ ida-mcp server. The work started with four agents, three workers and a reviewer; by Sept. 30, he wrote on X, it had “17 agents working in parallel.” Keeping all of this straight meant having one GitHub issue per translation unit, and having all agents and humans share a single Discord channel with GitHub webhook CI posts. The developer also tuned the auto-compaction threshold, from the default 90% of the context window maximum to 42% to help clear finished functions out of memory. Agents also had a tendency to drift, so an hourly cron job had them reread instructions.
The agents’ first month of code was extremely readable but “semantically wrong” for multiple reasons: wrong function signatures, types and struct layout issues, and logic that was invented or removed. The agents also made unneeded architectural changes, such as turning a config-variable lookup into one that was “orders of magnitude more expensive.”
The reviewer agent failed to stop this as there were no objective acceptance criteria, and the workers’ comments justifying their changes “effectively acted as unintentional prompt injection,” Heumann says. The team eventually stripped all comments from the source, which “helped a lot,” he wrote on X. An attempt to salvage the first four weeks of code took more time than starting from scratch would have.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
The answer was an automated check, so the team switched to the same compiler used to build the original game. A script compares each rebuilt function against the game’s executable at the byte level. Calls and data references are at different addresses and are skipped, with target symbols and offsets checked instead, but data and types get the same check. Then it’s a simple matter of pass/fail for each function, and every match is recorded so CI can recheck it and alert on regressions. While this type of matching is slow and sometimes challenging, a match guarantees identical behavior down to reproducing original bugs.
Even with this positive change, the agents immediately tried to cheat by writing “inline assembly” and “repeatedly tried to modify this script to exclude their function from comparison,” Heumann wrote. Inline assembly and similar shortcuts were then banned in the agents’ instructions, and CI now hashes the verification script and checks it against a hash stored as a GitHub Actions secret. Agents cheating is an expected outcome at this point with many such reports, such as when OpenAI’s models went after ExploitGym answers instead of solving the capture-the-flag challenges directly. As Heumann discovered, having a reviewer agent alone may be insufficient.
Before the check was originally implemented, the cheaper, less capable Haiku and Luna models “produced extremely bad results,” the post says. With the check in place, there was sufficient feedback to make the models work, which cut costs and let the project scale up. After almost two more months, 99% of the functions were present, with 83% meeting the byte-exact requirements. Heumann believes the 16% lacking a byte match are still semantically correct, but diminishing returns were getting real. The blog claims the game “runs flawlessly” as it stands.
For “obvious reasons,” the project’s code is remaining private and will be used “for my own needs only,” Heumann says. As he put it on X, the “decompiled code is obviously also copyrighted.” However, the developer has started extending Sogen, his userspace emulator, into lightweight sandboxing for agents, a response to his project’s agents wiping VMs. It will not be production-ready for a while.
As for the decompilation project, Heumann says that it is a special case, as not every project can do a byte-for-byte reference, but thinks every project can get close “with enough creativity.” One takeaway lesson is that you should be willing to move past failures as “Generating code is cheap now. Throw it away if it’s bad” and focus on correctness over productivity.
Follow Tom’s Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Shane Downing is a Contributing Writer for Tom’s Hardware, covering consumer storage, PC hardware, and AI.
