articles.title: GitLab 19.4 Adds Goal-Driven Agents and Tighter Cost Controls
articles.text:
GitLab has released version 19.4 of its DevSecOps platform, adding a goal-driven mode to GitLab Duo CLI, three hosted open-weight models, a larger set of Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools, and more detailed controls for AI spending. The release moves GitLab's agents beyond individual prompts and predefined flows, while keeping their actions within the permissions and approval rules already used by a project.
The new /goal command in GitLab Duo CLI, now in public beta, accepts an open-ended objective and continues working until it completes the task or reaches an iteration limit. One model implements the changes while a separate model checks progress against the stated goal. A developer can stop the run, change the goal, or redirect the agent. The work runs locally and retains the project's existing context and controls.
"This release takes agentic automation from something individual developers use to something an organization can scale at speed and under the controls already in place."
Manav Khurana, GitLab
GitLab's use of the word "verified" has a specific meaning here. The second model judges whether the result meets the natural-language goal; this is not formal verification of the code. The command can report work that it could not resolve, and the iteration limit prevents it from continuing indefinitely. Clear acceptance criteria therefore remain important, even though the developer no longer has to supervise every intermediate step.
GitLab Duo Agent Platform also gains support for the hosted open-weight models Kimi K3, MiniMax M3 and GLM 5.3. GitLab says these provide up to four times as many calls per GitLab Credit as many comparable frontier models. Group owners can set a default model for a feature and restrict the models available to teams. This lets an organisation use a lower-cost model for routine work and reserve a more expensive model for tasks where it performs better. The announcement does not include model-by-model benchmark results or absolute per-call prices, so customers will still need to test the options against their own workloads.
"The platform running the automation is what governs which tools an agent can touch and attributes what it consumes."
Manav Khurana, GitLab
The expanded GitLab MCP server tools let agents in third-party clients trigger and inspect pipelines, open and review merge requests, update work items, browse repositories, and manage vulnerabilities. Read-only tools default to "Always Allow", while write and delete operations default to "Always Ask". Administrators can change those rules at group or project level. Most of the MCP tools are available on the Free, Premium and Ultimate tiers, although the vulnerability management tools require Ultimate.
This is part of a wider move to let coding agents act through MCP without granting unrestricted access. InfoQ reported in 2025 that Google's Agent Mode for Android Studio could use MCP to reach external tools. GitHub Copilot also supports MCP across its main interfaces, with enterprise policies for controlling access to servers. GitLab's approach applies a decision to each tool and places a human checkpoint in front of changes by default.
Cost controls matter more when agents run automatically rather than in response to an individual prompt. DevOps consultancy and GitLab partner ReleaseTEAM cautions that "the practical risk is automation", because a flow attached to every pipeline failure or new merge request could run hundreds of times a day. It recommends setting usage caps before connecting a flow to a high-volume trigger, then measuring consumption in a limited pilot.
The fourth main change concerns cost attribution. Credit usage exports now include a row for each billable event, with the user, project, session, flow type, credits and token counts. A new settings page lets owners set a default per-user cap and add individual overrides without using the GraphQL API. Developers can see their own consumption, while billing managers receive warnings when on-demand use reaches 50% or 80% of a monthly cap.
The release follows a series of changes to GitLab Duo during 2026. GitLab 19.2 put agents to work on dependency remediation and security reviews, with a person still responsible for approving changes. Earlier, versions 18.10 and 18.11 introduced flat-rate automated code reviews, free-tier access to the Duo Agent Platform, and monthly credit limits. Version 19.4 extends that approach to longer-running development tasks and gives administrators a closer view of the resulting costs.
GitLab 19.4 was released on 17 September 2026. The /goal command is available to Premium and Ultimate customers on GitLab.com, GitLab Self-Managed and GitLab Dedicated, and requires GitLab 19.3 or later with Duo CLI 9.17.0 or later. The command and expanded MCP tools remain in public beta, while the new credit usage visibility is generally available.

articles.title: Nie wieder Batteriewechsel: Wie Herzzellen künftig Implantate mit Strom versorgen
articles.text:
Herzzellen als Stromquelle: Neues Bio-Netz könnte Batterien in Implantaten ersetzen
Bislang sind medizinische Geräte wie Herzschrittmacher, Defibrillatoren oder Hirnschrittmacher auf fest verbaute Batterien angewiesen. Wenn deren Kapazität erschöpft ist, müssen Patient:innen für einen Austausch erneut operiert werden. Ein Team der US-amerikanischen University of Massachusetts Amherst stellt nun eine Methode vor, die dieses Problem physisch umgehen soll. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science Advances veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, haben die Forscher:innen ein Gitter entwickelt, das mit dem menschlichen Gewebe verwächst und die physische Zellbewegung in elektrischen Strom umwandelt.
Damit vollziehen die Wissenschaftler:innen konzeptionell eine Abkehr von der zentralisierten Energieversorgung hin zu einem dezentralen Modell. „Unser Körper ist ein Kraftwerk, das rund um die Uhr in Betrieb ist“, erklärt Hauptautorin Siqi Wang in einer Mitteilung der Universität. Jede einzelne Zelle erzeuge ihre eigene Energie in Form von mechanischen oder elektrischen Impulsen. Um diese mikroskopische Energieabgabe nutzbar zu machen, setzt das Team auf den sogenannten piezoelektrischen Effekt.
Ein Gitter aus Polymeren und Piezokeramik
Als wandlungsfähiges Kernmaterial kommt Blei-Zirkonat-Titanat zum Einsatz. Diese spezielle Keramik baut eine elektrische Spannung auf, sobald sie mechanisch verformt wird. Die Forscher:innen brachten Streifen davon auf eine Trägerschicht aus Polyimid auf. Dabei handelt es sich um einen extrem widerstandsfähigen und biegsamen Kunststoff, der unter anderem für flexible Bauteile in Smartphones verwendet wird.
Die Abmessungen des Gerüsts sind extrem klein: Die Keramikstreifen sind nur wenige hundert Nanometer dick, und damit fast hundertmal dünner als ein menschliches Haar. Das fertige Gitter besteht aus Bändern, die mit einer Breite von 20 Mikrometern feiner als ein Spinnenfaden sind. Durch diese offene Struktur bleibt den Zellen viel Freiraum, um in das Netz einzuwachsen.
Dieses Gerüst wurde sodann im Labor mit menschlichen Herzzellen besiedelt. Im Laufe der Kultivierung wuchsen die Zellen in die Hohlräume des Gitters ein und formten ein zusammenhängendes Mikrogewebe. Wenn sich die Herzzellen in ihrem natürlichen Rhythmus zusammenziehen, verbiegen sie das integrierte Netz. Diese mechanische Kontraktion erzeugt den Strom.
Messungen zeigten, dass das System in der optimierten Variante eine Spannung von bis zu 750 Millivolt aufbaut. Das entspricht exakt der halben Spannung einer handelsüblichen 1,5-Volt-AA-Batterie. Die absolute Energiemenge pro einzelnem Kontraktionszyklus und Bauteil ist mit etwa sieben Pikojoule (einem Billionstel Joule) zwar verschwindend gering. Rechnet man diesen Wert jedoch auf das gesamte dreidimensionale Netz hoch, erreicht das System eine Energiedichte von über zehn Mikrowatt pro Kubikzentimeter.
Zur Einordnung: Ein moderner Herzschrittmacher benötigt für den Dauerbetrieb eine Leistung von etwa ein bis zehn Mikrowatt. Rein rechnerisch würde also bereits ein Kubikzentimeter dieses biohybriden Gewebes ausreichen, um ein solches Implantat dauerhaft zu versorgen.
Bessere Biokompatibilität durch räumliches Einwachsen
Das biohybride Gewebe weist laut der Studie eine effektive Energiedichte auf, die bisherige Systeme um mehr als das Zehnfache übersteigt. Herkömmliche Ansätze zur Energiegewinnung im Körper basieren meist auf Modulen, die lediglich auf der Oberfläche von Organen fixiert werden. Das neue Netz wächst hingegen dreidimensional in das Zellgewebe ein. Dieser Vorgang erhöht die Biokompatibilität und soll verhindern, dass der Organismus das System als Fremdkörper erkennt und abstößt.
Professor Jun Yao, der als Senior-Autor an der Studie beteiligt ist, verweist auf bekannte Szenarien der Science-Fiction, in denen biologische Organismen und Maschinen zusammenarbeiten. Er betont jedoch, dass das System bislang ausschließlich in In-vitro-Versuchen getestet wurde. Bis ein solches Kraftwerk in der medizinischen Praxis eingesetzt wird, sind weitere Entwicklungsstufen notwendig.
Ein kritischer Aspekt für den klinischen Alltag ist die Materialwahl. Die verwendete Keramik Blei-Zirkonat-Titanat enthält das Schwermetall Blei. Aus gutem Grund ist Blei in Alltagsprodukten wie Trinkwasserrohren oder Unterhaltungselektronik längst streng reguliert oder verboten, da es den menschlichen Organismus schädigt. Für ein Implantat, das dauerhaft im Körper verbleiben soll, ist ein solches Material ein immenses Risiko.
Zwar haben die Forscher:innen die Bauteile in ihren Versuchen mit einem speziellen Kunstharz hermetisch versiegelt, und zwar in etwa vergleichbar mit der schützenden Isolierung eines Stromkabels unter Wasser. Dennoch belegt die vorliegende Arbeit zunächst lediglich die grundsätzliche physikalische Machbarkeit dieser Art der Energiegewinnung. Kommende Studien müssen nun klären, ob solche Beschichtungen auch über Jahre im ständigen Bewegungszyklus von Muskelgewebe mechanisch stabil bleiben und einen Kontakt des Bleis mit den Körperzellen dauerhaft verhindern.

articles.title: Vibe coder brings PS2 game disc support to jailbroken PS5 consoles
articles.text:
Vibe Has No Limits: Sony has decided to pursue a decidedly anti-consumer strategy by scaling back physical game releases. Needless to say, gamers are reacting in ways that could hurt the company's business prospects. Every script kiddie now seems eager to experiment with the PlayStation 5, including finding ways to run older PlayStation games on the latest console generation.
PlayStation 2 emulation is alive and well, even on the latest PlayStation 5 models. A vibe-coding enthusiast recently demonstrated the trend by sharing a new PS2-based "experience" that can allegedly run original PlayStation 2 games directly from the PS5's Blu-ray drive. Needless to say, the recently released PS5SX2 emulator largely repurposes existing open-source code for a different purpose.
Sword, the vibe coder in question, demonstrated how PS5SX2 can run PS2 games on the PS5 in a brief clip posted on X. A few days later, he released a new version of the emulator that can actually do so. PS5SX2 2.01 can automatically launch DVD-based PS2 games on a PS5 equipped with a Blu-ray drive. However, the tool must first dump the disc's contents to the console's internal storage before launching the game.
Sword acknowledged that the autoplay feature has only been tested on a single PS5 model and that the console cannot read CD-based PS2 games in any case. However, someone has contributed an experimental solution for loading PS2 game dumps from a USB Blu-ray drive. This could eventually allow digital-only PS5 models to support PS2 discs as well.
 – Sword (@sword_pdf) October 9, 2026
PS5SX2's ability to run PS2 games is impressive, but it is not exactly a plug-and-play solution. The emulator runs only on jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles with compatible hacked firmware. Game performance may vary, although fan favorites such as God of War and Gran Turismo 4 should run without issues at 60 frames per second.
Like many vibe-coded "projects" these days, PS5SX2 essentially repurposes existing code for a somewhat different purpose. The tool relies on the enormous human effort that went into PCSX2, the legendary project that effectively "solved" PS2 emulation on modern computers after countless developers spent more than two decades improving its code.
In any case, PS5SX2 and the prospect of PS2 disc support on the PS5 highlight the PlayStation 2's enduring influence on video game history. Hardware hackers are still uncovering new secrets in the console's original hardware components, while the PCSX2 team continues to improve the emulator, adding features, expanding compatibility, and introducing modern enhancements.

articles.title: SA accommodation booking app LekkeSlaap acquired by investor consortium - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
South Africa’s largest accommodation bookings app LekkeSlaap has been acquired by a consortium of investors.
Founded by university dropouts Jonathan Womersley and Marcel van de Ghinste in 2009, LekkeSlaap began life in a garage as TravelGround with 300 establishments listed. LekkeSlaap itself was launched in 2013, as South Africa’s first Afrikaans leisure accommodation booking platform, quickly usurping TravelGround, and growing to the point it now lists over 40,000 properties across Southern Africa and has managed bookings for over nine million guests since inception.
It has now been acquired for an undisclosed amount by a consortium of investors co-led by investment firms Bellair Road Investment Partners and Janic Capital, alongside the Ferreira Family Office, the Moolman Family Office, and Investec. The platform’s current executive management team has also invested and will continue to lead LekkeSlaap, but Womersley and van de Ghinste have exited.
“LekkeSlaap remains proudly local and independent in spirit, but with the right partners behind us, we can now dream even bigger,” said CEO Frans Joubert.
Former RMB CEO and Outsurance Group chairman Herman Bosman will now chair the board of LekkeSlaap, and GetSmarter co-founder Robert Paddock has also joined the board. Both have invested in the acquisition.
Bosman called LekkeSlaap a great example of what South African entrepreneurs could build with persistence and ambition.
“I am excited to join LekkeSlaap as chairman and to guide and support Frans, the management team, and fellow shareholders as LekkeSlaap enters its next phase of growth,” he said.

articles.title: Profitable French scale-up Wiremind raises €35 million after 12 years of bootstrapping | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Wiremind, a Paris-based AI software company serving the transport, air cargo, and events industries, has closed a €35 million funding round, its first since being founded over a decade ago.
The round brings three new investors: IronWave (formerly Wendel Growth), Bpifrance Investissement through its Large Venture fund, and Seaya Andromeda. The company said Wiremind’s co-founders, CEO Colin Girault-Matz and CTO Charles Pierre, will remain majority shareholders and retain control of the business.
“In twelve years, and without a single euro of outside capital, Colin, Charles and their teams have built systems that today drive the revenue of the largest rail and air operators,” said Victoire Laurenty, founder and General Partner of IronWave (formerly Wendel Growth).
Founded in October 2014, Wiremind is a bootstrapped company driven by its founders’ passion for data visualisation, tech and optimisation. They first crossed paths at SNCF, where they identified a gap in the market for machine learning-powered tools to help transport operators manage revenue and capacity more effectively.
Its flagship product is called CAYZN, an AI-first revenue management system for passenger transport operators. After being adopted by leading transportation companies, the system has reportedly delivered revenue gains between 5 and 15% on average. In 2025, CAYZN’s annual recurring revenue grew 81% year over year. The company has expanded its portfolio to include PAXONE, a next-generation inventory and distribution platform, CARGOSTACK for air cargo management, and EVENTORI, an AI-driven ticketing and revenue management platform for sports clubs and event organisers.
The fundraiser marks a significant milestone for a company that has operated entirely without outside capital while remaining profitable. In 2025, the company said its revenue grew 67% across the board, and it now works with more than 80 clients, 23 of which joined over the year.
“Charles and I began our careers more than fifteen years ago in the rail and aviation industries, so we have a unique understanding of the challenges our clients face. It is this first-hand knowledge that we leveraged to grow Wiremind over the years, while staying completely self-financed and investing in our own R&D,” said Girault-Matz, co-founder and CEO, Wiremind.
He added, “Today, we’re accelerating our efforts given the speed at which the market is adopting artificial intelligence tools. This financing round will allow us to reach rapidly growing geographic markets where decisions on technology investments are being made right now.”
The funding will be used to support two strategic priorities: expanding into new international markets and deepening investment in AI research and development. The company will continue its growth in South America and extend its reach into the Middle East and APAC regions, building upon its success in Europe and North America.

articles.title: Après l'OTAN et la Finlande, les drones français Parrot vont peut-être équiper la prestigieuse armée américaine
articles.text:
Parrot annonce ce lundi près de 2 millions de dollars de commandes de son micro-drone ANAFI UKR sur la plateforme d’achat de l’US Army. Le Français est aussi retenu pour la suite d’un programme de reconnaissance de l’armée américaine.
Après la Finlande, l'OTAN et un programme européen de blindés, Parrot enchaîne les bonnes nouvelles et s'ouvre les portes de l'armée américaine, avec son micro-drone très sollicité ANAFI UKR. Le fabricant parisien a annoncé, ce lundi 12 octobre 2026, avoir enregistré ses premières commandes sur l'UAS Marketplace, la plateforme d'achat lancée en mars par l'US Army. Il fait aussi partie des cinq industriels retenus pour la suite du très importantprogramme Short Range Reconnaissance, et c'est d'ailleurs le seul européen du lot.
Le micro-drone français de Parrot s’invite dans les achats de l’armée américaine
Lancée en mars 2026, l’UAS Marketplace (pour Unmanned Aircraft Systems, autrement dit les systèmes de drones) fonctionne comme une centrale d’achat en accès restreint. Des unités de l’armée, agences gouvernementales et pays alliés y comparent des drones déjà testés et validés par l’US Army, puis commandent directement celui qui convient à leur mission. C’est un vrai changement de méthode, puisqu'au lieu de passer par un programme d’acquisition centralisé, ce sont désormais les besoins du terrain et les retours de ceux qui pilotent ces drones qui orientent les achats.
On n'entre pas non plus dans cette plateforme d'achat comme dans un moulin. Car avant d'apparaître dans ce catalogue, chaque drone doit passer les procédures de qualification et de conformité de l'US Army. Dans le détail, ce sont des évaluations techniques pour vérifier qu'il tient ses promesses en vol, et un examen de cybersécurité qui juge sa résistance au piratage. Le Français Parrot a obtenu son ticket d'entrée au troisième trimestre et revendique déjà près de 2 millions de dollars de commandes d'ANAFI UKR, sans dire qui précisément a acheté. Alors c'est peut-être encore modeste pour un groupe qui a réalisé 80 millions d'euros de chiffre d'affaires en 2025, mais ce nouveau canal de vente démarre sur de bonnes bases.
Pour se démarquer, Parrot mise aussi sur la vitesse, avec des délais de livraison visés d’environ deux semaines. L'entreprise hexagonale peut compter sur une production assurée aux États-Unis et en Corée du Sud, un sérieux atout au moment où Washington durcit le ton face aux drones étrangers. Depuis le 3 septembre, de nombreux drones importés sur le sol américain subissent en effet une surtaxe douanière de 25 % ou de 100 %. Les fabricants chinois comme DJI sont parmi les plus exposés, tandis que les appareils sud-coréens peuvent, sous conditions, profiter d’un taux plafonné à 15 %.
Parrot revient dans la course à la reconnaissance de l’US Army
Vendre sur la marketplace, c’est une très bonne nouvelle pour Parrot, mais c'est le court terme. Avec le programme Short Range Reconnaissance (SRR), l'entreprise joue une partie plus longue, puisqu'ici, l’US Army y sélectionne, au fil d’une compétition en plusieurs étapes, les drones légers qui équiperont ses unités de niveau section, soit quelques dizaines de soldats engagés en première ligne. L’idée est de leur offrir une paire de jumelles volante, capable de recueillir du renseignement, de surveiller une zone et de reconnaître le terrain en temps réel, y compris dans des conditions plus difficiles.
Parrot a réussi la première épreuve, puisqu'à l’issue d’essais en vol menés en juin, le fabricant figure parmi les cinq retenus, aux côtés de quatre entreprises américaines. Place maintenant à l’évaluation de la maturité industrielle (Manufacturing Readiness Assessment). Après avoir vérifié que le drone remplit sa mission, l’US Army s’assure que son fabricant saura le produire en série et le déployer à grande échelle. Parrot connaît la maison. Il faisait déjà partie des industriels retenus pour le SRR en 2019, et ses ANAFI USA équipent depuis plusieurs agences fédérales et forces de l’ordre américaines.
Pour convaincre son monde, le drone ANAFI UKR peut compter sur une autonomie parmi les meilleures de sa catégorie, jusqu’à 50 minutes de vol avec sa batterie XLR, selon Parrot. Il sait suivre seul un plan de vol, et ses communications sécurisées compliquent la tâche des oreilles indiscrètes. Surtout, il peut se passer du GNSS, ces systèmes de positionnement par satellite comme le GPS, et continuer à voler quand l’ennemi brouille les ondes. Le drone, qui pèse moins d'un kilo et fut à l'origine présenté au salon du Bourget en juin 2025, a été pensé à partir des contraintes du front ukrainien, d’où son nom. « Nous sommes encouragés par la forte demande initiale », assure levice-président et directeur commercial de Parrot, Chris Roberts. Le fabricant n'a pas fini de montrer tout son potentiel.

articles.title: Ledger confirms spy chip implant behind wallet crypto thefts
articles.text:
Ledger has confirmed that some of its devices distributed through Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis were compromised with a hardware implant that drained users' cryptocurrency wallets.
The company has been investigating reports of users losing funds from wallets purchased through CryptoBilis, a major Malaysia-based hardware wallet retailer operating across Southeast Asia.
Some researchers have shown the implant in Ledger X since September 16, saying tampered devices were available for nearly half the price of the original hardware.
Ledger wallets are physical devices designed to securely store the private keys that control cryptocurrency assets and authorize transactions.
On October 9, Ledger said it had launched an investigation into user reports of cryptocurrency losses and asked CryptoBilis to stop selling and shipping Ledger devices.
The next day, the company confirmed hardware tampering on at least one device, though it’s still unclear exactly how or when the devices were tampered with.
"Ledger can confirm that one of the impacted users’ devices contained an unauthorized hardware implant. Ledger is reaching out to impacted users as part of the ongoing investigation," Ledger said.
The crypto wallet maker also noted that it was working with authorities to identify the perpetrator and bring them to justice.
“[...]Ledger recommends users who purchased a Ledger device from this reseller to not initiate set up if they have not yet done so. If you have set up your Ledger device, consider moving assets to a new Ledger signer (with a new seed),” warned Ledger.
Yesterday, Ledger provided another update, confirming that all user reports of unexpected fund drains were linked to devices sold through CryptoBilis and describing the affected volume as “limited.”
While the company did not disclose the type of devices compromised in this supply-chain attack, reports online talk about a spy implant in Ledger X devices that blends with the legitimate hardware.
Mark Karpelès, currently leading Karpeles Lab Inc. and CTO at Shells.com, showed a picture of the new implant in Ledger X, saying that it was "quite an evolution" from previous versions featuring manually soldered wires.
The former CEO of Mt. Gox said the implant was concealed behind the screen, but its antenna cable would have indicated that something was wrong.
According to Karpelès, the malicious hardware captured the device's display output and button presses to identify the seed phrase, then transmitted it to the attacker over an LTE connection using an eSIM.
"Ledger Nano X are used to store crypto. The spy implants are used to steal whatever crypto you store in those Ledger Nano X," Karpelès explained.
Although the CEO did not name CryptoBilis as the vendor of the compromised LedgerX, he said the device was not purchased via Ledger's recommended channels but from "a well known platform via a Chinese seller (product shipped from Malaysia)."
Tibane Labs, a cryptocurrency research and development studio, confirmed Karpelès' finding, adding that there were two implant versions for Ledger X.
The researchers obtained two variants, one in a Ledger device bought on Amazon Japan from " China-based seller · shipped from Malaysia," the other purchased on Yahoo! Auctions, Japan.
In a report over the weekend, Tibane Labs notes that the threat actor made room for the malicious circuitry by replacing the original battery with a smaller one, which powers both the implant and the Ledger X.
"Under the battery and antenna sits an ST STM32G431KBU6 (Arm Cortex‑M4, 128 KB flash, UFQFPN‑32)," the researchers found inside one of the devices.
For connectivity, the actor used "a tiny eSIM, an 8‑pad package just 2×2 mm, next to the MCU, and a shielded LTE module that sends the words out."
In the second hardware wallet analyzed, Tibane researchers found that markings on both the MCU (Microcontroller Unit) and the eSIM had been scraped off to hide the part numbers.
The second variant, which appears to be the same one that Karpelès described, is more advanced. It ran on the original battery and fit into the space normally occupied by the foam padding under the OLED display.
In both cases, the tell tale was the antenna wire, which ran along the top edge in the case of the second implant. In the first implant, the antenna is taped across the top of the battery and the shielded LTE module.
The researchers warned that the specimen above used "a designed, panelised flex PCB, the kind ordered from a board house, not a hand-built one-off."
Ledger is advising users to avoid purchasing from unauthorized resellers as they run an increased risk of getting counterfeit or modified devices.
The company is also reminding its authorized resellers and distributors to get the products only through authorized channels and to avoid restocking returned products.
Ledger provides a ‘Genuine Check’ mechanism to determine the authenticity of the device; however, it explicitly warns that it cannot detect added implants when the device’s original Secure Element remains intact.
At this time, there’s no indication that any other Ledger resellers are shipping compromised wallets; however, the community’s trust in the resellers’ network has been compromised, with many now calling for its dismantling.

articles.title: SpaceX s'apprête à tenter une récupération complète du Starship, une première dans l'histoire des fusées orbitales
articles.text:
Le planning approximatif est désormais fixé : il faudra attendre le mois de novembre pour revoir le Starship dans les airs. Elon Musk, le patron de SpaceX, a avancé que le quinzième vol de la fusée géante aurait lieu « avec un peu de chance dans quatre à six semaines », selon une estimation qu’il a partagée le 10 octobre dernier.
Mais la date ici est presque secondaire : ce qui importe le plus, c’est que SpaceX souhaite profiter du vol pour tenter – enfin – une manœuvre que personne n’a encore réussie. L’entreprise veut rattraper les deux étages de la fusée avec les bras de sa tour de lancement.
La « première récupération complète d’une fusée de classe orbitale »
D’après Elon Musk, ce serait « la première récupération complète d’une fusée de classe orbitale », c’est-à-dire capable de mettre une charge en orbite. Elon Musk a déjà avancé plusieurs dates, sans qu’aucune ne soit tenue. En novembre 2024, après le sixième vol, il envisageait de rattraper le vaisseau dès le vol 8. Le 25 juillet 2026, il évoquait encore une tentative au vol suivant, avant de la repousser « dans quelques mois » le 20 août. Seul le premier étage a été rattrapé à quelques reprises.
SpaceX sort d’un tir relativement récent, puisque le vol précédent date du 28 septembre. Après treize vols d’essai depuis avril 2023, le Starship a atteint l’orbite pour la première fois et a déployé 26 satellites Starlink V3. En revanche, l’un des six moteurs Raptor du vaisseau s’est coupé trop tôt pendant la montée, et SpaceX a préféré écourter la mission.
Pour Elon Musk, cette panne ne pose pas de gros problème et serait « assez facile à corriger ». Elle venait, selon les évaluations actuelles, du logiciel de l’ordinateur qui pilote un seul moteur, a-t-il expliqué lors du même entretien. Il a aussi jugé robuste le bouclier thermique, ces tuiles qui protègent le vaisseau de la chaleur quand il rentre dans l’atmosphère.
Précédemment, SpaceX semblait pouvoir enchaîner plus vite. Des documents de coordination de l’espace aérien plaçaient le vol 15 au plus tôt le 19 octobre, et on envisageait même deux vols du Starship en octobre. Le 8 octobre, une nouvelle version de ces documents a repoussé la date provisoire au 8 novembre.
La fourchette donnée par Elon Musk, comptée à partir du 10 octobre, va donc du 7 au 21 novembre environ. Il a lui-même évoqué un lancement avant Thanksgiving, qui tombe le 26 novembre. Ses calendriers pour le Starship ont toutefois rarement tenu depuis le premier vol, en avril 2023.
Rattraper le vaisseau, l’étape qui manque à SpaceX
Le Falcon 9, la fusée qui assure l’essentiel des lancements de SpaceX, récupère son premier étage depuis 2015. Son second étage, en revanche, est perdu à chaque mission. Le Starship doit régler ce problème en récupérant aussi la partie haute, ce qui devrait faire baisser fortement le coût d’un lancement.
SpaceX sait déjà attraper le Super Heavy, le premier étage d’environ 72 mètres équipé de 33 moteurs, avec les bras de sa tour. Elle l’a fait pour la première fois en octobre 2024. Le vaisseau, lui, n’a jamais été rattrapé et termine ses vols dans l’océan. Lors du vol 14, aucun des deux étages n’a d’ailleurs été récupéré : le Super Heavy a amerri dans le golfe du Mexique, le vaisseau dans le Pacifique. Musk espère même que le vol 16 réutilisera le premier étage et le vaisseau du vol 15, à condition qu’ils soient rattrapés puis remis en état.

articles.title: KB-RPCS3 : la PS5 fait enfin tourner des jeux PS3 grâce au jailbreak, mais l'installation s'annonce complexe — Frandroid
articles.text:
Les PS5 déverrouillées savent maintenant lancer des jeux PS3. Le 9 octobre, un développeur connu sous le pseudo kamb205 a mis en ligne sur GitHub la première version alpha de KB-RPCS3, une adaptation de RPCS3 pour la console de Sony. RPCS3 est l’émulateur PS3 open source de référence sur PC, c’est-à-dire un logiciel qui imite le fonctionnement de la console pour faire tourner ses jeux. Sony, lui, s’est arrêté à la PS4 : la PS5 lit les jeux de sa devancière, mais le catalogue PS3 n’y est disponible qu’en streaming, pour les abonnés PlayStation Plus Premium.
Pour nos confrères de Numerama, cette étape rapproche la PS5 d’une machine capable de lancer presque tous les jeux PlayStation. Le jailbreak consiste à contourner les protections de Sony pour installer des logiciels que la marque n’autorise pas. Il a pris de l’ampleur fin septembre avec Relapse, une chaîne de failles publiée sur GitHub qui se lance depuis le navigateur de la console.
Relapse fonctionne sur les PS5 qui tournent sous les versions 7.00 à 13.60 du logiciel système, PS5 Pro comprise. Depuis, les émulateurs s’enchaînent. Le 10 octobre, le développeur Sword a ajouté à PS5SX2, son adaptation de l’émulateur PS2 PCSX2, la lecture des disques PS2 originaux dans le lecteur de la PS5.
Jusqu’à 330€ d’avantages avec nos offres Hello Prime ou Hello Prime Duo, dont 80€ cash à l’ouverture de compte !
Une version alpha à compiler soi-même
Par contre, KB-RPCS3 n’a rien d’un logiciel prêt à l’emploi. Son auteur ne publie que le code source, sans fichier à installer sur la console. Il explique qu’un programme qui combine le cœur de RPCS3, sous licence libre GPL-2.0, et des composants PS5 sous GPL-3.0 ne peut pas être distribué, car ces deux licences imposent des conditions incompatibles.
Il faut donc compiler l’émulateur soi-même, autrement dit transformer le code en programme, sur un ordinateur Linux équipé des outils de développement PS5. Le joueur doit aussi fournir le logiciel système de la PS3 et ses propres jeux, que KB-RPCS3 n’inclut pas. Une fois installés, ces jeux apparaissent en tuiles sur l’écran d’accueil de la PS5, avec les vibrations de la DualSense, les sauvegardes et les notifications de trophées.
Côté performances, on manque encore de recul. Un autre projet, RPCS3-PS5, a été essayé sur une seule PS5 Pro avec une poignée de jeux. Selon Wccftech, Need for Speed Carbon y est entièrement jouable, alors que le premier inFAMOUS a des problèmes de performances.
La PS3 reposait sur le processeur Cell, une puce à l’architecture très particulière, réputée difficile à émuler. L’équipe officielle de RPCS3 a d’ailleurs dit qu’elle ne comptait pas développer de version PS5, à cause des limites du processeur Zen 2 de la console.
La mise à jour 14.00 ferme la porte
Relapse ne fonctionne pas avec la version 14.00 du logiciel système, et certains jeux l’exigent déjà. Tom’s Hardware cite le cas de Marvel’s Wolverine : d’après des témoignages de joueurs, la mise à jour de la version numérique du jeu demande la version 14.00. Ce qui signifie qu’installer cette mise à jour fait perdre le jailbreak.
Sur une PS5 déjà passée en 14.00, aucun de ces émulateurs ne fonctionne aujourd’hui. Et même sur une console compatible, KB-RPCS3 reste expérimental : kamb205 ne publie, ne teste et ne promet pour l’instant aucune version installable.

articles.title: Kenya’s CBK seeks powers to take over struggling fintechs
articles.text:
Kenya’s central bank is seeking powers to take over struggling payment companies and sell their businesses, expanding the regulator’s role in protecting customer money when providers run into trouble.
The draft National Payment System Bill, 2026, would allow the Central Bank of Kenya (CBK) to intervene when a provider fails to meet its obligations to customers or other financial institutions, breaches regulatory requirements, or threatens financial stability.
The measures could put CBK at the centre of resolving failures in an industry where customers rely on private companies to hold and move their money. It could force service providers and their investors to surrender control of a troubled business before it reaches liquidation, with CBK deciding who runs it and appointing a statutory manager to sell it.
“The Central Bank may intervene in the management of a payment service provider or a payment system operator where … the payment service provider or payment system operator fails to meet its obligations to customers,” the draft bill states.
A company that fails to comply with a regulatory directive could also face action, while CBK could intervene during a crisis to protect financial stability and public confidence.
That would give the regulator room to act while a business still has assets and operations worth preserving. In payments, a provider’s inability to settle its obligations can affect merchants awaiting sales proceeds, customers making transfers, and other institutions expecting payment.
CBK appointing officials
The proposal also allows CBK to remove company officials it deems responsible for a company’s deterioration, appoint a director who cannot be dismissed without its approval, and stop the firm from taking on new payment business or agents.
“All the powers of the directors, significant shareholders, senior officers or trustees” would cease on the manager’s appointment, except where the manager permitted them to continue, the draft says.
Such restrictions could limit the amount of additional customer money exposed to a troubled provider. They could also leave its owners with little influence over how the company responds to its troubles.
While the proposal places the protection of customer money at the centre of any intervention, it does not guarantee uninterrupted access to funds. A statutory manager could suspend payments to customers and other creditors while managing the company’s affairs.
CBK has intervened in a payment company before. In October 2021, it revoked the authorisation of Mobile Pay, which operated under the Tangaza brand, citing regulatory breaches that put customer funds at risk. According to the regulator, the company failed to submit audited accounts for its business and trust fund, as well as security audits and other reports.
The proposed law would build on those powers with a detailed statutory management regime, including provisions for replacing management and selling a provider’s business.
CBK has exercised similar powers in the banking industry over the past decade. It placed Imperial Bank into receivership in October 2015 and announced its liquidation in December 2021.
Chase Bank, which entered receivership in April 2016, reopened that month under KCB’s management. In 2018, a deal transferred 75% of the value of its deposits to SBM Bank, before the remaining business went into liquidation in 2021. The interventions show the options available to the regulator.
The proposal, which will repeal and replace the National Payment System Act of 2011, will now allow the registration and licensing of fintech startups to resolve a legal grey area that has slowed the expansion of fintechs in the country, allowing commercial banks and telcos to dominate.

Monday, October 12th 2026
Montech Announces CyberFlow AIO Liquid CPU Coolers
MONTECH, a global leader in PC cases, power supplies, and cooling solutions, proudly announces the global launch of CyberFlow Series, the company's most advanced all in one liquid cooling family to date. Created for builders who expect thermal strength, precision engineering, and a fully resolved design, CyberFlow brings one common performance architecture to two distinct visual identities.
CyberFlow ARGB translates the cooling platform into a bold, cyberpunk inspired centerpiece with immersive ARGB lighting. CyberFlow CORE takes a more restrained direction, pairing the same performance foundation with classic styling for clean, timeless systems. Together, the series gives enthusiasts a meaningful choice in expression without asking them to compromise on the cooling platform beneath it.Ultimate Thermal Performance
At the center of CyberFlow is a pump designed to operate at up to 3500 RPM, paired with a 32 mm aluminium radiator that expands the available cooling surface. The system is designed as a complete thermal path, from optimized thermal paste at the processor to high pressure airflow through the radiator.
Cooling Where It Matters
A magnetic VRM fan adds targeted airflow around the CPU power delivery area. Operating at up to 3500 RPM, it extends the cooling strategy beyond the processor and supports demanding systems where surrounding component airflow matters.
Designed to Make Advanced Cooling Effortless
Preinstalled radiator fans reduce preparation time and simplify installation. A 400 mm tube length supports flexible placement, while compatibility with Intel LGA1700 and 1851, plus AMD AM4 and AM5, covers current mainstream desktop platforms.
E25 Performance Fans
Every CyberFlow arrives with preinstalled E25 120 mm performance fans. CyberFlow ARGB features E25 ARGB fans, while CyberFlow CORE uses E25 PWM fans. Each fan reaches up to 2700 RPM, delivering 93.12 CFM of airflow and 7.43 mmH2O of static pressure through a durable fluid dynamic bearing.
Designed for Broad Case Compatibility
The 32 mm aluminium radiator increases the available cooling surface while maintaining broad case compatibility. Available in 240 mm and 360 mm formats, CyberFlow also features 400 mm tubing and preinstalled fans to support flexible placement and a more straightforward installation process.
Confidence Beyond Performance
Every CyberFlow cooler is backed by a six-year warranty. Coverage for component damage caused by leakage resulting from a product defect is provided according to the applicable warranty terms.
As part of MONTECH's tenth anniversary, CyberFlow also delivers a commemorative unboxing experience with a dedicated tube clip, thank you card, and anniversary sticker. The details reflect the same intent as the product itself: performance made complete through thoughtful execution.
Ready for Modern Intel and AMD Platforms
CyberFlow supports Intel LGA 1700 and LGA 1851, along with AMD AM4 and AM5 platforms. This broad socket compatibility makes it ready for both current systems and new performance focused builds across the latest mainstream Intel and AMD platforms.
Availability and Pricing
MONTECH CyberFlow ARGB and CyberFlow CORE are scheduled to launch on October 12, 2026. Both series will be available in 240 mm and 360 mm sizes, with black and white color options.

articles.title: Hackers hit European supermarket refrigeration systems, spoiling food and forcing stores to dump stock
articles.text:
In a nutshell: Cyber attackers are causing major headaches for grocery shoppers across Europe. On Sunday night, hackers targeted refrigeration systems at around 150 Intermarché stores, forcing employees to toss out food that is no longer safe to consume. And that's only the tip of the iceberg.
A spokesperson for the supermarket chain told Bloomberg that attackers infiltrated controls for the cooling systems and activated the defrost mode, which heated them to 50 degrees Celsius, or 122 degrees Fahrenheit. Roughly six hours passed before employees noticed. By that time, all of the food in the coolers had been ruined.
The attack wasn't limited to Intermarché stores. According to Agence France-Presse, fewer than 100 Cooperative U stores were also hit. BMF added that some Leclerc stores were also impacted. La Dépêche reports that electronic pricing label systems were also impacted.
Bloomberg said the systems targeted in the Intermarché attack were managed by Danfoss. Just a few months back, security researchers with Team 82 published a report highlighting multiple vulnerabilities in Danfoss refrigeration controllers that could lead to this exact sort of attack. It is no surprise, then, that an attack materialized in the real world.
The immediate fallout from the attack isn't fully clear, outside of the obvious inconvenience to shoppers, supermarket employees, and food suppliers. Early reports pin the financial loss at around 300,000 euros, but that figure could climb much higher as the full scope of the attack comes into focus.
Dominique Schelcher, CEO of Cooperative U, said teams have been dispatched to their stores to fix the issue, adding that they will conduct a full investigation into the matter. No suspects have been publicly identified as of this writing.
It is entirely possible that this was a test run used by the attackers to demonstrate its effectiveness. If deployed in conjunction with other destructive attacks on the power grid or utilities, the effects could be devastating. It is the sort of worst case hacking scenario we've been warned about for years – fortunately, it hasn't materialized... yet.

articles.title: Novo “rival” do Office foi criado com auxílio da IA • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Novo “rival” do Office foi criado com auxílio da IA
WordCraft, GridCraft e DeckCraft são projetos de código aberto criados com auxílio do Claude.
Há três novos aplicativos para quem procura alternativas à soluções do pacote Office. Chamados de WordCraft, GridCraft e DeckCraft, eles reproduzem funções do Word, Excel e PowerPoint, respectivamente, e foram criados por Brandon Thomas, desenvolvedor responsável pelo ArtCraft.
A iniciativa amplia o catálogo do projeto que reúne alternativas gratuitas a programas comerciais de criação e produtividade. Segundo o Tom’s Hardware, Thomas quer oferecer opções para quem prefere não depender de assinaturas para usar esse tipo de ferramenta. Os apps, porém, ainda não substituem integralmente as suítes consolidadas.
Os aplicativos para escritório, assim como o ArtCraft, são desenvolvidos com auxílio do Claude, modelo de inteligência artificial da Anthropic, e podem ser baixados gratuitamente pelo GitHub.
Os três aplicativos tentam reproduzir alguns fluxos de trabalho comuns dos programas de escritório da Microsoft. O WordCraft é voltado à edição e formatação de documentos; o GridCraft, às planilhas e cálculos; e o DeckCraft permite criar apresentações com textos, imagens, gráficos e outros elementos visuais.
Os projetos foram desenvolvidos em Rust e têm versões destinadas a Windows, macOS e Linux, além de opções para execução no navegador.
O estágio de desenvolvimento varia entre eles:
Assim como em outras suítes de código aberto conhecidas, como o LibreOffice — que Thomas critica abertamente —, as alternativas naturalmente não conseguem reproduzir todas as opções e formatos da Microsoft.
Antes dos programas de escritório, Thomas já trabalhava no ArtCraft, uma iniciativa de código aberto semelhante a pacotes como os oferecidos pela Adobe. O catálogo inclui programas de edição de imagem, ilustração, edição de vídeo, tratamento de fotografias e edição de PDFs.
A comunidade também discute a expansão do catálogo para outras categorias. Entre as ideias está o CADCraft, ferramenta voltada a desenho técnico e projetos assistidos por computador, em uma proposta semelhante à do AutoCAD, da Autodesk.
Em todo caso, Thomas tem sofrido críticas na comunidade de programação que consideram os projetos como “vibecodados” — termo usado para descrever programas produzidos por ferramentas de IA. Thomas rebateu os comentários no X, destacando que possui 15 anos de experiência e defendeu o uso da IA como ferramenta de apoio. “Modelos de IA me permitem trabalhar como uma empresa inteira”, declarou.

articles.title: NASA vai investigar buraco na Lua que pode levar a uma caverna
articles.text:
A NASA selecionou uma missão para investigar uma abertura na superfície da Lua que pode dar acesso a uma estrutura subterrânea maior. O projeto, chamado Geophysical Instruments for Marius Lunar pit Investigation (GIMLI), pretende estudar o poço Marius Hills Pit (MHP) diretamente no solo lunar, para determinar se ele se conecta a uma caverna formada por antigas atividades vulcânicas.
Localizado em uma região com histórico de atividade vulcânica, o buraco tem dimensões estimadas de até 150 pés (cerca de 46 metros) de profundidade e 300 pés (cerca de 91 metros) de largura. Cientistas acreditam que a formação pode ser uma abertura causada pelo desabamento do teto de um tubo de lava subterrâneo, estrutura que também pode ajudar a explicar a história geológica da Lua.
Como será a investigação da NASA
Até agora, o Marius Hills Pit foi estudado apenas por observações feitas a partir da órbita lunar. A missão GIMLI pretende avançar nessa investigação com o uso de um veículo robótico equipado com instrumentos especializados para analisar as características do terreno e identificar possíveis estruturas abaixo da superfície.
Entre os equipamentos previstos estão um radar de penetração no solo, sondas sísmicas e um gravímetro, sensor que mede a intensidade do campo gravitacional. O rover também contará com câmeras para registrar imagens das partes expostas do poço.
A iniciativa é conduzida por pesquisadores do Planetary Science Institute (PSI). A maior parte dos instrumentos será construída pela Honeybee Robotics. O financiamento vem do programa Payloads and Research Investigations on the Surface of the Moon, da NASA, enquanto a espaçonave será fornecida por uma empresa privada no âmbito da iniciativa Commercial Lunar Payload Services, também da agência espacial.
O que o poço pode revelar sobre a Lua
A confirmação de um tubo de lava de grandes dimensões ajudaria os cientistas a compreender melhor como o vulcanismo ocorreu na Lua. Gareth Morgan, cientista sênior do Planetary Science Institute e vice-investigador principal do programa GIMLI, afirmou que a descoberta de uma estrutura desse tipo permitiria obter informações sobre os processos vulcânicos que moldaram o satélite natural.
A região próxima ao Marius Hills Pit apresenta camadas expostas de regolito — material solto que cobre a superfície lunar — e antigos fluxos de lava. Segundo o PSI, o estudo dessas formações pode revelar como a lava se deslocou pelo terreno no passado.
Cavernas lunares também podem abrigar astronautas
Além do interesse geológico, as estruturas subterrâneas da Lua chamam a atenção por seu possível uso como abrigos para astronautas. Como o satélite natural praticamente não tem atmosfera, sua superfície fica exposta à radiação solar e cósmica.
Cavidades subterrâneas poderiam oferecer uma proteção natural contra essa radiação e proporcionar condições de temperatura mais controladas. Essas características são consideradas relevantes para a possibilidade de estabelecer uma presença humana de longo prazo na Lua.
A missão GIMLI buscará determinar se o poço Marius Hills Pit permite acessar uma estrutura subterrânea maior. A investigação poderá ajudar a avaliar tanto o potencial científico dessas formações quanto suas possíveis aplicações em futuras atividades humanas no satélite.
Ana Figueiredo é editora de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em Jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).

articles.title: Bricksforge WordPress Plugin Vulnerability Exploited in the Wild
articles.text:
A critical vulnerability in the Bricksforge WordPress plugin is being exploited in the wild, according to WordPress security company Patchstack.
The vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-85097 and it has a CVSS score of 9.8. Unauthenticated attackers can exploit it to upload arbitrary files and execute malicious code.
This can allow threat actors to take full control of the targeted WordPress websites.
The security hole was patched with the release of version 3.1.8.10. Versions 3.1.8.9 and earlier are affected.
Patchstack started seeing in-the-wild exploitation attempts on October 7.
Bricksforge is a commercial add-on for the Bricks visual site builder that layers extra tools onto WordPress sites, such as custom forms, animations, an email designer, and admin-area pages. Patchstack reported that it’s used by roughly 6,000 websites.
“Two clusters stand out in our telemetry,” Patchstack explained. “In the first, 44 IPs sent 56 requests with identical payloads within seconds of each other. In the second, three IPs tested 25 variations of PHP extensions and encodings against the same temporary file.”
The company added, “Both patterns point to automated exploitation over rotating proxies or distributed infrastructure. They do not, on their own, attribute the activity to a single threat actor.”
It’s not uncommon for threat actors to target WordPress vulnerabilities shortly after patches are released, including plugin flaws and weaknesses affecting WordPress itself.

articles.title: The Yandex outage probably didn’t blitz Russian bots
articles.text:
Multiple Ukrainian drone strikes over the last week have taken Russian data centers offline and reportedly caused online bot traffic to plummet — but in reality it’s probably not the kind of bot activity most people associate with Russia.
The Yandex outage probably didn’t blitz Russian bots
At least, not the troll traffic that blights social media.
A chart citing Cloudflare data has been circulating around social media platforms, showing a sharp decline in bot traffic following attacks on Yandex servers — a technology company often described as “Russia’s Google.” While many people are inferring that the chart refers to bot farms that push disinformation, conspiracy theories, and other harmful content across online platforms, reputed troll farm exposer antibot4navalny says the data “has nothing to do with social media.”
In a thread on X, antibot4navalny says the chart is actually measuring requests from automated Yandex web crawlers. These bots have broad uses, so while they can be used maliciously to hack user accounts and target people with spam, they’re also very commonly used to index websites for search engines and provide customer service support. The chart is also specific to Yandex-based traffic, and not bot activity from Russia at large — which remains largely unchanged around the data center attacks, according to Cloudflare.
Other charts have also been shared that show the same alleged decline in Russian disinformation bot activity. One such diagram was shared on X by European Parliament member Tomáš Zdechovský, who claimed that online activity around the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) political party plummeted following the Russian data center attacks.
Computer scientist Raphael Wimmer says he suspects the source diagram shared by Zdechovský is AI-generated, pointing out several inconsistencies with the activity timeline it’s supposedly tracking, including a data point logged for a future date: October 15th. The image appears to have first been posted by Threads user Robin Schlingheider. The data’s source isn’t established, and the original doesn’t include any reference to Germany’s AfD party. Wimmer says Schlingheider has evaded his questions about where the image originated.
“Could we (and especially politicians, journalists and scientists who should know better) please stop sharing unverified images?” Wimmer said.
Meanwhile, the vast majority of Yandex-operated systems still appear to be offline following the latest drone strike, including the Yandex Pay digital payment service, leaving users unable to transfer funds, check balances, or make purchases. Yandex Fintech head Dima Pirogov said in a statement (translated via Google) that “we can’t yet give you a precise restoration timeline, but we promise: we won’t stop until the service is restored.”

A very cheap 5060 laptop
If you're in the market for a budget gaming laptop, then $1,149 for a 15-inch RTX 5060 HyperX OMEN is about as good as it gets right now. Walmart has slashed $750 off the price of this Intel Core Ultra 7 machine with 16GB of RAM and 1TB SSD, now just $1,149.
● Check out this deal at Walmart
In a world where PC prices are skyrocketing, gaming laptops and desktops are getting more expensive on a near-weekly basis. This is a generous spec and price in the market given current conditions, and worth considering for anyone who wants to take their first step into mobile gaming or to upgrade from an older device.
This RTX 5060 gaming laptop features a 15-inch, 2K IPS display with a 165Hz refresh rate, Intel Core Ultra 7 225H, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB SSD.

articles.title: Kontrollverlust berechenbar: Wenn lokale Sprachmodelle plötzlich gefährlich werden
articles.text:
Physiker finden mathematische Formel: Wann lokale KI-Modelle plötzlich gefährlich werden
Die Nutzung von Sprachmodellen direkt auf Endgeräten wie Smartphones oder Tablets nimmt branchenübergreifend zu. Da diese sogenannten Edge-KI-Modelle lokal und ohne Cloud-Anbindung arbeiten, fehlen ihnen herkömmliche nachgeschaltete Sicherheitsfilter, sogenannte Guardrails.
Das birgt Risiken für Anwender:innen, die auf Offline-Modelle angewiesen sind, etwa im medizinischen, juristischen oder militärischen Sektor. Zwei Physiker der US-amerikanischen George Washington University wollen solche Risiken nun mit einer mathematischen Formel besser abschätzen.
In einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Patterns veröffentlichten Studie präsentieren Neil F. Johnson und Frank Yingjie Huo eine Gleichung, die berechnen soll, wann ein Sprachmodell von einer angemessenen Antwort zu einer potenziell schädlichen Ausgabe kippen kann.
Edge-KI und das Problem der fehlenden Cloud-Sicherheitsfilter
Ein Teil heutiger KI-Schutzmechanismen greift erst während der Nutzung: etwa durch cloudbasierte Filter, Monitoring oder nachträgliche Sicherheitsupdates. Bei reiner Offline-Nutzung stehen solche externen Guardrails nicht zur Verfügung, sodass eine fehlerhafte oder gefährliche Ausgabe ungefiltert auf dem Bildschirm der Nutzer:innen erscheinen kann.
Besonders problematisch ist dies bei Fachpersonal, das aus Datenschutzgründen etwa keine Patientendaten oder Mandanteninformationen in die Cloud senden darf. Ohne laufende externe Überwachung fehlt in solchen Anwendungsbereichen ein zusätzliches Sicherheitsnetz, das riskante Antwortverläufe erkennen oder nachträglich abfangen könnte.
Die beiden Wissenschaftler wählten für ihre Untersuchung einen Ansatz, der komplexe neuronale Netze rechnerisch auf einen sogenannten „effektiven Attention Head“ reduziert. Diese Komponente moderner Sprachmodelle berechnet, wie stark einzelne Textbausteine im Kontext zueinander in Beziehung stehen. Sie steuert, auf welche Informationen die KI bei der Verarbeitung ihre „Aufmerksamkeit“ richtet. Auf die Datenverarbeitung dieses Bausteins wandten die Forscher anschließend ihre Analysemethoden an.
Der Attention Head als physikalisches Modell
„Wir haben den Riss gefunden, der die Ausgabe einer KI von dem, was man will, zu dem, was man nicht will, umkippen lässt“, wird Autor Neil F. Johnson in einer begleitenden Pressemitteilung auf Eurekalert zitiert. Den Physikern zufolge verhält sich die Mechanik der KI-Modelle dabei ähnlich wie komplexe Festkörper, deren Verhalten sich oft durch die Beobachtung eines einzelnen Atoms erklären lässt.
Innerhalb des Modells fließen die verarbeiteten Informationen durch den sogenannten Residual Stream. Dieser zentrale Datenkanal reicht die Eingaben im neuronalen Netz von Schicht zu Schicht weiter.
Auf diesem Weg stehen bei jeder Abfrage verschiedene Antwortmöglichkeiten in ständiger Konkurrenz zueinander. Die Forscher betrachten die zugrundeliegenden mathematischen Werte (Vektoren) für wünschenswerte und unerwünschte Ausgaben als Täler in einer Topografie.
Ein KI-Modell kann zu einer schädlichen Antwort wechseln, wenn der jeweilige Gesprächskontext den unerwünschten Antwortbereich stärker begünstigt als den erwünschten. Die von Johnson und Huo entwickelte Formel beschreibt diese Konkurrenz und soll abschätzen, wann die Schwelle zur unerwünschten Ausgabe überschritten wird.
Die Gefahr des verzögerten Kipppunkts
Die Untersuchung zeigt, dass sich der problematische Umschlag bei der Textgenerierung nicht zwingend schon beim ersten Token ereignen muss. Ein Modell kann zunächst eine lange Reihe inhaltlich unproblematischer Antworten liefern, bevor es unbemerkt in den problematischen Bereich abrutscht.
Dieses Verhalten täuscht eine falsche Sicherheit vor. Dabei geht es den Forschern zufolge nicht um mangelnde Qualität oder einen schwindenden Wahrheitsgehalt der Aussagen. Eine schädliche Antwort kann faktisch völlig korrekt, aber hochgradig gefährlich sein – beispielsweise eine Anleitung für den Bau einer Waffe. Die Berechnungen der Physiker zeigen, dass erst die Reihenfolge der vorherigen Eingaben das Verhalten des Attention Heads maßgeblich in diese Richtung steuert.
Jede Information im vorherigen Gesprächsverlauf verschiebt die Vektorgewichtung und zieht die nächste Ausgabe näher an das unerwünschte Tal heran. Sobald das System einmal gekippt ist, kann jede nachfolgende schädliche Antwort die KI weiter in eine Abwärtsspirale ziehen.
Erfolgreiche Tests an Open-Weight-Modellen
Um die theoretische Formel in der Praxis zu validieren, testeten Johnson und Huo ihre Vorhersagen an sieben verschiedenen Open-Weight-Modellen. Diese Modelle aus drei unabhängigen Technologiegruppen wiesen Größenordnungen zwischen 124 Millionen und 12 Milliarden Parametern auf.
Die mathematische Vorhersage traf in den Tests der Forscher überraschend oft zu. In 18 von 19 untersuchten Fällen erkannte die Formel korrekt, ob ein Modell sofort oder erst verzögert oder – im Untersuchungszeitraum – gar nicht in einen problematischen Antwortverlauf kippt.
Der Ansatz lässt sich laut Studie auf verschiedene Risikobereiche übertragen, etwa medizinische Desinformation, Aufrufe zur Selbstverletzung oder problematische juristische Ratschläge. Ob die Formel in all diesen Feldern gleich zuverlässig funktioniert, müssen allerdings weitere Tests zeigen.
Schwächen bei der Semantik und Ausblick auf Warnsysteme
Eine technische Schwäche gibt es bei der Methode noch: verneinte Sätze. Hier stoßen die Berechnungen an ihre Grenzen. Das System bewertet dann einzelne Wörter zu stark und übersieht, dass ein simples „nicht“ oder „kein“ die Bedeutung des gesamten Satzes umkehrt.
Hinzu kommt eine praktische Hürde: Bevor die Methode im Alltag funktioniert, müssen Entwickler:innen für jeden Anwendungsfall erst einmal mathematisch definieren, was genau als gute und was als schlechte Antwort gilt. Nicht nur diese erforderliche Vorarbeit dürfte verhindern, dass die Technik schon morgen flächendeckend auf unseren Geräten landet. Die Autoren betonen ausdrücklich, dass eine größere Studie mit vorab festgelegten Kriterien, neuen Prompts und weiteren Modellen nötig sei, um die Formel als quantitative Risikoanzeige zu kalibrieren.
Trotzdem liefert die Formel perspektivisch einen wichtigen Baustein für die KI-Sicherheit. Sie könnte künftig als eine Art integrierte Warnleuchte für lokale Sprachmodelle etwa auf Smartphones dienen, die rechtzeitig vor Entgleisungen warnt. Und das ganz ohne aufwendige Datenabgleiche in der Cloud.
Ein Hinweis zum Schluss: Die anschaulichen Gesprächsbeispiele der Studie basieren auf GPT-2 Base mit 124 Millionen Parametern. Das Modell dient als Forschungsproxy für ressourcenbeschränkte Geräte, soll laut den Autoren aber nicht das Sicherheitsverhalten moderner, auf Anweisungen und Sicherheitsvorgaben nachtrainierter KI-Assistenten abbilden.

articles.title: One-Punch Man Tome 35 : où précommander l’édition collector ?
articles.text:
En plus de la version classique du tome 35 de One-Punch Man, vendue au prix de 7,30 € et prévue pour le 15 octobre 2026, Kurokawa propose une version collector au prix de 12,95 €, qui sortira le même jour. Le volume est déjà proposé en précommande chez plusieurs enseignes.
One-Punch Man tome 35
Auteur : ONE et Yusuke Murata
Éditeur : Kurokawa
Date de parution : 15/10/2026
Nombre de pages : 208 pages
Format : Manga broché
Prix : 12,95 € (édition normale : 7,30 €)
Cette édition spéciale du manga imaginé par ONE et dessiné par Yusuke Murata reprend le tome 35 de l’édition classique, avec plusieurs bonus. Elle comprend une jaquette alternative en plus de la couverture classique, cinq cartes holographiques et un recueil de 28 pages d’illustrations en couleurs. Le recueil met en avant le dessin de Yusuke Murata, l’un des points forts de la série.
Comme pour d’autres éditions collector de manga, mieux vaut surveiller les stocks si vous souhaitez l’ajouter à votre bibliothèque dès sa sortie.
On en est où, dans l’histoire de One-Punch Man ?
Attention, nous dévoilons quelques éléments sur l’intrigue des précédents tomes.
One-Punch Man suit les aventures de Saitama, un héros capable de terrasser presque n’importe quel adversaire d’un seul coup de poing. Après trois années d’entraînement intensif, il est devenu si puissant, et totalement chauve, que les combats ne lui procurent plus aucune excitation. En quête d’un adversaire à sa mesure, il rejoint l’Association des héros et croise la route de personnages hauts en couleur.
Dans le tome 35, Saitama a emménagé dans son nouveau logement. Accompagné de son camarade Genos, il retourne dans les décombres de son ancien appartement, au cœur de la ville Z ravagée, pour récupérer quelques affaires. Mais leur exploration prend une tournure inattendue lorsqu’ils rencontrent un étrange chien et un drôle de singe, qui ne tardent pas à les suivre jusqu’à leur nouvel appartement.
One-Punch Man garde son humour absurde et le dessin soigné de Yusuke Murata. La série enchaîne toujours les gags et les combats sans se prendre au sérieux, et ce tome 35 compte bien respecter les codes de la série.
